pages.d: A web UI for AI agents in Python. Streaming chat, an artifacts canvas, selectable layouts, a dashboard and docs sites, from one pip package.

s.x: Python 3.10 or higher. Scaffold a starter for any agent framework (agent, openai, anthropic, langgraph, crewai, pydantic-ai, praisonai, or dashboard), or write app.py directly: Open . aiui run app.py opens cleanly in focused mode (Chat + your own pages) in the React app shell. Pass --preset agent for Sessions, Approvals, Usage and Memory, --preset ops for the full control plane, or AIUI_LAYOUT=chat-canvas aiui run app.py to open the side canvas.

Build streaming AI agent interfaces with starters, profiles, reasoning steps, tool calls, HITL approvals and an artifacts canvas. Combine chat with 5 selectable layouts, Python or YAML data pages, notifications, themes and built-in ops views. Let agents push live interactive surfaces, forms and controls over JSONL and WebSocket into a split Chat + Canvas workspace. Explore all 81 Python and YAML UI builders — inline chat blocks, split-pane chat panels, file uploads, spreadsheets, whiteboards, DataFrames, Plotly charts and forms. Turn a folder of Markdown and one aiui.yaml into a fast, searchable documentation site with SEO, OpenAPI and llms.txt. Extend the app with pip-installable @aiui/sdk React pages and themes, behind deny-by-default auth and reverse proxies. Looking something up? The CLI, the Python API and the YAML configuration cover every command, function and key. PraisonAIUI is MIT licensed. Install it from PyPI as aiui; the import name is praisonaiui and the command is aiui.

s.x: PraisonAIUI is one Python package. The PyPI name is aiui, you import it as praisonaiui, and the command is aiui. The browser UI ships inside the wheel, so you do not need Node.js or npm to run an app or build a docs site.
Python 3.10 or higher. The browser UI ships inside the wheel. You need Node.js only to change the React frontend in a clone of the repository (version in src/frontend/.nvmrc).
pip uv pipx Check the install: A version number means the aiui command is on your path. Next: the quick start. The wheel installs two commands that do the same thing: aiui and praisonaiui.

The base install runs the server, the chat UI and aiui build. Extras add integrations. Install one with pip install "aiui[ ]". Extra Adds praisonai PraisonAI Agents, the PraisonAI wrapper, gateway and bot dependencies, for --backend praisonai. A YAML chat app (aiui run chat.yaml) needs only pip install praisonaiagents memory ChromaDB and LiteLLM for agent memory knowledge mem0, ChromaDB, MarkItDown and Chonkie for the knowledge base graph mem0 graph memory sql SQLAlchemy (async) and aiosqlite for SQLAlchemyDataStore postgres sql plus asyncpg bot Telegram, Discord and Slack bot libraries slack, discord, teams One channel's SDK only mcp The MCP client SDK a2ui PraisonAI Agents with A2UI support (agent canvas) langchain, llama-index, semantic-kernel Framework integrations all Every extra above dev pytest, ruff, mypy and the test dependencies (for contributors) The list is [project.optional-dependencies] in pyproject.toml.

Nothing in this repository is published to npm for the current UI: src/frontend/package.json is private and its build is committed into the Python package. Plugins for the React app shell import @aiui/sdk, which the shell provides at runtime; see UI plugins. The older praisonaiui package on npm (0.1.0) is a separate docs-site runtime, described under TypeScript SDK; aiui run and aiui build do not use it.
To work on PraisonAIUI itself: See Testing for the test commands.

s.x: The style decides which frontend serves your app. aiui run picks one from your code when you do not name it.

Style What it renders chat React chat interface: sessions, streaming, starters, profiles agents React multi-agent view with a tabbed agent/session sidebar playground React side-by-side input and output panels for prompt testing dashboard The legacy vanilla-JS admin dashboard with built-in and custom pages (only when asked for) docs React documentation site (sidebar, table of contents, search) custom React site built from your YAML templates and components, with an optional floating chat widget app The React app shell with selectable layouts (the default) app is what create_app() and aiui run open when nothing else picks a style (owner decision, 2026-11-22); aiui run starts it in the chat layout (no canvas) unless the app, its YAML or AIUI_LAYOUT picks another. See React app shell for what it contains and Layouts for its layouts.

After loading app.py, the CLI looks at the callbacks and agents it registered (server.detect_style): Your code registers Detected style @aiui.profiles and at least one aiui.register_agent() agents one or more @aiui.page(...) callbacks app (it lists the pages; dashboard before 2026-11-22) anything else, such as @aiui.reply only app (the React app shell, chat layout)
--style has no default value, so any style you name, chat included, wins over aiui.set_style() and detection.
A YAML chat app (aiui run chat.yaml) reads style: and applies it through aiui.set_style():
AIUI_SHELL=app turns the dashboard style into app; AIUI_SHELL=legacy turns app back into dashboard (the kill switch). It has no effect on the other styles.

layout.mode in a YAML site config places the React chat on the page instead of filling it: layout.mode Description fullscreen Full-page chat (default) sidebar Fixed right-side panel bottom-right Floating widget, bottom-right corner bottom-left Floating widget, bottom-left corner top-right Floating widget, top-right corner top-left Floating widget, top-left corner In the docs and custom styles, chat.enabled: true with one of the four corner modes adds the floating chat widget on top of the site. In the dashboard style the equivalent is aiui.set_chat_mode("fullpage" | "floating" | "sidebar").

Pages built in Python with @aiui.page and aiui blocks - filters in the URL, forms and page actions, lazy tabs, auto refresh and job status.

s.x: A server page is a Python function that returns blocks. The app shell (style: app, the default) fetches them from GET /api/pages/{id}/data and renders them; forms and buttons talk back through POST /api/pages/{id}/action. Both endpoints sit behind the same auth as every other /api/* route. This guide builds a filter page step by step. Each part works on its own.

@aiui.page("channels", title="Channels") on a function that returns aiui.layout([...]) ({"_components": [...]}) makes a page; every helper in aiui (metric, table, tabs, form, ...) is a block, see Components. aiui.register_page(id, title=..., handler=fn) does the same without the decorator. Run the app with aiui run app.py.

s.h: 2. Page parameters: filters in the URL
s.x: A handler that takes params receives the page URL's query string as a dict. A key given once is a string; a key given more than once is a list: The handler is matched by its signature: a parameter named params (or **kwargs) gets it by keyword, a single required positional parameter gets it positionally, and a handler with no parameters is called as before. The app shell sends the URL's query string with every data request, so a filtered view survives a refresh, a bookmark and a shared link. The page's Refresh button re-fetches with the current params.

aiui.form(action_id, children=[...], submit_label=...) collects every input inside it by name (or by its label when it has no name). Give inputs a name so the keys are stable. The first argument is the action id, normally the page id. There are two ways to submit.

The values are written into the page URL (history.replaceState) and the page data is fetched again, so the page handler sees them in params. No action handler is needed. This is the right choice for a filter form: Render each input with value= taken from params, so the form shows the active filters after a refresh. An empty value removes its key from the URL; other keys in the URL stay. Keys starting with _ are never written.

The values are POSTed as JSON to /api/pages/{page_id}/action. Handle them with aiui.register_page_action(page_id): What the reply can hold: Key Effect in the app shell _components Replaces the page with these blocks (return aiui.layout([...])). message (or status) A success toast. With _components, both happen. error An error toast; the page is left as it was. _params Written into the page URL's query string (aiui.layout([...], params={...})); None or "" removes a key. _refresh_every Starts or changes auto refresh (section 5). aiui.form(..., update_url=True) writes the submitted values into the URL after a successful POST, as method="get" does. Use it when the action both does something and changes the view; a reply's _params wins over it. A button posts {**payload, "action": action, "_params": {...}}. A form posts its values alongside "_params" (the page URL's current query string, same dict shape as params in the page handler).

To stream LLM tokens or step-by-step progress live without polling, make your @aiui.register_page_action handler an async def (or sync) generator that yields aiui.layout([...]) frames: The server streams each yielded frame as application/x-ndjson; the app shell updates the page live and displays a Stop button to cancel the stream.

Heavy sections can load when they are first opened instead of with the page: With lazy=True, a tab item without children is lazy; its key is its load value, or its label. An item with children renders at once. aiui.expander(title, lazy=True, load=key): the key defaults to the title. The body is fetched with POST /api/pages/{id}/action and the JSON body {"_lazy": key, "_params": {...}}. Reply with _components, as for any action. A reply with error (or an HTTP error) shows the message and a "Try again" button; a skeleton shows while it loads. Once loaded, a section stays loaded. When the page data reloads (Refresh, auto refresh, an action that re-renders), open sections fetch again; a closed one fetches again the next time it opens.

refresh_every (seconds, at least 1) re-fetches the page while its browser tab is visible. It pauses while the tab is hidden and resumes when it is shown again. After a failure it keeps the last good content, shows one error toast and doubles the wait on each failure in a row (up to 5 minutes). Set it when you register the page, or per reply (a reply's value wins, so a page can refresh only while something runs): @aiui.page(..., refresh_every=10) and aiui.register_page(..., refresh_every=10) set a fixed period; the data reply carries it as _refresh_every unless the handler set that key. @aiui.page(..., badge=...) and aiui.register_page(..., badge=...) show a short pill beside the page title in the app shell sidebar (across Classic and all selectable layouts). Pass a string, an integer, or a zero-argument callable (evaluated when the manifest is served) for live counts such as unread items or queued jobs. To update badges dynamically after an action without reloading the page, return aiui.layout([...], badges={"inbox": 2}) (or refresh_manifest=True).

aiui run app.yaml can declare server-driven block pages directly in YAML (alongside built-in page ids such as chat): Every component block (card, metric, table, chart, gallery, card_grid, filter_bar, select_input, list_detail, markdown_text, doc_viewer, pagination, color_picker_input, …) uses the same JSON/YAML dict format as Python's aiui.* helpers. Large apps can split page definitions into separate files with $ref: (e.g. - $ref: ./pages/overview.yaml). Edits to the YAML file, any $ref-included file, or a referenced markdown_file reload dynamically on the next fetch without restarting the server. Set api_endpoint: instead of components: to back a YAML-declared page with a custom API or plugin endpoint.

The app shell supports everything in this guide. The legacy dashboard style renders the page and its forms. It ignores params, method="get", lazy loading and refresh_every, and shows a status as plain text.

pages.d: A dashboard with only your pages, in the new app shell, with its own chat history.

s.x: Your own pages, Chat when you have a @reply, and nothing else: no built-in tabs, no pages from other apps on the machine, no other apps' chats.
The sidebar shows Chat and a My posts group with your two pages. Every layout of the app shell lists your pages in their group, and the layout picker still works.

You want Use The new app shell Nothing: style: app is the default. aiui.set_style("app") makes it explicit Only your pages aiui.only_my_pages() or aiui.set_pages([]) Your pages and Chat (minimal preset) aiui.set_pages("minimal") or aiui.only_my_pages("chat") (automatic default when running aiui run app.py with @aiui.page/@aiui.reply) Core Agent preset (Chat, Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory) aiui.set_pages("agent") or aiui run app.py --preset agent A few specific built-in pages aiui.set_pages(["chat", "sessions", "usage"]) (ids: aiui pages ids) Every page (full Ops console) aiui.set_pages("ops") / aiui.set_pages("all") or aiui run app.py --preset ops

Wrap any Python function (sync, async def, or streaming yield generator) into an interactive page without writing separate @aiui.page and @aiui.register_page_action handlers: set_pages is the one switch for what shows. It covers built-in pages, the app shell's layout pages (start, artifacts, templates, connect, api-reference) and dashboard-plugin folders, including the ones in ~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins that every app on the machine would otherwise share. Pages you register yourself (@aiui.page, aiui.register_page, aiui.register_plugin) always show. A wrong id is reported at startup: set_pages() names 'chta', but no page has that id.

A server-driven page: @aiui.page(id, title=..., icon=..., group=..., order=...) returning aiui.layout([...]) of blocks (aiui.metric, aiui.table, aiui.columns, aiui.markdown_text, aiui.card, ...). Pages with the same group sit together in the sidebar; order sorts them. Links: a page of markdown links, as links above. A React page or a whole plugin: see UI Plugins.

aiui run app.py keeps the app's chats in its own folder, ~/.praisonaiui/apps/ - /sessions/, so the sidebar never lists the chats of other apps or agents. Point it elsewhere with --datastore sdk:/path (or json:/path), or share the old machine-wide history with --datastore sdk. Set AIUI_DATA_DIR to move everything aiui keeps (config, sessions) for one app. See Sessions.

aiui.set_pages("all") (or aiui run app.py --pages all) is the opposite of a focused app: every page of the product, each in its React version where there is one and otherwise the legacy view inside the new shell, with every group (Agent, Work, Control, ...) listed in the sidebar of whatever layout is on. Your own pages still show in their group.

s.h: Mount only the shell (no agent endpoints)
s.x: When you embed PraisonAIUI as a dedicated dashboard host and do not want agent/chat endpoints (/sessions, /run, /agents, /teams, /api/chat/*) mounted on the port, use aiui.create_shell_app() instead of create_app(). Pass csp="strict" (or a directive mapping / callable) to attach a strict Content-Security-Policy with the exact 'sha256-…' hashes of the shell's inline scripts — no HTML buffering middleware or manual route allowlists needed: GET /focus serves the plugin page under a strict script-src 'self' 'sha256-…' header; GET /sessions and other unmounted routes return 404. For custom hosts that render the HTML themselves, aiui.render_shell_html(request) returns (html, script_hashes) and aiui.shell_csp_header(html) formats the full header (connect-src 'self' covers same-origin WebSockets; pass extra= for any external host).

s.h: Check it before you call it done
s.x: The list must hold only your page ids (and chat). Then open the page in a headless browser and look at the sidebar.

style: dashboard is the old vanilla UI. It still works (aiui run app.py --style dashboard, aiui.set_style("dashboard"), YAML style: dashboard or AIUI_SHELL=legacy, which prints a one-line notice), and set_pages applies there too, but new apps should not use it. Docs and examples that pass --style dashboard describe the legacy UI.

pages.d: A UI plugin is a Python package that adds pages, blocks, chat tool renderers,

s.x: A UI plugin is a Python package that adds pages, blocks, chat tool renderers, settings sections, sidebar groups, theme presets, HTTP routes and CLI commands to the React app shell (style: app, or AIUI_SHELL=app). Installing the package is the whole setup: the server finds it through the praisonaiui.plugins entry point. The smallest complete plugin lives in examples/plugins/aiui-hello-plugin. aiui run app.py opens the app shell (style: app) unless the app, its YAML or --style picks another style, so a plain @aiui.reply app needs no flag. AIUI_SHELL=app only switches the dashboard style to the app shell; it leaves an explicit chat or other React style alone (the server logs AIUI_SHELL=app ignored: style is 'chat'). Then open /hello (a React page) and /hello-blocks (a server-driven page). Three different things are called plugins UI plugins (this page): Python packages, entry point praisonaiui.plugins, React app shell only. Policy in YAML extensions:. Dashboard plugins: folders with a manifest.json under dashboard-plugins/, vanilla JS views (see Agent UI host). The app shell still hosts them as legacy pages. Docs plugins: site.plugins in aiui.yaml (static site compiler hooks). The default is nav-intercept; see Deploy to GitHub Pages → Legacy plugins.

The server imports each entry point once, isolates failures, and lists what the plugin contributes in the shell manifest. The shell installs window.__AIUI_SDK__ and then import()s every plugin module named in the manifest. An import map points the bare specifiers react, react/jsx-runtime, react-dom, react-dom/client and @aiui/sdk at small shims that re-export the shell's own modules, so a plugin shares the shell's single React (hooks work, nothing is bundled twice). A module registers what it provides through @aiui/sdk, or default-exports a component that the shell registers under the page id / block type / tool name. The app's own React pages and blocks use the same mechanism. The shell and the SDK are a small core that names no page: the chat page and its "New chat" command are the first-party plugin builtin.chat in src/frontend/src/builtin, registered with registerPage and registerCommand when the manifest lists the page; the approval toasts are builtin.approvals (on notify and navigate); and the core block types are registered with registerBlock. A test in the frontend (shell/core-purity.test.ts) fails if the core imports a feature module or names a built-in page.

The value names a plugin object, a class (instantiated with no arguments) or a zero-argument factory. The entry-point name becomes a URL segment, so it must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*. Every member except name is optional: Member Returns Effect name str Plugin id (/api/plugins/, /_plugins/ /, aiui) version str Shown by aiui plugins list sdk int Browser SDK major the plugin targets (default 1); a mismatch marks it incompatible pages() PageSpec or dicts Sidebar pages blocks() BlockSpec Renderers for block types tool_renderers() ToolRendererSpec Chat renderers for tool calls routes() Starlette routes Mounted under /api/plugins/ static_dir() Path Served at /_plugins/ / features() feature protocols Registered like built-in features (an enabled built-in's names win) cli_commands() typer.Typer or click command aiui … and aiui plugins … setup(ctx) None Called once per create_app() with {"style", "config"} lifespan(app) async/sync context manager Entered on ASGI startup and exited LIFO on shutdown (in both create_app() and create_shell_app()); failures are isolated per plugin settings() SettingsSectionSpec or dicts Sections of the shell's settings dialog (below) nav_groups() NavGroupSpec or dicts The sidebar groups your pages use, with their position themes() ThemeSpec or dicts Theme presets made of seed tokens layouts() LayoutSpec or dicts App shell frames (ADR 0003) the viewer can pick (below) PageSpec, BlockSpec, ToolRendererSpec, SettingsSectionSpec, SettingsField, NavGroupSpec, ThemeSpec, LayoutSpec and get_plugin_settings are importable from praisonaiui (or praisonaiui.plugin_registry). Dicts with the same field names work too.

kind Renders Needs react The component from module (default export, or export) module blocks A server-driven block tree (see below) api_endpoint, default /api/plugins/ /pages/ iframe module in a sandboxed iframe (no same-origin access) module These three are the only kinds a plugin can use. native and legacy are first-party only (the shell never imports a plugin's legacy view): a plugin page with another kind, or a misspelt one, is dropped with a warning and aiui plugins doctor fails on it. A relative module ("hello.js") resolves into static_dir(); the server then serves /_plugins/ /hello.js and adds its sha384 integrity to the manifest and the import map. The integrity is a cache-consistency check, not tamper protection: the server hashes the file it is about to serve (re-hashed when the file changes, so a rebuilt bundle keeps loading), which guards against a stale or partly written file between the page render and the module fetch. Someone who can change files in the plugin's static_dir can also change what is hashed. Declare integrity= on the PageSpec to pin a hash you computed at build time. When auth is enforced the page carries no manifest (and so no import-map integrity) before login; the shell loads plugin modules afterwards. When two sources use the same page id, the first wins: pages registered by the app (aiui.register_page), then built-in pages, then entry-point plugins (in discovery order), then dashboard-plugin folders. aiui plugins doctor warns about shadowed ids.

s.h: Settings, nav groups and theme presets
s.x: Three hooks contribute to the shell itself rather than to a page. They were added under SDK 1; a shell that has them lists the features settings, nav-groups and theme-presets in SDK_FEATURES, and an older host simply never calls them. Nav groups. NavGroupSpec(name, order=None, folded=False) names a group that your pages use in PageSpec.group. order places it among the groups: the groups the app lists in layout.groups.order (Agent, Work, Control by default) sit at 100, 200 and 300, groups without an order follow them, and layout.groups.last (Settings) stays last. So order=250 puts the group between Work and Control, and order=50 puts it first. folded=True starts the group collapsed until the viewer opens it. The app's own configuration wins: a plugin cannot move a group that layout.groups (or set_dashboard(groups=...)) names. Every frame lists a declared group. The classic frame shows all groups in its sidebar; the built-in layouts, which keep the app's own groups in More (⌘K), still show the groups plugins declared, in this order and folded as declared: under the primary pages in chat, chat-canvas, workbench and mission, in the rail in command, and under More tools in guided. Settings. A SettingsSectionSpec(id, title, fields, description="", order=100) becomes a section of the shell's settings dialog, which opens from "Plugin settings" (the sliders button in the classic header, a "Plugin settings" row or rail button in every built-in layout, shown only while some plugin has a section) or from "Plugin settings" in the command palette. Each SettingsField(key, label="", type="string", default=None, description="", options=None) is drawn from its type: type Control Default value string One-line text input "" text Multi-line text area "" number Number input 0 boolean Switch False select Select from options (strings or {"value", "label"} dicts) the first option The values are stored per plugin in $AIUI_DATA_DIR/plugin-settings/ .json (default ~/.praisonaiui). The server serves each section at /api/plugins/ /settings/: GET returns {"values": {...}} with the defaults filled in, and PUT {"values": {...}} validates every key against its field (unknown keys, wrong types and options not in the list answer 400 with {"error", "fields": {key: reason}}, and nothing is written). That path is reserved for a plugin that declares settings(): it is matched before the plugin's own routes. It sits under the same mount as routes(), so it is authenticated like every route and default-deny for entry-point plugins on remote or auth-enforced servers unless they are named in extensions.enabled. get_plugin_settings(name, section) returns the same values to Python; a stored value that no longer fits its field (an option you removed) falls back to the default. Theme presets. A ThemeSpec(id, label, light={}, dark={}) sets L0 seed tokens per colour mode: --seed-* (--seed-accent, --seed-tint, --seed-paper, --seed-ink …), --radius, --tint-mix and --accent-mix. Every surface, text and accent colour is derived from the seeds (see DESIGN.md), so a preset never names a shadcn variable. Values are plain CSS values; anything else (another property, ;, braces, url(...)) is rejected. The viewer picks a preset in the command palette ("Sunrise theme", "Default theme"); the choice is kept per browser. Invalid entries of all three hooks (and of layouts()) are dropped one by one with a warning, and one hook that raises does not drop the others. The warning is printed once per start in the aiui run terminal (and on the Logs page), and aiui plugins doctor runs every entry through the same checks and fails on each one it would drop. The contributions travel on the plugin's record in the shell manifest (plugins[].settings, plugins[].navGroups, plugins[].themes), only for plugins whose browser surfaces the viewer may load.

The pages and features that ship with PraisonAIUI use the same mechanism. Each domain is a first-party plugin record in praisonaiui.builtin: for example builtin.chat holds the Chat and Chat + Canvas pages with the chat and attachments features, and builtin.work holds Work Hub, Kanban and Jobs Board with the kanban feature. Features with no page of their own have a record each (builtin.tts, builtin.pwa, builtin.video …). The server reads pages and features through the plugin registry, so the extension policy can switch a whole domain off: or aiui.set_extensions(disabled=["builtin.training"]). A disabled built-in contributes no pages: they leave GET /api/pages, the shell manifest and the sidebar. Its feature routes are not mounted (/api/training/... returns 404), the server does not load its feature modules, and a bundled dashboard-plugin folder that belongs to it (kanban belongs to builtin.work, video-studio to builtin.video, the sample-board demo page in the Examples group to builtin.examples) is not served either. The same holds for the routes the host itself serves for a built-in: builtin.mcp owns /api/mcp/*, builtin.debug owns /api/debug, builtin.overview owns GET /api/overview, builtin.feedback owns GET /api/feedback and builtin.jobs owns the optional /api/jobs proxy (set_jobs_proxy), so disabling them returns 404 there. builtin.logs serves GET /api/logs and /api/logs/* from its feature, and installs its log handler only while it is on. With the built-in off, an entry-point plugin may use its page ids and feature names. A few host routes stay mounted whichever built-ins are off, because the host, several pages or the CLI use them: GET /api/status (aiui status, the same data as /api/overview), POST /api/feedback (the chat thumbs), /api/config, /api/gateway/status, /api/provider*, the chat protocol (/agents, /sessions, /run, /cancel, /teams, /starters, /profiles, /welcome, /api/actions/*, thread sharing), /health*, auth, /api/pages, /api/features, /api/shell/manifest and /api/plugins. Disabling builtin.config removes its page only. Where a page id is also a JSON path (/agents, /sessions, or an app page named like an API), a browser navigation to / gets the page and fetch() gets the JSON, under the dashboard and app styles. tests/unit/test_route_table_snapshot.py pins the default route table. Some features are required: the server itself depends on auth, theme, chat, usage, config_runtime and sessions_ext. Disabling their record (builtin.auth, builtin.theme-picker, builtin.chat, builtin.usage, builtin.config, builtin.sessions) removes its pages and its other features, keeps the required feature mounted and logs a warning. Disabling builtin.auth therefore never turns authentication off. Built-ins are trusted and on by default. extensions.enabled is an allowlist for third-party plugins only, so it never hides a built-in page. Only the builtin. name disables a built-in: disabled: [logs] means a third-party plugin called logs. A builtin. name that matches no record logs a warning. The page-level controls still apply on top: aiui.set_pages([...]), pages.enabled / pages.disabled in config.yaml and aiui.remove_page() hide single pages (their APIs stay mounted), and aiui.register_page() with a built-in id replaces that page. register_feature() before the server starts replaces a built-in feature of the same name, as before. GET /api/plugins?origin=builtin (or origin=all) lists the built-in records with their status (and required: true where the host needs one of their features). Without the parameter the endpoint lists third-party plugins only, as before.

A plugin module is plain ESM. Write it by hand (the example uses react/jsx-runtime directly) or build it with React and the SDK as externals: Only those five bare specifiers are mapped. Anything else must be bundled into the plugin file or imported by full URL.

Registration: Export Use SDK_VERSION 1 SDK_FEATURES List of capability names, for feature detection registerPage(id, Component) Component receives { page } (its manifest entry). A zero-argument arrow function is treated as a lazy loader: registerPage('x', () => import('./X.js')) registerBlock(type, Component, options?) Component receives { node, page }; node is { type, props, children }. It also overrides a core block type of the same name. { fallback: true } registers a default that anything else overrides registerToolRenderer(toolName, Component) Chat tool call UI; receives assistant-ui tool part props (toolName, args, argsText, result, status, …) registerSlot(name, Component, options?) Add a component to a slot of the shell registerCommand(command) Add an entry to the command palette. Returns a function that removes it. Groups list before the pages, in registration order; the groups Preferences, Layout and Theme list after them registerView(pageId, render, cleanup?) A vanilla view for a legacy page (same as window.aiui.registerView in custom.js) registerSettingsSection(section) Add a section to the shell's settings dialog: { id, title, description?, order?, fields, load(), save(values) }, fields as in settings(). A save rejection whose error has body.fields shows those messages next to the fields. Returns a remover registerNavGroup(name, { order, folded }?) Declare the sidebar group your pages use, like nav_groups(). Returns a remover registerThemePreset({ id, label, light?, dark? }) Offer a seed-token theme preset, like themes(). Returns a remover registerLayout(id, meta, Frame \ loader) Add a layout (the frame around every page). getLayouts(), useLayout(), setLayout(id), provideLayoutData(kind, feed) and useLayoutData(kind) go with it. Returns a remover onActivate(fn) Run fn({ manifest }) once the app is ready getPage, getBlock, getSlot, getToolRenderers Registry lookups subscribe(fn), useRegistryVersion() React to later registrations Shell services and components: Export Use navigate(pageId, { replace, params }?) Go to a page of the app: navigate('logs') pageHref(pageId, params?) Format an in-app page URL path (pageHref('revenue', { range: '30d' }) → /revenue?range=30d) pageLinkProps(pageId, params?, { replace }?) Return { href, onClick } for an in-app link: plain left click navigates inside the shell with no full document reload (Back/Forward work), while Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt/middle-click keeps native new-tab behaviour useLiveData(key, fetcher, options?) Keyed, visibility-aware live data hook shared with built-in block pages: aborts in-flight reads on key change (never flashing stale page data), retains the last result on refresh failure alongside error, skips hidden tabs, backs off on failures, and refreshes once when returning to an overdue tab notify(message, options?) Show a toast. Options: type (info, success, warning, error), description, duration, id, action: { label, onClick } fetchJson(url, options?) fetch for JSON APIs. It sends the session's gateway token to same-origin URLs only, JSON-encodes a plain-object body (the method then defaults to POST), decodes the response, and rejects with an error carrying status, url and body on a non-2xx status useManifest() React hook returning the shell manifest (pages, plugins, site, layout) getPageId(), usePageId() The id of the page on screen ('' at /), read the way the shell's router reads the URL; the hook re-renders on navigation. Never parse location yourself useThemeMode() React hook returning 'light' or 'dark', updated when the viewer or the OS switches dismiss(id?) Close a toast raised with notify(message, { id }) (all toasts without an id) Markdown The shell's Markdown renderer: {text} Style with the theme's CSS variables (var(--foreground), var(--border), var(--primary), …). The shell's Tailwind build only contains the classes the shell itself uses, so Tailwind classes in a plugin may not exist.

Use the services instead of globals such as window.fetch or the history API. They work the same in every page kind and they are part of the SDK contract. A command that throws, or whose promise rejects, is reported as a toast. An onActivate hook that throws is logged and does not stop the other hooks. #### In-page tabs and live-refreshing data Use pageLinkProps() for in-page navigation links or tabs so ordinary clicks stay in the SPA shell (0 document reloads, Back works) while Cmd/Ctrl-click still opens a new tab. Pair it with useLiveData() to share the framework's abort-on-navigation, hidden-tab pause, retry backoff, and retain-last-result logic:

A slot is a place in the shell that renders components from plugins. Slot Where Extra props header:actions The header bar, before search and the theme toggle. Not shown when the app hides the page header sidebar:footer The bottom of the sidebar, on desktop and in the phone menu collapsed page: :toolbar Above the body of page , for example page:logs:toolbar Every slot component receives { slot, pageId, page }: the slot name, the id of the page on screen and its manifest entry. Pass { id, order } so that several plugins can share a slot. id is the identity of your contribution (use the plugin name), and a lower order comes first (default 100). Registering the same id again replaces only that contribution. Without options, the call sets the slot's single default contribution and replaces an earlier one. This is the original behaviour. Each contribution renders inside its own error boundary. One that throws is removed and logged; the others and the shell stay. A slot nobody contributes to renders nothing.

A layout owns the frame of the app shell: the navigation, the session list, the top bar, side panels and the phone chrome. The page stays the page: every page renders inside every layout, in the outlet the shell hands the frame (ADR 0003). aiui ships six layouts (chat, what aiui run opens; chat-canvas, the app shell's default; plus workbench, command, guided and mission); the core's own frame is called classic. A plugin adds a layout with the same call the built-ins use. Which layout is on screen. The server's manifest lists the layouts it offers (layouts.available) and its default. The browser takes the first of: a ?layout= preview (kept for the tab, never saved), the viewer's own choice (the palette's "Switch layout: …" commands or Settings → Appearance, saved in this browser, only when the server allows a user choice), the server default, the classic frame. A layout the server does not offer is never chosen. Declare it in Python with a layouts() hook, which returns LayoutSpecs (or dicts with the same field names), like pages(): LayoutSpec field Meaning id Lower-case letters, digits and -, starting with a letter, at most 40 characters; classic is reserved title, description Shown in the picker (palette and Settings → Appearance) order Picker position (default 100; the built-ins use 10 to 50) module Required for a plugin layout: the ESM file that registers the frame. A relative path resolves into static_dir() (/_plugins/ /) and gets an SRI integrity hash, which the import map carries like a page module's css Optional stylesheet, resolved the same way (its hash is cssIntegrity in the manifest and on the ), added when the layout first loads home The page / opens while this layout is on screen primary Page ids of the primary nav, in order (at most 7 shown; YAML layout.primary wins) look Optional: the meta.look your frame registers (an id such as paper). When the layout is the server's default, the server sets from the first byte, so the look's fonts load instead of the Pro ones. It is not sent in the manifest The first plugin (or built-in) to declare an id keeps it; a later one is ignored with a warning, as is a malformed or classic id. On a remote or auth-enforced server an entry-point plugin's layouts follow the same default-deny rule as its pages. Configuration (which layouts are offered, the default) is in Layouts → Plugin layouts. Register the frame in the browser. The shell imports the module only when the layout is first rendered, never with the other plugin modules, so an inactive layout costs nothing. The module either calls registerLayout(id, meta, Frame)while it is evaluated (itsmeta then replaces the manifest's title and description) or default-exports the frame: The complete example is src/frontend/e2e/fixtures/layout-plugin/ (the suite e2e/specs/layouts-host.spec.ts runs it). What the frame receives (LayoutProps): Prop What it is Outlet The routed page, with its error boundary, toolbar slot and loading state. Render it once, inside your main pageId, page, fullBleed The page on screen, its manifest entry, and whether it asked for no padding (chat, iframes): then give the outlet the full height and no scroll nav primary (at most 7, the layout's own list), groups (every other page, by sidebar group, with folded), footer, activeId, go(pageId). Items carry id, title, href, active, navIcon, icon, group chrome siteTitle, siteLogo, openPalette({ query? }) (the one command palette, optionally prefilled), toggleColorMode(), Slot (the shell's slot host: ), mainId (give your main this id: the skip link and the palette focus it) viewport 'phone' (< 768 px), 'tablet' (< 1024 px) or 'desktop'; draw your phone frame from it layout id, available (the offered layouts), switchTo(id) useLayout() returns { id, meta } of the layout on screen (null for the classic frame), setLayout(id, { persist }?) switches live ('' or 'classic' is the classic frame), and getLayouts() lists the registered ones. meta.chat tells the chat page how to present itself in your frame (who draws the session list, the thread style, lazy regions such as aside, turnFooter and composerTool); see the ADR. meta.look names a look of the Pro tokens the frame paints with (the shell ships paper; DESIGN.md "Looks"). Frames read data such as the session list with useLayoutData('sessions'), which returns null while nothing provides it: render without it. The chat feed (builtin.chat) also acts on the open chat: prefill(text) fills the composer, send?(text) sends (optional: check for it, and fall back to prefill), cancel() stops the reply, and resolveApproval(id, approved, { always? }) decides a gate in the thread. Failure. A layout whose module fails to import, or whose frame throws, is replaced by the classic frame with one toast and an aiui:plugin-error event (detail.layout is its id). Other layouts are not affected. Keep a frame self-contained: import React and @aiui/sdk only, style with the theme's CSS variables, give icon-only buttons an aria-label, and make phone touch targets at least 44 px.

The SDK grows without a new major version, so SDK_VERSION stays 1. A named import of an export that an older shell lacks fails when the module loads. When a plugin must also run on older shells, use the default export and ask before you call a newer function: Feature names: pages, blocks, tool-renderers, slots, views, markdown, navigate, notify, fetch-json, manifest, commands, activate, slots.multi (the { id, order } options and the slot hosts), blocks.fallback, page-id (getPageId, usePageId), theme-mode (useThemeMode), notify.dismiss, settings (registerSettingsSection and the settings() hook), nav-groups (registerNavGroup, nav_groups()), theme-presets (registerThemePreset, themes()), layouts (registerLayout, getLayouts, useLayout, setLayout, manifest layouts), layout-data (provideLayoutData, useLayoutData), slots.dispose (registerSlot returns a remover), page-links (pageHref, pageLinkProps), live-data (useLiveData), ws-transport (getWsTicket, openWebSocket) and block-tree (BlockTree). A shell older than the services has no SDK_FEATURES.

A plugin's routes() may include Starlette WebSocketRoute endpoints under /api/plugins/ /*. In the browser, open them with openWebSocket(path) from @aiui/sdk (feature ws-transport) so stored gateway tokens are automatically exchanged for a single-use 60-second ticket via POST /api/auth/ws-ticket (credentials are never attached to cross-origin URLs): Call getWsTicket() directly if you construct a custom WebSocket URL yourself.

s.h: Reusing built-in blocks in React pages (BlockTree)
s.x: Custom kind="react" pages and plugin layouts can compose any built-in block (metric, table, diff_viewer, tree_view, timeline, status, button_group, …) or plugin-registered block via from @aiui/sdk (feature block-tree). The blocks engine loads lazily on first use, so shell boot size stays unchanged:

@aiui/sdk is not an npm package: the shell provides it at runtime. Its types are in src/frontend/src/sdk/aiui-sdk.d.ts, the frontend build also writes dist/aiui-sdk.d.ts, and the installed package ships the same file at praisonaiui/templates/frontend/aiui-sdk.d.ts (find it with python -c "import praisonaiui, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(praisonaiui.__file__).parent / 'templates/frontend/aiui-sdk.d.ts')"). Copy the file into a plugin project and include it in tsconfig.json (or jsconfig.json with checkJs) to type-check the plugin. It depends on @types/react only.

Each module is imported once. If one fails to load (network error, syntax error, no component to register), the shell logs it, shows a toast, fires an aiui:plugin-error window event, and loads everything else. The page shows "unavailable" instead of crashing. A block that throws while rendering is replaced by an inline error; the rest of the page still renders.

A docs site can use a block whose type is named like a component (HelloCard): in a page of an aiui build site renders it, and the build publishes the plugin's static folder with the site (your own components).

A blocks page is data, not code: its endpoint returns a component tree and the shell renders it with built-in React blocks. Page handlers already written for the dashboard (aiui.register_page(handler=…) with aiui.ui.* helpers) render unchanged. The payload may be {"_components": [...]} (also components, blocks, or a bare list), and each item is a flat dict ({"type": "card", "title": …}) or {"type", "props", "children"}. A button with action and every form POST JSON to the action endpoint: page.actionEndpoint (set for aiui.register_page_action), else /action for plugin pages, else /api/pages/ /action. A response with a component list replaces the page; message is shown as a toast; error (or a non-2xx status) as an error toast. Resolution order for a block type: a block registered with registerBlock(type, C), a window.aiui.registerComponent renderer from custom.js, a block registered with { fallback: true } (the core blocks are registered this way), then the legacy dashboard renderer, so every existing _components type keeps working. Text is always rendered as text, never as HTML. Links and images only accept relative, http(s), mailto: and tel: URLs (images also data:image/*). Core block types: text, caption, header/heading, markdown_text/markdown, code_block/code, json_view/json, card, metric/stat, stat_group, progress_bar/progress, columns/grid, row, container, separator/divider, tabs, expander, accordion, table, key_value_list, list, badge, alert, callout, empty, spinner, skeleton, toast, image_display/image, link, button/action, button_group, form_action/form, text_input, number_input, date_input, time_input, textarea_input, select_input, checkbox_input, switch_input, radio_input, slider_input.

Installing a plugin means trusting it: its Python runs in the server process and its JavaScript runs in the page with no sandbox (use kind: iframe for untrusted content). Because any installed package, including a transitive dependency, can declare the entry point, the browser parts of entry-point plugins (pages, blocks, tool renderers and /_plugins/ /) and their HTTP routes (/api/plugins/ /*) are default-deny when the server requires auth or is reached from a non-loopback address. They are listed as disabled-by-default (and answer 404) until you enable the plugin by name. The plugin's Python code still runs (setup(), features()): to keep an installed package from being imported at all, put it in extensions.disabled. extensions: [hello] is shorthand for enabled. From Python: aiui.set_extensions(enabled=["hello"]) (it beats YAML). A plugin object registered with aiui.register_plugin(obj) was chosen by the app author and is always trusted: the enabled allowlist does not apply to it, so extensions: {enabled: [hello]} never switches your own plugin off. Only extensions.disabled (its name) does. AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 skips the entry-point group entirely (the test suite sets it).

Command Does aiui plugins list [--json] [--config aiui.yaml] The built-in records (builtin.: status ok or disabled, whether the host requires part of it, its pages), then installed plugins with version, status (ok, error, disabled, incompatible, disabled-by-default) and load error. --json puts the built-ins under builtins aiui plugins doctor [--config aiui.yaml] [--no-builtin] Loads each plugin and checks SDK version, static_dir(), every module file and its sha384 (pages, blocks, tool renderers, layouts), page kinds, every settings(), nav_groups(), themes() and layouts() entry, routes, CLI name clashes and page ids shadowed by built-in pages or other plugins. A page shadowed by a built-in names the builtin. to add to extensions.disabled; a builtin. name that matches no record is a warning. Exits 1 on any failure aiui …, aiui plugins … The plugin's own commands aiui --help and built-in commands never import plugins; discovery runs only when a command name is not a built-in one.

Symptom Check Page says "unavailable" aiui plugins doctor; the browser console shows the import error Plugin listed as disabled-by-default Remote or auth-enforced server: add it to extensions.enabled Invalid hook call The module bundled its own React: mark react and react/jsx-runtime external does not provide an export named … The shell is older than the SDK export the module imports: see feature detection A slot component does not appear Check the slot name, and that the page header or sidebar is not hidden by the app aiui shell not booted The module was loaded outside the app shell (style must be app) Integrity error after editing a file The manifest hashes the file on every request; hard-reload the page so the browser drops its cached copy

pages.d: Side-by-side guide for moving Streamlit dashboards and chat apps to PraisonAIUI.

s.x: PraisonAIUI gives Python developers zero-JS UI components like Streamlit, built natively for AI Agents — with WebSocket streaming, tool calls, reasoning traces, inline approvals, persistent multi-session history, URL-synced filter bars, and built-in auth.

Streamlit PraisonAIUI (aiui) st.chat_message / st.chat_input @aiui.reply + aiui.stream_token() + aiui.send_block(...) st.dataframe(df) aiui.table(df, searchable=True) (pandas & Polars, works on pages and in chat) st.data_editor(df) aiui.sheet("Data", headers=..., rows=..., action="save") st.bar_chart(df) / st.plotly_chart(fig) aiui.chart("Title", data=df, chart_type="bar") / aiui.plotly_chart(fig) st.metric("Users", 42, "+12%") aiui.metric("Users", value=42, delta="+12%", sparkline=[...]) st.file_uploader("CSV") aiui.file_upload("CSV", name="doc", accept=".csv") + aiui.get_uploaded_file(data["doc"]) st.write_stream(gen) yield aiui.layout([...]) inside @aiui.register_page_action or aiui.interface() st.columns(2) aiui.columns([left, right]) (including aiui.chat_panel() for split-pane agent workspaces) streamlit run app.py aiui run app.py (opens cleanly in focused mode; pass --preset ops for full ops console)

Streamlit re-executes your whole script top-to-bottom on every widget click. PraisonAIUI uses explicit @aiui.page / @aiui.register_page_action handlers (or 5-line aiui.interface()) — so heavy models stay loaded in memory, filters live cleanly in the URL (method="get"), and chat sessions persist across reloads.

pages.d: Side-by-side guide for moving Gradio demos and Chatbot apps to PraisonAIUI.

s.x: Move from a prototype Gradio demo to a production multi-page Agent UI with persistent sessions, auth, inline approvals, and 81 composable blocks — while keeping Gradio's 5-line function simplicity via aiui.interface().

Gradio PraisonAIUI (aiui) gr.Interface(fn, inputs, outputs).launch() aiui.interface(fn, inputs=[...], title="App") + aiui run app.py gr.ChatInterface(fn) @aiui.reply + await aiui.stream_token(tok) gr.File() aiui.file_upload("Upload", name="doc") + aiui.get_uploaded_file(doc) Generator yield streaming yield directly inside aiui.interface() or @aiui.register_page_action gr.Chatbot inside gr.Blocks aiui.chat_panel() inside aiui.columns([...]) gr.Dataframe / gr.Plot aiui.table(df) / aiui.chart(data=df) / aiui.plotly_chart(fig)

For live webcam/sketchpad ML model demos (gr.Image(tool="sketch"), gr.Webcam), Gradio remains specialized for ML demos. PraisonAIUI shines when you are shipping AI Agent applications with tool calls, approvals, dashboards, file uploads, and authentication.

pages.d: Side-by-side guide for moving decorator-style Python agent chat apps to PraisonAIUI.

s.x: PraisonAIUI keeps the familiar async decorator lifecycle (@aiui.on_chat_start, @aiui.on_message, @aiui.on_stop, aiui.Message, aiui.Step, aiui.user_session) while adding 81 interactive UI blocks (usable both inline in chat and on custom pages), split-pane workspaces, selectable layouts, zero-code YAML apps, and an opt-in Agent Ops console.

Classic decorator pattern PraisonAIUI (aiui) @on_chat_start @aiui.on_chat_start (or @aiui.welcome) @on_message @aiui.reply (alias: @aiui.on_message) @on_stop @aiui.cancel (alias: @aiui.on_stop) Message(content=...).send() await aiui.say(...) or await aiui.Message(...).send() msg.stream_token(tok) await aiui.stream_token(tok) Step(...) async with aiui.Step(...) / await aiui.tool(...) Dataframe(df) / Plotly(fig) await aiui.send_block(aiui.table(df)) / await aiui.send_block(aiui.plotly_chart(fig)) (plus aiui.Dataframe / aiui.Plotly also render natively) Custom React Elements 81 built-in Python/YAML blocks (aiui.send_block(...)) + @aiui/sdk plugins CLI runner aiui run app.py (or aiui run app.py --preset agent for Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory)

pages.d: Turn a folder of Markdown files and one aiui.yaml into a fast, searchable documentation site with tabs, SEO, llms.txt and optional sign-in.

s.x: PraisonAIUI includes a complete static documentation builder. Write plain Markdown files, organize your menus in aiui.yaml, and generate a fast, searchable site — the exact site you are reading right now is built this way.

s.h: Launch a docs site in 3 steps
s.x: This creates aiui.yaml with site branding, theme, search and navigation defaults. Create pages under docs/ using standard Markdown plus built-in components like , , , and Mermaid diagrams: Deploy the built output to GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or serve it with aiui serve.

Feature Why it helps Guide Tabs, groups & icons Divide docs cleanly into top-level menus and nested sidebar groups Navigation Rich Markdown components Steps, tabs, cards, callouts, accordions, code highlights and Mermaid Writing docs Instant search & SEO Client-side search with tab filtering, OpenGraph tags and sitemap SEO AI-ready output Automatic llms.txt, llms-full.txt and Markdown source endpoints AI-ready docs API references Generate interactive docs from OpenAPI specs or Python docstrings OpenAPI Built-in sign-in Protect private docs or specific folders with a password in YAML Docs sign-in

Learn every frontmatter option, callout, tab, card and diagram block. Configure top-level tabs, sidebar groups, dropdowns and badges. Publish automatically on every push to main. Generate live API reference pages straight from your codebase.

pages.d: Every block a docs page can use, with its Markdown and a live example, and the look the site draws them in.

s.x: A docs site is a folder of Markdown and one YAML file. This page lists every block a page can use: the Markdown you write, then the block as this site draws it. Pages that aiui build publishes also exist as plain Markdown (/docs/ .md, components converted) and in llms.txt, so assistants read the same content (AI-ready docs).

site.theme.preset picks the colours. paper is the look of this site: warm paper, a navy accent, serif titles, 17px text on a 1.7 line height and a measure of about 75 characters. mode: system follows the reader's OS. The other presets and what each changes are in Theming.

YAML at the top of a page sets its title in the sidebar, the browser tab and search results, and its description for search engines and llms.txt. Every key is optional, and the common MDX page metadata keys work as they are. Key Type What it does title string The page title: the # heading when the body has none, the browser tab, search, llms.txt. Default: the first # heading, else the file name. description string Shown under the title (unless the first paragraph already says it), and the meta description, llms.txt and search snippet. Default: the first paragraph, for those but not shown again. sidebarTitle (or nav_title) string A shorter label in the sidebar. icon string Before the sidebar label: a lucide name (rocket, terminal, book-open, …), an emoji, or an image URL (https://… or /icons/x.svg). tag string A badge after the sidebar label, such as NEW or BETA. deprecated true/false true: a Deprecated badge, the label struck through, and a notice above the page. mode string wide: no "On this page", a wider column. center: no sidebar either. custom: only the article, full width (no breadcrumb, footer or pager). frame: custom with the sidebar. assistant: the page's text, then Ask AI under it. url string An https:// URL makes the page a sidebar link that opens that site in a new tab. The page itself is not published (no route, sitemap, llms.txt or search entry). hideFooterPagination true/false true: no previous / next links under the page. noAnchor true/false true: no copy-link icon on the page's headings. order number Position inside its folder (default: a number prefix such as 01-). hidden true/false Routable, but not in the sidebar, pager or indexes (Navigation). noindex true/false Tells search engines not to index the page (and leaves it out of the sitemap). searchable true/false false leaves the page out of the site's own search. keywords list of words, or one comma-separated string Extra search terms, matched but never shown; also the keywords meta tag and JSON-LD. canonical string The page's canonical URL (and og:url), for a page whose original lives elsewhere. robots string The robots meta, such as noindex, nofollow; a value with noindex also leaves the page out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search. og:*, twitter:*, article:* string That head tag for this page (quote the key: 'og:image': /images/card.png); site-wide: api.playground.display (OpenAPI). timestamp true/false Turns the "Last updated" date off or on for this page (see Page footer). lastUpdatedDate date (2026-05-01) The "Last updated" date, instead of the last commit's. related list of pages or URLs, or false The "Related pages" under this page, instead of the suggested ones; false shows none (Related pages). pageActions list of page actions, or false This page's page actions menu, in order, instead of the site's; false shows none (Page actions). rss true/false true on a changelog page: the build writes its entries as an RSS feed at /rss.xml and links it (Changelog). public true/false On a site with sign-in: true opens the page to everyone, false keeps it behind sign-in when a public pattern would open it. groups list of group names, or one name On a site with sign-in: only readers in one of these groups can read the page; Write a React component once and use it on any page as a tag. Point the site at one ES module beside aiui.yaml: The module registers each component with registerBlock from @aiui/sdk, or exports it under the tag's name. It imports React and the SDK as bare names: the build maps them to the page's own copies, so no bundler is needed for plain JS, and hooks work. Props. A quoted attribute is a string; {…} is a value: a number, true or false, an array or an object ({{ calls: 10 }}, JSON or JS-style); a bare attribute () is true. The component gets them as props, and as node.props like any block. Children. The tag's body is Markdown, rendered and passed as children. A self-closing tag that shares its line with text sits inside the sentence. Loading. The module loads only on a page that uses one of its tags, after the page has painted; until then, and if the module fails or the component throws, the page shows the tag's body. A built-in tag name (, ) keeps its built-in meaning. Tags. The build finds them in the module (registerBlock('Name' and export function Name). A minified bundle hides them: list them with site.components: {src: ./components/index.js, tags: [Counter, Price]}. Declared tags are not reported as unknown; a missing module, or one with no tag the build can find, is a 7021 warning. Security. The module is your site's own code, served from the site (script-src 'self'); the build adds the import map's hash to the Content-Security-Policy. Only same-site modules load. In the .md copy for agents the tag's body stays and the tag goes. Styles. Use the theme's CSS variables (var(--primary)), or add a stylesheet with site.customCss. Readers press ⌘ K ( Ctrl K ) or the search field. Search covers page titles, every ## and ### heading and all the text under it, and a result opens the page at its section with the words marked. It forgives typing: plurals and verb forms match ("themes", "theming"), a word matches as you type it ("inst"), one typo in a longer word still matches, and question words drop out ("how do I deploy"). Titles rank first, then headings, then text, each BM25 style. While the dialog is open the address bar carries the query, so a link such as /docs?q=api+keys opens search filled in. On a site with header tabs (Navigation), chips filter results by tab: search starts in the reader's tab, and one row offers the other tabs' results when it has none. A navigation group's boost: applies to its pages (a page's own wins). Site settings (search.provider is ignored and aiui validate says so): aiui build writes the index (search-index.json, up to 6,000 characters per section) and the same index in parts under search-index/, so the dialog downloads only what a query needs: Part Holds Fetched search-index/meta.json each page's path, keywords, boost and section headings with their word counts, and the sorted list of every word the first time a reader opens search search-index/ /w .json for a run of those words, the sections each appears in and how often when a query has a word in that run (by stem, prefix or one typo) search-index/ /p .json page i's section text when the page is in the results, for its snippets Ranking is the same as over the whole file: BM25, stems, prefixes, typos, keywords, boost and the tab chips. On this repository's 99 searchable pages the first open downloads 35 KB gzipped instead of 181 KB, and a first query about 13 KB more. is a hash of the index, so a page cached from an older deploy never mixes parts; a missing part, or a site built before the parts existed, makes the dialog read search-index.json whole, which every other reader (the MCP server, Ask AI, older pages) still uses. A site with sign-in gets no parts: its search-index.json is cut per reader.

List such a page in the nav by its file path (protocols/adp/README); the header still opens the tab that lists it.

aiui docs check-links finds every link that leads nowhere, before readers do: It checks Markdown links and images, reference links, href and src on components and HTML (, , ), the docs home hero and features links, the nav page entries and the navbar and footer links in the YAML. A #section link is checked against the ids the site gives its headings (## The aiui CLI is #the-aiui-cli). Links in code are skipped. Paths outside the docs (app routes such as /chat) are not judged. --external also requests every http(s) URL, and --json prints the result for scripts. The exit code is 1 when a link is broken, so a CI step needs one line. aiui validate --strict and aiui build --strict fail on broken links too; without --strict they print them as warnings.
