A printed page (Download as PDF, or the browser's own Print, Ctrl+P / ⌘P) is the article alone, on light paper even when the reader uses dark mode: The header, sidebar, "On this page", page actions, previous / next, footer and feedback are left out. Breadcrumbs and "Last updated" stay. Everything a click would reveal is shown: accordions, field lists and file trees open, every tab of and prints under its own title, and expandable code blocks print every line. Code wraps instead of running off the page; code blocks, callouts, cards, steps, table rows and images are not split across pages. External links print their address after the link text: link (https://example.com/docs). Site chrome added by custom JS (site.customJs) or a plugin can opt out of print with data-print="hide". The PDF comes from the reader's browser: no build step, no server-side renderer.

Under each page: "Was this page helpful?" (on by default, see Page feedback) and two optional parts, turned on in aiui.yaml: Edit this page links to pattern with :path replaced by the page's file under the docs folder (getting-started/quickstart.md). Last updated is the date of the last commit that changed the page. aiui build reads it from git. In a shallow clone, pages changed inside the cloned history keep their date; older ones get none rather than the clone's date. In GitHub Actions, check out with fetch-depth: 0 to date every page. A page's lastUpdatedDate: 2026-05-01 sets the date by hand, and timestamp: false (or true) turns it off (or on) for that page alone. Was this page helpful? keeps the vote (next section). With issues, a "No" also offers a new issue there with the page's title and address filled in. The footer of this page shows all three.

Under each page, "Related pages" lists the three pages closest to it. Nothing to configure: aiui build compares the words of every page (title, keywords, description and headings count most, then the text) and favours pages in the same sidebar group. Hidden, noindex and searchable: false pages and the home page are never suggested. The list is part of docs-nav.json, so it works on any static host and offline, and each page's agent-ready .md ends with it too. Pick the list for a page in its front matter, or turn it off: related: false shows none on that page. Site-wide, content.docs.related: 5 shows five (at most 10) and content.docs.related: false only the lists pages set themselves. aiui validate reports a target that is no page (7013). The block is left out when the page prints.

Nothing to configure: under aiui serve and aiui dev every docs page asks "Was this page helpful?". A vote is stored at once; the reader can then add a comment (up to 1,000 characters), which joins that vote. Read them with: Votes are lines of docs-feedback/feedback.jsonl in the data directory ($AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui). POST /api/docs/feedback takes same-origin requests only (plus --cors-origins, AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), checks the Host header, takes 4 KiB and 20 posts a minute per client, and stops at 20 MB. Nothing is readable over HTTP; the export is the CLI. Agents report through the docs MCP server's submit_feedback tool into the same store and limits (MCP server). A code flag is a -1 vote with kind: "code" and block, the block's index on the page, plus an optional comment. aiui serve and aiui dev say in the ui-config.json they serve where they keep votes (docsFeedback.url); a static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) serves the built file, which has no such entry, so with no endpoint the page sends no request at all and the question is shown only if issues is set. endpoint receives the vote as JSON, sent as text/plain when it is on another origin so the browser makes no preflight request: {"id", "path", "value", "kind", "block", "comment"}. A comment arrives as a second post with the same id. Every vote, wherever it goes, also fires a browser event your own script can send to analytics:

Off by default. Every docs page records how each of its requests went (aiui:docs-load records: retries, time-outs, failures, timings). Turn on telemetry and the page also sends the ones that went wrong, plus a sample of the good timings, home, so a reader's stalled page shows up without anyone watching that tab: Read what aiui serve stored with: What is sent: the requested file, its kind (doc or manifest), the attempt, the time it took, the outcome and reason, the HTTP status and the page path. Query strings and fragments are dropped. No user or session id and no user agent is sent, and the server stores no IP address or header. The page collects records while it is open and sends them in batches of up to 50 with navigator.sendBeacon when it is hidden or left, so nothing is sent while it loads. A post is JSON sent as text/plain (no preflight on another origin): {"v": 1, "records": [{"url", "kind", "attempt", "of", "ms", "outcome", "reason", "status", "page", "sampled"}]}. With telemetry: true only aiui serve and aiui dev receive records: they name /api/docs/telemetry in the ui-config.json they serve (docsTelemetry.url). A static host serves the built file, which has no such entry, so the page sends nothing and asks nothing. The endpoint takes same-origin requests (plus --cors-origins, AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), checks the Host header, takes 16 KiB and 30 posts a minute per client, and stops at 20 MB; on a site with sign-in it needs a signed-in reader. Records are lines of docs-telemetry/telemetry.jsonl in the data directory ($AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui). The pre-QA dashboard (tools/preqa) shows them when that file exists.

s.h: What the build publishes for assistants
s.x: File What it holds /llms.txt every page with its description, by nav group (llmstxt.org) /llms-full.txt every page's agent-ready Markdown in one file /docs/ .md one page's agent-ready Markdown (AI-ready docs) /docs/ .source.md the page source the site renders /search-index.json headings and text per page, for the site's own search /search-index/ the same index in parts, fetched as a query needs them (Search) /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt for search engines Each page's HTML also carries that page's source (a JSON script, id="aiui-initial-doc"), so the first visit renders without a second request for it. Pages over 200 KB of Markdown are fetched as before. It also carries docs-nav.json and route-manifest.json (id="aiui-boot-data", each up to 100 KB; not the navigation of a site with sign-in) and preloads ui-config.json; see Deploy to GitHub Pages → How pages load.

pages.d: Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.

s.x: Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.
Create aiui.yaml:
Create .github/workflows/deploy.yml:
Go to Settings → Pages in your GitHub repo Set Source to Deploy from a branch Set Branch to gh-pages / / (root) Push to main — your site deploys automatically

A repository other than .github.io is published at https:// .github.io/ /, under a path prefix. --base-path auto in the workflow above handles it: in GitHub Actions it reads the repository name, so every asset, page, link, search and Markdown URL starts with /, and the sitemap, llms.txt and canonical links use https:// .github.io/ as the site URL. Nothing else to configure, and no custom domain needed. auto builds for the root when the repository has a CNAME file, when the repository is .github.io, when seo.siteUrl is set (its path is the prefix), and outside GitHub Actions. To set the prefix yourself: The same works for any host that serves the site under a path, such as example.com/docs behind a reverse proxy (--base-path /docs). Write links in your Markdown as usual (/docs/guide, ../img/x.png): the build and the app add the prefix. Order of precedence: --base-path, then site.basePath, then the path of seo.siteUrl. --base-path / builds for the root. If you deploy with actions/configure-pages (Pages source "GitHub Actions"), you can pass its output instead, which also knows a custom domain set in the repository settings: --base-path "${{ steps.pages.outputs.base_path }}". Preview a prefixed build locally: aiui serve --base-path /my-repo serves it at http://127.0.0.1:8000/my-repo/ (and aiui serve --no-build serves an existing build under the prefix it was built for). Under a prefix, the legacy plugins that read the URL themselves (content-loader, homepage, topnav) are not supported; the default nav-intercept and fetch-retry are.

To use a custom domain (e.g., docs.example.com): Create a CNAME file in your repo root: Configure DNS — add a CNAME record pointing to .github.io The workflow above copies CNAME into the build output. The build also uses it as the site URL for the sitemap and canonical links.

MkDocs AIUI mkdocs.yml aiui.yaml mkdocs build → ./site/ aiui build --output site → ./site/ mkdocs serve aiui dev pip install mkdocs-material pip install aiui What carries over from Material for MkDocs pages: Admonitions (!!! note "Title", collapsible ???), content tabs (=== "Tab" with 4-space indented content) and fenced code blocks render. attr_list ({ .class }) is not supported and shows as literal text; :material-*: icon shortcodes do not render as icons; raw HTML blocks are not styled. Remove them. The nav: list in mkdocs.yml is not read. Pages are ordered by the frontmatter order value, then a number prefix in the file name (01-intro.md), then the file name. See Navigation.

Create aiui.yaml (see the example above) and run aiui validate --strict. Replace mkdocs build with aiui build --output site --minify in your CI workflow. Check the pages for the unsupported syntax listed above. Push to main.
See Hot Reload.

aiui build --output site produces: With a site URL (seo.siteUrl, or the CNAME file) the build also writes sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt; see SEO. Everything is static, so GitHub Pages serves it directly.

Opening a page from the sidebar fetches its .md file. A reader on a lossy network (Wi-Fi, VPN, a mobile link) sometimes gets one new connection that hangs for 15 to 30 seconds while every other request is fast. The docs app keeps one such request from freezing the page: Time limit and retry. Each request for a page has 3 seconds to get an answer from the server. Past that it is cancelled and a fresh request goes out, which opens a new connection. There are three attempts (3 s, 5 s, then 8 s for a link that is only slow), with a short random pause between them. A network error or a 5xx answer is retried the same way; a 404 is not. From the second attempt the loading skeleton says "Taking longer than usual. Trying again (2 of 3)", so a slow page is never a silent skeleton. Stalled downloads. Once the answer starts, a page whose download sends nothing for 4 seconds has stalled and is requested again; one that keeps arriving, however slowly, gets up to 15 seconds. No queueing behind another tab. A browser lets one request per URL at a time fill its HTTP cache entry; a second request for the same file (from another tab, say) waits inside the browser until the first one is answered. Page Markdown, and every retry, is requested with cache: 'no-store', so a stuck request elsewhere can never hold this page. The CDN still caches, and the app keeps pages it has loaded in memory. aiui:docs-load records. Every attempt's outcome is pushed to window.__aiuiDocsLoad (newest 200), sent as a window event aiui:docs-load and logged to the console (console.warn for retries and failures). A record is {v: 1, type: 'aiui:docs-load', url, kind: 'doc' | 'manifest', attempt, of, ms, outcome, reason?, status?, detail?, at}, where outcome is ok, retry, failed, inline, inline-mismatch or duplicate, and reason is headers-timeout, body-idle, body-timeout, network-error, http-5xx or network-change. A dead connection. Every tab of a browser profile shares one HTTP/2 connection per site. When it dies silently (the laptop slept, the Wi-Fi changed), requests on it wait until the browser notices, and only the browser decides when (its own ping and idle timeouts); a page cannot close it or pick another. What a page can do, it does: each attempt is cancelled at its time limit and a fresh request goes out, and when the browser comes back online or the tab becomes visible again while a request has waited half a second or more, that attempt ends at once (network-change) and a new request goes out on the browser's fresh connection, since browsers drop their pooled connections when the network changes. The last attempt is never cut short. Prefetch. Resting the pointer on a sidebar, previous / next or in-article docs link for 80 ms, focusing it with the keyboard, or pressing it starts loading that page. Once a page has shown, its previous and next pages load while the browser is idle. Other spellings of a page URL. A page's file URL (/docs/x.html, /docs/x/index.html) and a URL in the wrong letter case (/docs/API/sessions, which a static host answers with 404.html) show the page and then move the address bar to the page's own URL (history.replaceState, so Back does not return to the old spelling). The docs home page's own URL is the site root: its sidebar link goes to /, never /docs/index. A wrong-case URL has no redirect file, because the spellings of a path are unbounded; when two pages differ only by case, such a URL shows "not found" rather than a guess. Nothing optional delays load. The page's load event waits for every request in flight. The previous / next prefetch, hover and focus prefetch, the GitHub star count and the opt-in telemetry chunk start only after load, when the browser is idle (src/frontend/src/docs/afterLoad.ts); a press on a link still loads its page at once. In-memory cache. A page loaded or prefetched once shows at once when you come back to it, without a request, until the tab is reloaded. The last click wins. Clicking another link cancels the request for the page you left, so fast clicking never builds a queue. No long wait for the renderer. A fetched page waits at most one second for the code highlighter and math renderer; after that the text shows and upgrades when they arrive. Retry state. When every attempt fails, the page says "Couldn't load this page" with a Retry button instead of a loading skeleton. First load. Every page aiui build writes carries the navigation (docs-nav.json), the route manifest and the page's own Markdown, so a first visit or a reload asks for none of them (aiui build --strict fails if a page's inlined Markdown is keyed by another URL than the app requests); ui-config.json is preloaded with the page (a live aiui serve adds Ask AI, MCP and feedback to it, so it is not baked in). The loader's tag names the plugins, so plugins/plugins.json is not requested either: on this site a first docs page went from five JSON requests and three plugin scripts to one and two. A file the page does not carry (a navigation over 100 KB, the navigation of a site with sign-in, a page served without its content) loads with the same time limit and retries as a page. If it cannot load, the page says "Couldn't load the docs" with a Retry button instead of staying blank. This site, https://ui.praison.ai, is built the same way: see .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml. It deploys only when the built site changed: every deploy replaces the branch and empties the CDN cache, so a merge that does not change the site (tests, CI, Python code the docs do not show) publishes nothing. src/frontend/scripts/site-hash.mjs hashes the fresh build (every path and its bytes; a sitemap's dates are left out because they are file times, the checkout time in CI) and writes aiui-site-hash.txt into it. The workflow compares that with the file the last deploy published and skips the deploy when they match. Run the workflow by hand with force to deploy anyway.

The docs app renders code (Shiki), mermaid diagrams, MkDocs tabs and admonitions, "On this page" and the header tabs itself. By default a build loads only one of the vanilla plugins in plugins/: Plugin Why it loads nav-intercept Keeps in-article /docs links on in-app navigation (no full page load) fetch-retry (retry a failed request for the site manifests) is no longer in the default list: the app reads the navigation and route manifest from the page and fetches ui-config.json with its own time limit and retries, which fetch-retry leaves alone. List it under site.plugins to keep it. mermaid, syntax-highlight, code-copy, toc, mkdocs-compat, content-loader, homepage and topnav no longer load by default: they skip React docs pages, and mermaid and syntax-highlight fetched about 40 files from cdn.jsdelivr.net and cdnjs.cloudflare.com on every page (each new origin is another connection that can stall). A site can still list any of them under site.plugins in aiui.yaml. index.html loads plugins/plugin-loader.js?v=, where the version is a hash of the plugin files in the build (also in plugins/plugins.json), and names the plugins on the same tag (data-plugins), so the loader does not fetch plugins.json (a server's pages, which lack it, still do). The loader imports every plugin with the same ?v=, so browsers and the CDN cache them until a build changes a plugin.

pages.d: Build streaming AI agent interfaces in minutes with Python decorators or zero-code YAML.

s.x: PraisonAIUI gives any AI model or agent a polished, responsive agent interface without writing frontend code. Every app ships with streaming Markdown, tool calls, reasoning steps, approvals, code blocks, conversation history, light and dark themes, and mobile support out of the box.

s.h: Two ways to build an agent app
s.x: Pick whichever matches how you work — you can switch or combine them at any time. Use simple decorators in app.py to hook into any model, SDK, or custom logic: Run it with aiui run app.py. Define an AI assistant without writing Python (pip install "aiui[praisonai]" and set OPENAI_API_KEY): Run it with aiui run chat.yaml.

s.h: What Agent UI includes out of the box
s.x: Capability What your users see Learn more Lifecycle hooks Greeting on open, per-chat setup, live Stop button, clean-up on exit Chat lifecycle Streaming & prompts Token-by-token replies, interactive questions, action buttons and toasts Messages & streaming Starters & profiles One-click starter cards on empty chats and selectable assistant personas Starters & profiles Reasoning & tool steps Collapsible, timed tree of tool calls, searches and sub-runs Steps Artifacts canvas Side-by-side preview for generated code, tables, diagrams and files A2UI canvas Attachments & media Drag-and-drop uploads, inline images, audio, video and downloadable files Attachments Voice & MCP tools Spoken replies, real-time voice input and external MCP tool servers MCP servers

s.h: Learn the core concepts in order
s.x: Understand when welcome, start, reply, stop and end handlers run. Send replies, stream tokens, ask follow-up questions and show action buttons. Guide new users with clickable prompt cards and switchable assistant modes. Show live, collapsible tool calls and thinking steps inside every reply.

pages.d: Understand every moment in a chat session — from the opening greeting to streaming replies, stopping and clean-up.

s.x: Every conversation follows a predictable sequence of events. You only need to write @aiui.reply to start; add the other decorators whenever you want custom greetings, per-chat setup, or clean-up.

Every decorator works with both async def and plain def. Decorator Alias When it runs Typical use @aiui.welcome — Once when an empty chat loads Show a friendly greeting above starter cards @aiui.on_chat_start — Once per chat, right before its first reply Initialize per-chat memory, DB client, or agent @aiui.reply @aiui.on_message Every time the user sends a message Call your model, stream tokens, run tools @aiui.cancel @aiui.on_stop When the user clicks Stop mid-reply Log cancellation or clean up an external job @aiui.goodbye @aiui.on_chat_end When the chat's last browser tab closes Close database connections or temporary files Annotate your @aiui.reply parameter as str (async def on_message(text: str)) to receive plain text. Omit the annotation (or type it as MessageContext) when you also need message.session_id, message.agent_name, or message.attachments.
Save this as app.py and run aiui run app.py:

Stopping a reply: Pressing Stop cancels the running @aiui.reply task (asyncio.CancelledError at the next await), immediately halting slow model calls or tool loops. Exceptions: If @aiui.reply raises an error, the UI displays the error cleanly beneath anything already streamed and preserves it on reload. Per-chat isolation: aiui.user_session is scoped to the current chat session, so two users talking at the same time never overwrite each other's state. See Handler context.
Stream tokens, ask interactive follow-up questions and add clickable buttons. Save conversations to disk or SQL so users can resume later.

pages.d: Send complete replies, stream tokens live, ask the user follow-up questions, attach media and trigger clickable buttons.

s.x: Inside @aiui.reply (or @aiui.on_chat_start), PraisonAIUI gives you simple async functions to communicate with the user.

Use aiui.say() when you already have the full reply, or aiui.stream_token() to display tokens live as your AI model generates them. Markdown — headings, tables, links, math, and syntax-highlighted code blocks — renders automatically as tokens arrive.
Pause the agent to ask the user for clarification or confirmation using aiui.prompt(). It waits for the user's answer and returns a result object (answer.text or answer.choice).
Show buttons below a message with aiui.action_buttons() and handle clicks with @aiui.button(" "):

Render any of PraisonAIUI's 81 UI blocks — metrics, searchable tables, pandas/Polars DataFrames, Plotly figures, charts, spreadsheets, whiteboards, cards, or aiui.layout([...]) — directly inside a chat reply with await aiui.send_block(...):

Helper Purpose Example await aiui.send_block(block) Render any UI block, DataFrame, or Plotly figure inline await aiui.send_block(aiui.table(df, searchable=True)) await aiui.image(url, alt="") Display an inline image await aiui.image("/static/chart.png", "Sales chart") await aiui.audio(url) Embed an audio player await aiui.audio("/static/briefing.mp3") await aiui.video(url) Embed a video player await aiui.video("/static/demo.mp4") await aiui.file(url, name="") Attach a downloadable file await aiui.file("/static/report.pdf", "report.pdf") await aiui.notify(msg, type="info") Show a toast (pass persist=True to also save in the header bell) await aiui.notify("Saved!", type="success", persist=True) await aiui.error(msg, details=...) Show a formatted error card await aiui.error("Request failed", details=str(exc)) Want rich cards, tables, or side-by-side previews inside chat? See Message elements and A2UI canvas.
Give new visitors one-click prompts and switchable assistant modes. Wrap tool calls and searches in collapsible, timed steps.

pages.d: Help users start fast with clickable prompt suggestions, switchable assistant personas and friendly display names.

s.x: A blank chat box can feel intimidating. Starters show users what your assistant can do on the very first click, while profiles let them pick a specialized mode (such as General, Code, or Writer).
Return a list of {label, message} items from @aiui.starters. They appear as cards on every empty conversation.
Use @aiui.profiles to offer multiple personas or models in the UI. Inside @aiui.reply, inspect message.agent_name to route to the chosen profile.
When internal agent IDs look technical (like support_triage_v2), map them to friendly display names with @aiui.author_rename:
Turn on thumbs-up / thumbs-down buttons and log ratings with @aiui.on("feedback"):
Show live progress when your assistant calls tools or searches data. Add custom dashboard pages, layouts and notifications around your chat.

pages.d: A step is a named piece of work inside a reply: a tool call, an LLM call, a

s.x: A step is a named piece of work inside a reply: a tool call, an LLM call, a retrieval, a sub-run. The chat shows the reply's steps as a collapsible tree with each step's name, status (running, done, failed, stopped) and duration; opening a step shows its input, output and child steps. Steps are saved with the reply, so a reload shows the same tree with the same durations. @aiui.step works bare, with () or with arguments (@aiui.step("Search the web", type="tool")), on sync and async functions. The step is named after the function unless named; its input is the call's arguments (self/cls left out), its output the return value, and an exception marks it failed (and is raised as usual). aiui.Step is used as async with or with (sync code and worker threads too); in sync code step.stream_token(t) sends without await. Nesting is automatic: a step opened while another runs becomes its child, across awaits, in tasks started from it (asyncio.gather, create_task) and in aiui.make_async threads. parent= sets the parent explicitly.

aiui.Step(name, type="reasoning", parent=None, metadata={}, input=None, output=None) Field Meaning type run, tool, llm, embedding, retrieval, rerank, undefined, tool_call, reasoning, sub_agent, custom input, output Shown when the step is opened; data as JSON, text as is, each at most 1 MB metadata Extra data sent with the step's start and end id, start, end, duration, status, error Read-only: epoch ms, seconds, running/done/error/stopped, the exception text @aiui.step(name=None, type="reasoning", **metadata) wraps each call in a Step. Events (WebSocket and /run SSE, protocol 1.2), each with step_id: step_start (name, step_type, parent_id, start in epoch ms, input), step_update (token to append) and step_end (end, status, duration in seconds, error, and input/output when changed). The saved reply keeps steps: [{step_id, parent_id, name, step_type, status, start, end, input, output, error}]. A step outside a reply sends nothing but still times itself. await aiui.think("...") still shows unnamed reasoning text.

pages.d: Inside an @aiui.reply (or @aiui.on_message) handler you can ask who is calling, keep state for

s.x: Inside an @aiui.reply (or @aiui.on_message) handler you can ask who is calling, keep state for this chat, read the chat's history in the shape an LLM wants, pop a notice, and call the UI from blocking worker code. Nothing to configure. Each API resolves to the chat being answered (two people chatting at once never see each other's data), also in tasks the handler starts and aiui.make_async threads.

Attribute Value id The chat (session) id. user The signed-in user as a dict (id, username, extra fields; never the password hash), or None. aiui.current_user() returns the same dict. client_type "webapp" (a browser), "api" (a script or HTTP client), "copilot", or the bot platform ("slack", "discord", "teams", …). chat_profile The profile chosen for this chat, or the server-wide selection. chat_settings Settings sent with the chat (dict). env Per-chat values sent by the client (dict of strings). language The best tag of the caller's Accept-Language ("fr-CA"), or None. headers Request headers, lower-cased, with credentials removed (Authorization, Cookie, and any header whose name mentions a token, key, secret, password, auth or session). It is None outside a handler. A client names itself with ?client= on the chat WebSocket or an X-Aiui-Client: header (letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters). A chat turn ({type: "chat", ...} on /api/chat/ws, or the body of POST /api/chat/send) may carry chat_profile, chat_settings and env; they stay with the chat for its later turns.

A key/value store private to the current chat, kept across its turns. Preset keys: id, user, chat_profile, chat_settings, env. Values live in memory (the last 5,000 chats), so keep what must survive a restart in your own database. Outside a handler get returns the default and set raises.

The chat's messages, oldest first, including the one being answered; each finished reply is added. After a restart the saved history is reloaded from the datastore. At most 200 messages are kept. Method Does get() A copy of the messages: [{"role", "content"}, ...]. add(content, role="assistant") Append a message (a string with a role, or a {"role", "content"} dict). Roles: system, user, assistant, tool. remove(message) Remove the latest message equal to message; returns True if one was removed. clear() Forget the history (for example on a "new topic" command). to_openai(system=None, max_messages=None) OpenAI chat messages, with an optional system prompt first and only the last max_messages. Works with any OpenAI-compatible client.

Run blocking work in a thread so the chat stays responsive, and call the UI from inside it: make_async(fn, executor=None) runs fn on a thread pool (yours, if given) with the handler's context. From that thread, run_sync(coro, timeout=None) runs the coroutine on the server's loop and waits; in a plain script it starts its own loop; in async code it raises RuntimeError (use await).

@aiui.on_chat_start runs once per chat before its first reply, as that chat, so it is the place to fill aiui.user_session; @aiui.on_chat_end runs as the chat when its last connection closes. See Chat lifecycle.

Load a model, an index or a client once and share it across every chat (@aiui.cache(ttl=3600, maxsize=8) takes options; async def works too): Option Does ttl=None Seconds an entry is kept; None keeps it until cleared. maxsize=None Keep only the most recently used entries; None for no limit. fn.cache_clear() Forget every entry. Entries are keyed by the arguments (unhashable ones, like a list, by their repr) and live in the server's memory. It is thread-safe; concurrent first calls share one computation (a caller cancelled by Stop does not cancel it). Exceptions are never cached, so the next call tries again.

type is info, success, warning or error; duration is in milliseconds. The notice is never saved with the reply or added to aiui.chat_context. Clients receive {type: "toast", session_id, run_id, message, variant, duration?} on the chat WebSocket; both built-in chats show it as a toast. Returns False outside a handler. (aiui.toast(...) builds a toast component for a page.)

pages.d: A message can carry elements: images, PDFs, videos, audio, files and code

s.x: A message can carry elements: images, PDFs, videos, audio, files and code blocks shown with the message text. Each element is a dict with a type, the fields below, and an optional name and display.

These reach the chat as message_element events: aiui.audio(url) and aiui.video(url) work the same way. msg.add_image(), add_pdf(), add_video(), add_audio(), add_file() and add_code() validate their arguments and append typed elements (ImageElement and the others in praisonaiui.schema.models); they reach the chat like dicts. So does any object with model_dump() or to_dict().

Each aiui.Message(...).send() and each aiui.say(...) is its own message: the chat shows it at once, as its own block under the same answer, with its author when it is not the agent, and its elements and actions under it. A reload shows the same blocks. Copy, feedback and Regenerate act on the whole answer. The saved reply keeps content (the messages joined by a blank line) and segments ([{id, text, author?}]); elements carry the message_id of their message. msg.update() and msg.remove() change only that message while the reply runs. On the wire every piece of reply text names its message: run_content carries message_id with a token (appended) or a whole content (sets that message's text), plus author when set. message_element and message_actions carry the same message_id; message_update, message_remove and action_remove edit a message already shown. The sections below list each element's fields.

Display images with thumbnail and click-to-zoom functionality. Properties: url (required): Image URL name (optional): Display name alt (optional): Alt text for accessibility display (optional): Display mode - "inline" (default), "side", "page" width (optional): Fixed width in pixels height (optional): Fixed height in pixels

Display PDF documents with inline viewer or link to open in new tab. Properties: url (required): PDF URL name (optional): Display name display (optional): "inline": Embedded PDF viewer (600px height) "side": Smaller embedded viewer (400px height) "page": Link to open in new tab

Display videos with native HTML5 video player. Properties: url (required): Video URL name (optional): Display name controls (optional): Show video controls (default: True) autoplay (optional): Auto-play video (default: False) loop (optional): Loop video (default: False)

Display audio with native HTML5 audio player. Properties: url (required): Audio URL name (optional): Display name controls (optional): Show audio controls (default: True) autoplay (optional): Auto-play audio (default: False) loop (optional): Loop audio (default: False)

Display downloadable files with file type icons and size information. Properties: url (required): File download URL name (optional): Display name size (optional): File size in bytes mime_type (optional): MIME type for file type detection

Display syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy functionality. Properties: content (required): Code content language (optional): Programming language for syntax highlighting name (optional): Display name

pages.d: Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are

s.x: Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are read into the agent's prompt, images go to the model as multimodal input. The default limit is 10 MB per file.
The agent receives the extracted PDF text before the user message. The reply streams to WebSocket clients (see Gateway Chat).

Content type Processing What the agent sees application/pdf Text extracted with pypdf (a dependency of aiui) --- Attached PDF: name --- block before the message image/* File path passed to the agent's attachments The image, for vision-capable models Anything else allowed File read as text --- Attached File: name --- block before the message

POST /api/chat/attachments accepts three encodings so uploads work out of the box even without python-multipart: Raw binary body with X-Filename header and file Content-Type (what aiui.file_upload() sends). JSON body ({"filename", "content_type", "data_base64", "session_id?"}). multipart/form-data with a file field (when python-multipart is installed; returns HTTP 415 otherwise). Category MIME types Text & Markup text/plain, text/csv, text/tab-separated-values, text/markdown (text/x-markdown normalized), application/xml, text/xml Data & Office application/json, application/pdf, .xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), .docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document) Images image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp Audio audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/webm, audio/ogg, audio/mp4 Common OS MIME quirks (such as Windows sending application/vnd.ms-excel for .csv, or application/octet-stream for known safe data/media extensions) are normalized safely. Active web types (text/html, image/svg+xml, application/javascript) are always rejected with 400 {"error": "Type not allowed: ..."}. Files over the size limit return 413 / 400. Files are stored under /praisonai_attachments/ with sanitized UUID filenames, automatic TTL eviction (default 3600 seconds) and capacity eviction (default 500 entries). Internal filesystem path values are never returned in HTTP responses — resolve them server-side with aiui.get_uploaded_file().

On @aiui.page and aiui.interface() forms, use aiui.file_upload() to render a drag-and-drop uploader and resolve the uploaded handle safely in Python: Inside a manual @aiui.register_page_action handler, always resolve client handles via meta = aiui.get_uploaded_file(data.get("doc")) — it validates UUID syntax and looks up the file in the server's registry, blocking path traversal and expired/forged handles.
Add -F "index_to_knowledge=true" to the upload to also store the file in the knowledge base. The response then carries knowledge_indexed (and knowledge_error when it failed).

AttachmentManager(storage_dir=None, max_size_mb=10, allowed_types=None) takes the limits. The server creates its default instance with praisonaiui.features.attachments.get_attachment_manager(); there is no public setter for a custom one yet.

Layer Module Backend-agnostic? Detection media_utils.py Yes — normalises OpenAI, URL, b64, element dicts Protocol provider.py — RunEventType.MESSAGE_ELEMENT Yes Adapter providers/__init__.py — PraisonAI bridge only No — maps SDK/callback queue → protocol Transport chat.py — broadcast + persist Yes Storage attachments.py — GET /api/chat/media/{id} Yes — reuses attachment store for b64 UI chat.js, ElementRenderer Yes — renders {type, url, alt} Detection and UI do not import PraisonAI. s.x: The Chat page of the dashboard style (and of the app shell, which hosts the same view): real-time agent chat over a WebSocket, with markdown rendering, tool call cards and session history. The browser side is the vanilla chat.js view; the server side is the chat feature (praisonaiui.features.chat). The chat in the app shell, dark: an agent thought for two seconds, ran python3 --version, answered and now waits for approval to install numpy; the table and script it made sit under the answer
Without a @aiui.reply callback the chat runs the configured agents through the PraisonAI provider (pip install "aiui[praisonai]").
A chat message travels through 5 layers before reaching the browser:

File Layer Responsibility src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js Frontend WS connection, DOM rendering, session history src/praisonaiui/features/chat.py Backend ChatManager, _run_and_broadcast, history API src/praisonaiui/server.py Backend SSE streaming path (run_agent endpoint) src/praisonaiui/providers/__init__.py Provider SDK → RunEvent bridge, _run_direct_mode src/praisonaiui/datastore.py Storage MemoryDataStore / JSONFileDataStore src/praisonaiui/provider.py Protocol RunEventType enum definition

Agents created via YAML config, CRUD API, jobs, or channel bots automatically get tools resolved through the ToolResolver. Tool names in config are resolved to callable Python functions from 4 sources: Local tools.py file (backward compatibility) praisonaiagents.tools.TOOL_MAPPINGS (built-in tools) praisonai_tools package (community tools) Tool registry (programmatically registered tools)
Agents created via POST /api/agents also support tools:

Component Tool Resolution Gateway _create_agents_from_config() ✅ ToolResolver Integration create_gateway_from_yaml() ✅ ToolResolver Provider _get_or_create_agent() ✅ Default tools Channel bot _start_channel_bot() ✅ Default tools Jobs _execute_job() fallback ✅ ToolResolver CRUD agents _run() fallback ✅ ToolResolver CRUD agents _sync_to_gateway() ✅ ToolResolver

Assistant messages are rendered with full markdown support: Bold, italic, strikethrough Inline code and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting Ordered and unordered lists Links (auto-detected and rendered safely)

A tool call row (execute_command, Done in 0.3 s) above the answer, then an approval card for pip install numpy with Approve and Deny When agents use tools, each call is displayed as a collapsible card: Tool name and status indicator (running/completed/failed) Input arguments (JSON) Output results (rendered in code blocks) #### Tool Call Lifecycle Tool calls go through 4 stages: emit → enrich → dedup → persist. 1. Emit — The SDK fires TOOL_CALL_START / DELTA_TOOL_CALL / TOOL_CALL_END events via StreamEventEmitter. The provider maps these to RunEvent types (TOOL_CALL_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED). 2. Enrich — _run_and_broadcast() in chat.py enriches each tool call event with display-friendly fields via _enrich_tool_payload(): Field Source Example icon Mapped from tool name 🔍, 📝, 💾 description Generated from name + args "🔍 Searching for 'Django latest version'" step_number Auto-incrementing counter per run 1, 2, 3 formatted_result Truncated result string "✓ Done" tool_call_id SDK-assigned or UUID fallback "call_abc123" 3. Dedup — Both DELTA_TOOL_CALL (stream) and hook callbacks fire for the same tool call. The handler uses _seen_tool_started / _seen_tool_completed sets keyed by tool_call_id and name to suppress duplicates. A re-broadcast with has_complete_args=True is allowed to update the description with keyword-rich text. 4. Persist — After the run completes, all enriched tool calls are merged by tool_call_id into collected_tool_calls and saved alongside the assistant message: #### Reloading during a reply The React chat asks for run_attach when it opens a session. A run whose tab was reloaded comes back as the tab's own turn: the reply so far (the server keeps each live run's events, consecutive tokens merged, up to 2,000 events), the Stop button, and the composer waiting until the run ends. A run that another open tab started shows read-only, also with the reply so far; both tabs can keep sending. #### Turn order A reply is saved when its run ends, so two runs in one session (a second tab, or a question sent after a reload while the first reply is still running) finish out of order. A user message carries a turn_id and its reply a reply_to with the same value; GET /api/chat/history/{id} lists each reply right after its own question. History saved before these fields existed is shown in the order it was saved. #### Tool Call Persistence Schema Tool calls are persisted alongside assistant messages in the datastore. When a session is reloaded from history, tool call steps are reconstructed from the toolCalls array on each assistant message. Assistant message schema in the datastore: #### History Reload Rendering
New Session: Click "New Chat" to create a fresh session Session History: Switch between sessions in the sidebar Message History: Full conversation history per session via REST API

Click the Stop button (or send chat_abort with the run_id over the WebSocket) to cancel a run Only the connection that started a run may stop it or answer its prompts (or any client, once that connection is gone) The partial response is preserved in history
Upload files to include with your chat messages — see Attachments for details.

Chat history is stored through the BaseDataStore interface: by default the praisonaiagents session store, or JSON files, memory or SQL with aiui run --datastore. See Session Management. Each stored session holds its messages, with toolCalls on assistant messages:

The content field on assistant messages stores the SDK's final response from agent.chat() — the same text displayed by finalizeDelta() in the live view. This ensures the reloaded view matches what the user saw during streaming. During streaming, text tokens are accumulated in full_response. When RUN_COMPLETED arrives with event.content (the SDK's authoritative return value), it replaces the accumulated tokens for storage. This prevents intermediate narrative text from being duplicated on reload.
On a server with auth on, the browser first exchanges its key for a single-use ticket (POST /api/auth/ws-ticket) and connects with ?ticket=; see Deployment.
A frame that is not a JSON object is answered with {"type": "protocol_error", "error": ...}; the connection stays open.
All events include session_id and run_id.

Response includes toolCalls on assistant messages:

During streaming, all text tokens go into a single currentDeltaEl DOM element — even across tool call boundaries. Tool call cards are sibling elements inserted alongside the text element. When run_completed arrives, finalizeDelta(content) replaces the accumulated text with the SDK's final response.

pages.d: Require explicit human approval before agents run sensitive tools, with inline chat cards, a dedicated Approvals queue and SSE updates.

s.x: When an agent is about to execute a sensitive tool (shell commands, deployments, payments, file deletions), PraisonAIUI pauses the run and asks a human to Approve or Deny — inline inside the chat thread and in the built-in Approvals page (builtin.approvals).

The agent runtime or backend submits an approval request (POST /api/approvals). Connected browsers receive it live over SSE (GET /api/approvals/stream) and show an inline approval card in chat plus an entry on the Approvals page. Pair with aiui.push_notification(..., action={"label": "Review now", "page": "approvals"}) so operators also get an immediate toast + unread badge in the header Notification Bell on the same dashboard. A reviewer clicks Approve (POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve) or Deny (POST /api/approvals/{id}/deny), optionally updating reusable policy rules (PUT /api/approvals/policies). The agent resumes or aborts cleanly, and the decision is recorded in GET /api/approvals/history.

Each spawn is a record of parent agent, child agent and session in the server's SubagentManager: When praisonaiagents is installed, the manager subscribes to its handoff hook, so every agent handoff is recorded (parent, child and session id come from the hook payload; missing values become parent, child and default). pages.d: 1. Code is submitted with a target language. A language outside the allowlist (default: python, javascript, bash) is a 400; so is any language other than Python

s.x: Sandboxed code execution with language allowlists, behind a human approval. Runs Python through the SDK's execute_code (praisonaiagents.tools.python_tools), which carries @require_approval(risk_level="critical"). Every run waits until someone approves it in the Approvals page.

Code is submitted with a target language. A language outside the allowlist (default: python, javascript, bash) is a 400; so is any language other than Python, because the SDK sandbox runs Python only. Without praisonaiagents the response is 503 with status: "degraded". Nothing runs, and nothing is simulated. Otherwise the request goes through the SDK's own approval gate on execute_code, wired to the aiui approvals queue. A pending execute_code entry (risk critical, arguments = the exact code) appears in GET /api/approvals/pending, and the HTTP request waits for the decision without blocking the server. Approve runs the code and returns 200. Deny, or no answer within the SDK registry timeout (300 s by default), returns 403 with status: "denied". One run needs one approval. Only the entry the server created for that run counts: an entry created with POST /api/approvals does not unlock a run, and approving a run with always: true approves that run only (critical tools never get a standing approval). To skip the human step on a trusted machine, opt out explicitly: add execute_code to the auto_approve_tools policy (PUT /api/approvals/policies; remove it to turn the gate back on) or set PRAISONAI_AUTO_APPROVE=true for the server process. Authentication is the server's job (AUTH_ENFORCE, require_auth, AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN): without credentials, the run and the approve/deny endpoints return 401.
Endpoint Method Description /api/code/languages GET List supported languages /api/code/execute POST Execute code in sandbox
Skills — Code execution tools in the skill catalog

s.x: The model fallback feature (praisonaiui.features.model_fallback) lists the available models and stores an ordered fallback chain that the UI can show and edit. The chain is stored, not applied Nothing in PraisonAIUI reads the chain when it sends a request: the provider still calls the agent's own model, and a failed call is not retried on the next model. The chain is also kept in memory only, so a restart clears it. Use it as a setting your own provider or @aiui.reply callback reads (see below).
The model list comes from litellm.model_list when LiteLLM is installed and has models configured. Otherwise it is a short static list: gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-5-sonnet and gemini-2.0-flash.
Use the server's shared manager, not a new ModelFallbackManager(), so you see what the API set:
Endpoint Method Description /api/models GET Available models and the current fallback chain /api/models/fallback PUT Set the chain ({"models": [...]}; 400 if not a list)
Providers: LLM provider configuration

pages.d: Give your agents the tools of any Model Context Protocol server, declared in YAML, over Streamable HTTP, SSE or stdio, with secrets kept on the server

s.x: The MCP page (builtin.mcp) connects the app to Model Context Protocol servers so agents can use their tools. Declare servers once in the config; they connect when the app starts. Users can add more from the page only where you allow it. Install the client once: pip install "aiui[mcp]".

Put the block in the config the app starts with (aiui run app.py --config aiui.yaml) or in the data-dirconfig.yaml(AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui). aiui validate checks it. Each server has a url or a command, not both: Key Meaning url Remote server (Streamable HTTP or SSE) command, args Local server started as a subprocess (stdio) env stdio: extra environment variables for the subprocess headers Remote: HTTP headers, for example Authorization transport streamable-http, sse or stdio (type works too). Usually not needed, see below ${NAME} in url, args, env and headers reads the environment variable NAME, so tokens stay out of the file. A list with a name per server (servers: [{name: github, url: ...}]) works too; names must be unique. The servers connect in the background at startup, all at once, so a slow server never delays the app. One that fails shows its error on the page, with a Connect button to try again. They disconnect when the app stops.

Server What the app uses command stdio url Streamable HTTP; if the server does not answer it, SSE url whose path ends in /sse SSE transport: sse or transport: streamable-http Exactly that one, no fallback

By default users can reconnect the declared servers but add nothing new. Open it up with allow: allow.urls entry Admits mcp.example.com That host on its default port, http or https *.example.com Any subdomain of example.com https://h.example.com/mcp/ That scheme and host, paths under /mcp/ https://h.example.com:8443 That port * Any public host A wildcard (*, *.example.com) never reaches a private, loopback or link-local address, so users cannot reach your internal network or a cloud metadata endpoint through the app. To allow an internal server, name its host: http://localhost:9000. allow.commands lists the executables users may start, matched exactly: npx does not admit /tmp/npx. A user-added stdio server cannot set env. Allowing npx or uvx lets users run any package they name, so list them only for people you trust; * admits any command (the older PRAISONAIUI_ALLOW_REMOTE_MCP_STDIO=true does the same). A user cannot reuse a declared server's name for another target.
mcp: {enabled: false}: nothing connects at startup and the page cannot add servers. To remove the page and its routes: extensions: {disabled: [builtin.mcp]}.

GET /api/mcp/servers and the connect response show header and env names with *** values, drop user and password from URLs, and mask query values (?api_key=***). Header and env values, every ${NAME} value, and any Bearer token are redacted from the app's logs, tracebacks included.

Every route needs the same credentials as the rest of the API in each auth mode. Route Does GET /api/mcp/servers Servers with status, transport, tools, last_error, source (config or user) and masked connection_data; plus enabled and allow POST /api/mcp/connect {name} connects a declared server. {name, url, headers?, transport?} or {name, command, args?} adds one that allow admits (403 otherwise, 409 for a declared name) POST /api/mcp/disconnect/{name} Disconnects a server From Python, aiui.on_mcp_connect and aiui.on_mcp_disconnect run when a server's state changes. App code may call praisonaiui.features.mcp.connect_mcp_server({...}) directly; the allow lists apply to users, not to your code.

pages.d: Talk instead of typing. When an app turns on voice input, the chat composer

s.x: Talk instead of typing. When an app turns on voice input, the chat composer gets a microphone button. Press it, speak, and press it again: the recording is turned into text and put in the message box, after anything already typed, for you to read over and send. Voice input belongs to the realtime feature (builtin.realtime). It is off unless the app asks for it, so no other chat shows a microphone.

Give aiui a realtime manager that can transcribe speech. The bundled OpenAIRealtimeManager uses OpenAI speech to text (OPENAI_API_KEY, and OPENAI_BASE_URL for a compatible server): aiui.OpenAIRealtimeManager is the same class. There is no praisonaiui.realtime module: import it from praisonaiui or praisonaiui.features.realtime. Your own backend works too. Subclass RealtimeProtocol and implement transcribe: A manager without transcribe keeps the microphone hidden. aiui.set_realtime_manager(None) turns voice input off again.

State What you see At rest A microphone icon button before Send ("Record a voice message") Recording A red stop button and a running time; screen readers hear "Recording". Press the button again to stop and transcribe, or Escape to discard Transcribing A spinner in the button Done The text in the message box, with the caret at its end The browser asks for the microphone the first time. If access is blocked, a message says how to allow it in the browser's site settings; no microphone, or one busy in another app, gets its own message. A recording stops by itself after two minutes. The button is keyboard accessible (Tab to it, Enter or Space to start and stop, Escape to discard) and has a visible focus ring. Its code is a separate chunk that loads only for an app with voice input on.

Endpoint Method Description /api/realtime/voice GET {"enabled": bool, "max_seconds": 120, "max_bytes": 8388608}: whether the composer shows the microphone /api/realtime/transcribe POST The recording as the raw body (Content-Type: audio/*). Returns {"text": "..."} /api/realtime/transcribe answers 404 while voice input is off, 415 for a body that is not audio, 400 for an empty one, 413 over 8 MiB, 501 when the manager cannot transcribe, and 502 when the speech service fails (its message is logged by type only, never returned). Both routes need the same credentials as every other /api route.
The reply is text. Speaking it aloud (see TTS) and a hands-free, speech-to-speech session are not part of this feature.

pages.d: PraisonAIUI uses a provider protocol — a simple abstraction that lets you plug in any AI backend.

s.x: PraisonAIUI uses a provider protocol — a simple abstraction that lets you plug in any AI backend.

The provider protocol is the only contract between the frontend and any AI backend. All dashboard pages (/api/overview, /api/config, /api/logs, etc.) are provider-agnostic — they always work regardless of which backend is active. The provider only handles agent execution (run()), agent listing (list_agents()), and health checks (health()).

The user sends a message: a chat frame on the WebSocket /api/chat/ws (the default for the chat page and the app shell), or POST /run (SSE) The server calls provider.run(message) on the active provider The provider yields RunEvent objects (start, content, tool calls, reasoning, completion) The server sends each event as an SSE data: frame (RunEvent.to_dict()) or as a WebSocket message, and stores the finished turn in the datastore. The WebSocket adapter forwards only selected fields per event type (for example, reasoning events carry step but not action, confidence or next_action), so only SSE clients receive every serialized field The frontend renders the events as they arrive

PraisonAIProvider is the default. When the app registers a @aiui.reply callback, it runs the callback and turns its aiui.say(), aiui.think(), aiui.image() and other calls into RunEvents: Without a callback it runs a praisonaiagents Agent (install aiui[praisonai]): the agent named in the request when one is defined through the agents API or config.yaml, else a default assistant. Without praisonaiagents it echoes the message.

The default provider resolves tools for agents using ToolResolver from the praisonai package. Agents created via the CRUD API or ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml get their tool names (strings) automatically resolved to callable Python functions: When an agent has no tools configured, the provider gives it the tools of the SDK's autonomy profile (file operations, command execution, web search). The default assistant runs with reflection off.
Implement BaseProvider.run() — that's it:

Any provider can attach rich media to chat messages using MESSAGE_ELEMENT events. The UI renders them inline and persists them in session history. Tool results from PraisonAI agents are also detected automatically when they match OpenAI image shapes ({"data": [{"url": "..."}]}) or explicit element dicts — no provider code required. Callback handlers can use await aiui.image(url) (or dict entries in Message.elements) and the default PraisonAIProvider maps those to MESSAGE_ELEMENT events. Typed elements from Message.add_image() are not forwarded yet; see Message Elements. Full architecture, data flows, and tests: Image Preview in Chat.

Every event has a type field and optional payload fields: Field Type Used By type RunEventType All events content str RUN_COMPLETED, RUN_CONTENT token str RUN_CONTENT (streaming) name str TOOL_CALL_* args dict TOOL_CALL_STARTED result any TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED tool_call_id str TOOL_CALL_* (pairs start and completion) step str REASONING_STEP (also action, confidence, next_action) query, references, time_ms str, list, float REFERENCES (RAG sources) error str RUN_ERROR agent_id, agent_name, team_id str Multi-agent events extra_data dict Custom payload (includes element for message_element)

Agent Events Type Description run_started Agent run begins run_content Streaming token or content chunk run_completed Agent run finished run_error Error occurred run_cancelled User cancelled tool_call_started Tool invocation started tool_call_completed Tool returned result llm_content Narrative text between tool calls reasoning_started Thinking begun reasoning_step Individual reasoning step reasoning_completed Thinking finished memory_update_started Memory write begun memory_update_completed Memory write done updating_memory Memory being updated run_paused Run paused (e.g. waiting for user) run_continued Run resumed references RAG source chunks for the answer message_element Inline media element (image, video, file, etc.) — see Image Preview in Chat Team Events Type Description team_run_started Team run begins team_run_content Team streaming content team_run_completed Team run finished team_run_error Team error team_run_cancelled Team cancelled team_tool_call_started Team tool call started team_tool_call_completed Team tool call done team_reasoning_started Team reasoning begun team_reasoning_step Team reasoning step team_reasoning_completed Team reasoning done team_memory_update_started Team memory update started team_memory_update_completed Team memory update done

Subclass and implement run() to create a custom provider. Method Description run(message, *, session_id, agent_name, **kw) Required. Async generator yielding RunEvent objects list_agents() Optional. Returns list of available agents run_team(...) Optional. Multi-agent run health() Optional. Returns health check dict message_element_event(element) Static helper: a MESSAGE_ELEMENT event for an element dict
Structured event with type: RunEventType and optional payload fields (see the table above). to_dict() serialises it to the JSON the frontend reads.
30 string values matching the frontend types.ts; see the Agent Events and Team Events tabs above.

pages.d: PraisonAIUI supports a four-layer integration model so standalone mode and SDK-integrated mode can share the same feature APIs.

s.x: PraisonAIUI supports a four-layer integration model so standalone mode and SDK-integrated mode can share the same feature APIs.

Feature API layer Endpoints live in feature modules and expose stable HTTP/CLI behaviour. Feature manager layer Each feature manager keeps local fallback logic for standalone operation. Backend factory layer praisonaiui.backends provides optional injected factories (get_workflow_runner(), get_hooks_lister(), get_usage_query(), etc.). SDK/runtime layer PraisonAI or praisonaiagents implementations are used when injected or importable.

Injected backends are optional and must be callable. Features must keep local fallbacks when injected backends are absent or fail. Backend call signatures should remain minimal and dict/list based. Integration should not introduce hard imports in feature modules when a fallback already exists.
When integrated, wrappers should inject backend callables at startup; when standalone, features should run without any backend injection.

s.x: The app shell is a React interface for the PraisonAIUI dashboard: a sidebar, a header with a command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K), a React chat and a host that runs every existing dashboard page inside it. It is the default style (owner decision, 2026-11-22): create_app(), aiui run app.py and an app that registers pages all open it. The vanilla-JS dashboard is the legacy UI; it still renders exactly as before when you ask for it: Where Legacy dashboard YAML config style: dashboard Python aiui.set_style("dashboard") CLI aiui run app.py --style dashboard (prints a one-line legacy notice) Environment AIUI_SHELL=legacy

AIUI_SHELL=legacy turns app back into dashboard, whatever the config says. It is the documented way back once the default flips (see flip criteria).

Every page you have today. A page is resolved in this order: a React page registered through the SDK (built-in ports such as chat, or a UI plugin page); a server-driven page (register_page with a handler, @aiui.page), rendered from its _components tree as blocks; otherwise the original dashboard view, mounted inside the shell. React chat over the WebSocket /api/chat/ws (streaming, tool calls, reasoning, inline approvals and questions, attachments, Stop, history). When the socket cannot open it falls back to Server-Sent Events (POST /run); on SSE an agent's question says that answering needs a live connection. One markdown renderer (Streamdown) for chat and docs, with lazy code highlighting (74 languages), Mermaid and KaTeX. In chat, external links open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow", and remote images are shown as a click-to-load placeholder naming their host (same-origin, data:image/ and blob: images load directly). Approval toasts. A new approval anywhere raises a toast with a "Review" button that opens the Approvals page. On the chat page the approval is shown in the thread instead.

Colours now come from a small set of seeds (--seed-accent, --seed-ink, --seed-paper, …). Everything else (--background, --primary, sidebar and chart colours) is derived from them in CSS with color-mix(), separately for light and dark. Python emits seeds only (praisonaiui.themes.get_seed_theme_css(preset, radius, accent, density)): neutral presets (zinc, slate, stone, gray, neutral) are monochrome: the accent follows the ink; colour presets (rose, blue, …) seed the accent from the 600 shade in light mode, and the button text colour is picked automatically for at least 4.5:1 contrast; radius presets are unchanged. get_theme_css() is kept for API compatibility but the compiler no longer uses it. Runtime themes (register_theme, named presets) are converted to seeds in the browser.

Listed in the changelog for the release that ships the app shell. shadcn variables used to hold bare HSL triples that the stylesheet wrapped in hsl(). They are now complete colours: aiui validate warns (code 5001) when site.custom_css sets one of these variables to a bare triple. Custom CSS and runtime themes that still use triples are converted in the browser where possible, but update the CSS.

Code chunks are content-hashed (assets/ - .js) and served with Cache-Control: immutable. assets/index.js and assets/index.css keep fixed names in the bundle; the server references them as ?v=, so a release never mixes an old entry with new chunks. aiui build writes content-named copies of both, assets/index- .js and assets/index- .css, and loads them from index.html and every route page. A static host such as GitHub Pages ignores the query string, so ?v= alone could pair a cached old page with the new entry. index.js and index.css stay in the build, so a page cached before the switch still loads, and the copies are listed in the site's aiui-manifest.json (keys aiui-entry-copy:), so the deploy's carry-forward keeps them next to the chunks. When a chunk imports the entry module (none does today) the build keeps index.js?v=, which would otherwise load the entry twice. The docs deploy keeps the previous build's chunks, and with its ledger (aiui-carried.json) older builds' chunks for --keep-days (default 2) (src/frontend/scripts/carry-forward-assets.mjs), so a reader with an old page open can still load its lazy parts. A stale chunk that does fail to load triggers one automatic reload, and only when the server's HTML (fetched past the cache) names another build. The reload opens the page as ?aiui-build=, a URL no browser or CDN cache holds, and the boot removes the parameter again. When the boot chunks themselves cannot load, the page says so and offers Reload. A docs page never waits for good: each markdown request has a time limit for its headers and one for its body, a stalled request is sent again, and a page that still cannot load shows "Couldn't load this page" with Retry (src/frontend/src/docs/docLoader.ts). A retry also moves to a fresh connection (it switches between requests with and without credentials, which the browser keeps on separate connection pools), so a connection that a router dropped while idle does not cost the page. An attempt with no response headers after 1 s (0.4 s after 10 s without a request) also goes out on the other pool and the first answer wins; a request that fails outright switches at once. A visitor coming back after 10 s without input sends one small request (ui-config.json) the same way, so the next click already uses a working connection. python -m preqa netfault reproduces the dead connection (budget 2.5 s; measured 0.15-0.19 s). Static files are sent gzip-compressed. Each file is compressed once per version (path, mtime, size) in a worker thread and kept in memory (at most 64 MB), so a cold page load does not compress the bundle again on the event loop. Range requests get the plain bytes. The page HTML, /api/shell/manifest, /api/pages and dashboard-plugin files are compressed too. aiui run app.py serves the bundle from the installed package; it no longer copies it into ./aiui on every start (a ./aiui left by an older version is ignored for a chat app; delete it). A site built with aiui run --config is served gzip-compressed with Cache-Control: no-cache, likeaiui serve, and its ownassets/ (for example theme.css) is looked up after the package's. aiui serve answers a page's canonical URL (/docs/x) from docs/x.html directly, without a redirect to /docs/x/.

Gate Command (in src/frontend) Limit Types npx tsc -b 0 errors Unit tests npm test, npm run test:scripts all pass Size (gzip) npm run size shell boot ≤ 151.3 kB, chat route ≤ 144,500 B, /chat first-screen JS ≤ 264,400 B, index.css ≤ 32 kB, Streamdown ≤ 100 kB, shikiPlugin ≤ 55 kB, legacy App path ≤ 250 kB, docs Try it chunk ≤ 7,566 B, Pro fonts (Geist + Geist Mono woff2) ≤ 58 kB, Paper fonts (Newsreader + Source Sans 3 + JetBrains Mono woff2) ≤ 140 kB, all assets ≤ 11,180,139 B uncompressed First screen stays light npm run check:closure no Streamdown, Shiki, Mermaid, KaTeX or assistant-ui in the static closure of the entry, the shell or the legacy App Committed bundle npm run check:bundle templates/frontend equals a fresh build (pull requests that touch the frontend only) Browser suites npm run test:e2e see src/frontend/e2e/README.md The docs style preloads Streamdown before first paint (about 98 kB gzip on that path). The HTML parser it needs for raw HTML and docs components (rehype-raw, about 48 kB) is a chunk of its own that only pages whose markdown has HTML load (markdown/rehypeRawGate.ts). This is an accepted exception until docs pages are pre-rendered at build time.

The owner made app the default on 2026-11-22, before every criterion below was met. The table is kept as the remaining work list: # Criterion Status 1 Every page renders in the shell with status ready, 0 page errors and 0 leak delta in the Playwright sweep Not met. Every manifest page is ready (a page that prints a JSON error body, or whose own data endpoint fails, now counts as an error; the Inspector was one and is fixed), 0 page errors, no page grows per visit, and every page opens by URL.
