pages.d: The theme feature (praisonaiui.features.theme) holds the dashboard's colour

s.x: The theme feature (praisonaiui.features.theme) holds the dashboard's colour preset, mode (dark or light) and corner radius on the server, and serves them as CSS custom properties (--db-*) over /api/theme. The vanilla dashboard style and its chat page read these variables; the React app shell bridges them to its own tokens.
PUT /api/theme accepts any of preset (one of the 22 presets or a registered custom theme; an unknown name returns 400), mode and radius, and returns the full state.

Each mode sets a group of --db-* variables; the preset adds the accent and the radius setting adds --db-radius. A few of them: Variable Dark Light Usage --db-bg #18181b #fafafa Page background --db-text #ffffff #18181b Primary text --db-text-dim #a1a1aa #71717a Secondary text --db-border #3f3f46 rgba(0,0,0,0.08) Borders --db-card-bg rgba(255,255,255,0.03) rgba(0,0,0,0.02) Cards --db-hover #27272a rgba(0,0,0,0.04) Hover background --db-accent preset accent preset accent Buttons, links, highlights --db-accent-rgb preset r,g,b preset r,g,b Accent with alpha --db-accent-glow accent at 15% accent at 15% Focus and glow Sidebar, muted, popover, semantic (--db-success, --db-warning, --db-error, --db-info) and scrollbar variables follow the same pattern. Override any of them with aiui.set_custom_css().

A custom theme is an accent colour. Register one from Python: accent is any CSS colour; accentRgb is derived from a hex accent and is required otherwise. An invalid value raises ValueError. The theme then appears in the theme picker and in /api/theme/presets. Or over HTTP: A built-in preset name cannot be registered or deleted.

Endpoint Method Description /api/theme GET Full theme state and CSS variables /api/theme PUT Set preset, mode and/or radius /api/theme/presets GET All presets with accents, split into builtin and custom /api/theme/register POST Register a custom theme (name, accent, optional accentRgb) /api/theme/{name} DELETE Delete a custom theme

pages.d: Enable and customize dark mode for your site.

s.x: Enable and customize dark mode for your site.
Enable dark mode and choose the header toggle style in aiui.yaml:

site.theme.toggle Behavior switch (default) Starts on your configured mode (system follows the OS). One click immediately flips to the opposite mode (light ↔ dark) and saves the choice in localStorage (aiui-theme-preference) for future visits. menu Opens a 3-option dropdown (Light, Dark, System) — also available directly in React via and in the App Shell Command Palette (⌘K).

When darkMode: true, the runtime: Checks user's system preference (prefers-color-scheme) Adds a toggle button to the Header component Persists user preference in localStorage Applies data-theme="dark" to the HTML element

The React styles served by aiui run (chat, the default, plus agents, playground) and the app shell (style: app) pick the colour mode in this order: the viewer's choice, stored under aiui-theme-preference (light, dark or system); the app's: aiui.set_theme(dark_mode=True|False), else YAML site.theme.mode (light, dark, system) or site.theme.darkMode; the OS (prefers-color-scheme) when neither chose one. The page follows the OS when it changes. A static aiui build site has no server to report the app's choice, so it uses site.theme.darkMode (dark by default) unless the viewer picked a mode. With site.theme.strict: true a built site has no theme toggle and ignores the viewer's stored choice (Branding).

pages.t: How the UI Looks Are Built
pages.d: A beginner-friendly guide to how PraisonAIUI creates its visual appearance — what controls the colors, fonts, and layout you see on screen.

s.x: A beginner-friendly guide to how PraisonAIUI creates its visual appearance — what controls the colors, fonts, and layout you see on screen.

PraisonAIUI's appearance comes from three layers working together: In plain English: You choose a theme preset (like "zinc" or "blue") in your config The system translates that into CSS variables (color codes) Every button, text, and background reads those variables to know what color to be

dark_mode=True or False fixes the app's default mode. With dark_mode=None, or without set_theme(), YAML site.theme (mode: light|dark|system or darkMode) decides, and without that the UI follows the viewer's stored choice (aiui-theme-preference), then the OS.

The preset sets your color palette — it changes the accent color used for buttons, active states, and highlights across the entire UI. Category Options Neutral zinc (default), slate, stone, gray, neutral Warm red, orange, amber, yellow Cool blue, indigo, violet, purple, cyan, sky, teal Nature green, emerald, lime Vibrant pink, rose, fuchsia
When light mode is on, all backgrounds flip to white/light gray and text becomes dark.
Value Effect none Sharp, square corners sm Slightly rounded md Medium rounded (default) lg More rounded xl Very rounded, pill-shaped buttons

For fine-grained control, override these variables in customCss: Variable Default (dark) What It Controls --db-bg #0a0a0f Page background --db-sidebar-bg #111118 Sidebar background --db-accent #6366f1 Buttons, active items, highlights --db-text #e4e4e7 Primary text --db-text-dim #71717a Secondary/muted text --db-border rgba(255,255,255,0.06) Borders and dividers --db-card-bg rgba(255,255,255,0.03) Card backgrounds --db-radius 10px Corner roundness

When the same setting is defined in multiple places: Priority Source Example 1 (highest) CLI flag --style chat 2 Python API aiui.set_theme(preset="blue") 3 YAML config site.theme.preset: blue 4 (lowest) Built-in defaults zinc, dark, md radius
PraisonAIUI includes two different chat interfaces. Understanding the difference helps you choose the right one and know what features to expect.

When it's active: style: chat, style: agents, or style: playground This is the recommended chat for most users. It's built with React and benefits from the full modern web stack. What you get: Feature How it works 🎨 Your theme colors Automatically follows your preset and darkMode settings 📋 Copy code button Click to copy any code block — shows "✓ Copied" feedback 🌈 Syntax highlighting Code is color-coded by language (Python, JavaScript, etc.) 📊 Markdown tables Tables render as proper formatted tables 🔤 Rich typography Headers, bold, italic, lists — all beautifully styled 📎 File attachments Upload files to include as context

When it's active: style: dashboard This is a lighter chat built as a dashboard plugin. It's designed for quick admin interactions within the dashboard. What you get: Feature How it works 🎨 Dashboard theme Uses the dashboard's color scheme (now follows your preset!) 💬 Basic markdown Bold, italic, headings, code blocks, links, lists 🔧 Tool call display Shows when the AI is using tools 📋 Session management Create, switch, and manage conversations 🤖 Agent selection Pick which AI agent to chat with What it doesn't have (yet): ❌ Copy button on code blocks ❌ Syntax highlighting (code blocks are plain text) ❌ Markdown tables

If you want... Use this style Best chat experience with all features style: chat Multi-agent dashboard with admin controls style: dashboard Agent profiles and switching style: agents Side-by-side prompt testing style: playground

Where does each piece of styling live? File What It Does src/frontend/src/index.css Main CSS — imports Tailwind, defines default color variables src/frontend/src/themes.ts Theme engine — translates preset names to CSS variable values src/frontend/src/chat/ChatMessages.tsx React chat — has copy buttons, syntax highlighting templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js Dashboard chat — basic markdown, dashboard theme templates/frontend/plugins/dashboard.js Dashboard — defines --db-* color variables + reads config
Theming — Theme presets and YAML configuration Styles — The 6 UI styles (chat, agents, playground, etc.) Dark Mode — Dark mode toggle Dashboard — Dashboard feature overview

pages.t: How to Add a Feature to PraisonAIUI
pages.d: This guide explains every way a user can extend PraisonAIUI — and which approach fits your use case.

s.x: This guide explains every way a user can extend PraisonAIUI — and which approach fits your use case.

I want to add… Use Side Effort A new dashboard page @aiui.page() Server 5 lines A form that saves data aiui.form_action() + @aiui.register_page_action() Both 15 lines A brand-new UI component type window.aiui.registerComponent() + dict type Both 20 lines A page rendered entirely in the browser window.aiui.registerView() Client 10 lines Ship client-side JS from Python aiui.set_custom_js(path) Server 1 line A typed contract for a component aiui.register_component_schema(type, schema) Server 5 lines A custom theme aiui.register_theme() Server 1 line A new AI backend Subclass aiui.BaseProvider Server ~50 lines A whole new feature module (routes, state) Subclass BaseFeatureProtocol + register_feature() Server ~100 lines Persistence backend Subclass aiui.BaseDataStore Server ~50 lines

Goal: Show a new page in the sidebar with custom content. What happens: The page is registered in the server's page registry. It appears in the sidebar at /api/pages. When the user clicks it, the frontend fetches /api/pages/analytics/data. Your handler returns a dict; aiui.layout() wraps it in {"_components": [...]}. dashboard.js loops over _components and calls renderComponent(comp) on each. See Dashboard for the full @aiui.page() signature.

Goal: Let users submit data from the UI back to your Python code. What happens: The form renders with all inputs. On submit, the frontend POSTs to /api/pages/contact/action. The server invokes handle_contact(data) with the form values keyed by label. The returned dict is sent back to the browser as JSON. Note: Input labels become dict keys. Use distinct labels per input.
Goal: Add a new UI widget that doesn't exist in the 48 built-ins.

s.h: Step 1 — Python side: return a dict with your new type
s.x: If you stop here, the component renders as formatted JSON (graceful fallback).

s.h: Step 2 — Client side: register a renderer
s.x: Put this in a plugin.js file (or paste into DevTools Console): What happens: renderComponent(comp) checks COMPONENT_REGISTRY[comp.type] before the built-in switch. Your renderer takes priority and returns a DOM element.

Use aiui.set_custom_js(path) to ship client-side extensions directly from your app: The script runs after the plugin loader, so window.aiui.registerView and window.aiui.registerComponent are ready when it executes. No DevTools workaround needed.

Docs tags are driven by one table, DOCS_TAGS in src/frontend/src/markdown/docsTags.ts. A new tag is three small changes: An entry: the aiui-* element it becomes (el), the lower-case attributes the sanitizer keeps (attrs), an optional map from the author's attributes, and inline: true for a tag inside a sentence: Badge: { el: 'aiui-badge', attrs: ['color'], inline: true }. slots: ['caption'] renders an attribute as Markdown (an aiui-slot child; slots() in docs/DocsWidgets.tsx). Its React component under the same element name in DOCS_TAG_COMPONENTS (src/frontend/src/docs/DocsBlocks.tsx): those attributes are its props. The name in KNOWN_DOCS_TAGS (src/praisonaiui/compiler/docs_tags.py) so aiui build stops warning; tests/unit/test_docs_tags.py checks the lists. Placement (own line, one line, list items, self-closing, code left alone) and the sanitizer allowlist come with the table. Rebuild the bundle and document the tag in docs/features/writing-docs.md. A tag whose body is code is not a table entry: is listed in PASSTHROUGH and turned into a fence (codeBlockFence, docs/codeMeta.ts), so it renders through the same code frame (docs/DocsPre.tsx) as a fence. A new code option goes in parseCodeMeta and DocsPre. Content for the page's right-hand column is an aiui-panel block (, and / , which convertMkdocsBlocks turns into a panel around a code group): splitPanels (docs/panels.ts) moves every top-level one out of the article, and Content.tsx draws them in a sticky column in place of "On this page".

Goal: A page rendered entirely in the browser — no server round-trip on navigation. Still register a placeholder page in Python so it appears in the sidebar: What happens: registerView takes priority over the built-in + server-side rendering. Navigation calls your render(container) function. When the user navigates away, your cleanup() function runs.
See CSS Architecture for all variables.
See Providers.

Features live in praisonaiui/features/*.py and implement BaseFeatureProtocol: name and description are abstract on BaseFeatureProtocol; omitting either raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Optional hooks: cli_commands(), health() (kept cheap: it runs on every /api/features request) and on_config_reload() (drop what you cached from config.yaml; see Config Hot-Reload). See Protocol Architecture.

Clean separation — Python returns dicts, client renders DOM. You can mix and match server/client work per-feature. Graceful degradation — Unknown component types render as JSON (no crashes). Zero build step for Python users — No webpack/TS compile required for server-side pages. Single source of truth — Every feature has a protocol ABC. Hot-swap friendly — window.aiui.registerView/Component updates live without server restart.

Gap Resolution No aiui.set_custom_js(path) Implemented — serves the file at /custom.js and injects a tag after the plugin loader. Unit tests: tests/unit/test_custom_js.py (10 tests). form_action uses input labels as keys Implemented — every form input now accepts an optional name= kwarg that becomes the submit-key. Tests: tests/unit/test_form_input_names.py (18 tests). No typed Python ⇄ JS contract Implemented — aiui.register_component_schema(type, schema) + GET /api/components/schemas. Built-in schemas are auto-derived from ui.py signatures. Tests: tests/unit/test_component_schemas.py (9 tests). /api/features cold-start slow Mitigated — info() calls are parallelized via asyncio.gather. Warm calls are now instant; cold starts are dominated by LiteLLM import (out of scope). pygments 2.20 mkdocs build crash on providers.md Fixed — scripts/docs_hooks.py patches pymdownx.BlockHtmlFormatter.__init__ to coerce filename=None → "".

s.h: When NOT to use this approach
s.x: You need a full SPA with routing: Use the Next.js adapter or scaffold a React project with aiui init --frontend. Your UI needs TypeScript types: Use the TypeScript SDK (@praisonaiui/runtime). You need server-sent events beyond chat: Extend BaseFeatureProtocol with a WebSocket route.

[ ] Decide: is it a page, a component, or a backend module? [ ] Write the Python side first (returns a dict / routes). [ ] If you added a new component type: implement the JS renderer. [ ] Write a unit test (see tests/unit/test_form_action.py as an example). [ ] Add a runnable example under examples/python/. [ ] Update the docs under docs/features/ or docs/api/. [ ] Run mkdocs build --strict. [ ] Run pytest tests/unit -v.

pages.d: Production deployment guide for AIUI — covering Docker, environment variables, configuration, and security.

s.x: Production deployment guide for AIUI — covering Docker, environment variables, configuration, and security.

Variable Default Description AIUI_DATA_DIR ~/.praisonaiui Data directory for config, sessions, logs, and feature data (see below) AIUI_PORT 8082 Server port (Docker only) AIUI_HOST 0.0.0.0 Server bind address (Docker only) AUTH_ENFORCE false Enforce Bearer token auth on every route except the public surface (see below) AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS — Comma-separated origins allowed to call the server from another site (CORS and cross-site requests); * allows any AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS — Comma-separated host names the server answers to when reached on a loopback or private address (.example.com also matches subdomains); * turns the check off AIUI_KNOWLEDGE_ROOTS — Folders (os.pathsep-separated) that POST /api/knowledge/add-file may read, in addition to the chat attachments folder; any other file_path is refused with 400 AIUI_MAX_BODY_MB 25 Largest request body in MiB; a bigger one gets 413 before it is read. 0 turns this cap off. Paths that need no credentials (login, sign-up, protocol negotiation) always take at most 64 KiB AIUI_PUBLIC_STATIC_DIR — 1 serves every file in a static_dir without credentials (see Auth Enforcement); by default only code, styles, fonts, images and the HTML shell are public OPENAI_API_KEY — OpenAI API key for LLM provider

s.h: Feature data and the data directory
s.x: When AIUI_DATA_DIR or PRAISONAI_HOME is set (PRAISONAI_HOME wins when both are), feature data lives under that directory, so two servers with different data directories never see each other's data: Data With a data directory Without one (default install) Explicit override Recorded runs (Overview, Replay, Runs) /traces ~/.praison/traces PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR, then PRAISON_HOME/traces Memory /memory ~/.praisonai/memory and ./.praisonai/memory — Knowledge store /knowledge ./.praisonai — Training sessions /train ~/.praison/train PRAISON_TRAIN_DIR MCP server list /mcp.json ~/.praisonai/mcp.json — Video projects /projects ~/.praisonai/projects PRAISONAI_PROJECTS_DIR, set_video_engine(projects_dir=) Setting AIUI_DATA_DIR to its default, ~/.praisonaiui, counts as not set. The PraisonAI CLI always records runs to ~/.praison/traces. A server with a data directory does not show those runs unless you also set PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR=~/.praison/traces.

When AUTH_ENFORCE=true, every route requires a valid Bearer token in the Authorization header: /api/*, and also /sessions, /run, /cancel, /agents/{id}/runs, /teams/*, /v1/* (OpenAI-compatible), /agui and any route a plugin adds. Only the public surface answers without one (deny by default): Public paths (always accessible without auth): /health, /health/live, /health/ready, /api/health — health checks /api/auth/login, /login — login endpoints /api/protocol, /api/protocol/negotiate — protocol discovery the HTML page for a browser navigation (/, /chat, …; under style: app /sessions and /agents too, but only as the page, never their JSON) static code: /assets/*, /plugins/*, /_aiui/externals/*, /_plugins/*, /icon.svg, /manifest.json, /sw.js, /custom.js, /ui-config.json OAuth sign-in: GET /api/auth/oauth/{provider} and its /callback (they only redirect) A static_dir folder (create_app(static_dir=...), aiui run --config) is not public as a whole. Its code, styles, fonts and images (.js .mjs .css .map .woff .woff2 .ttf .otf .eot .svg .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .ico) answer without credentials. So do its HTML pages, but under AUTH_ENFORCE and require_auth they are served as the app shell only: the page's inlined markdown and copy are removed. Markdown, JSON (a search index) and any other file need credentials, under AUTH_ENFORCE, require_auth and URL-token mode alike. The docs app sends the stored access token with every request it makes (pages, manifests, search). A reader who has not signed in sees the sign-in prompt, and after entering the token reads the site as on an open server. Page titles and descriptions stay visible: /docs-nav.json lists them for the sidebar. To keep the folder public in front of a private API, set AIUI_PUBLIC_STATIC_DIR=1. A built docs site served by aiui serve takes a password, open pages and reader groups from content.docs.auth instead (docs sign-in). WebSocket handshakes are gated too (all of them). Browsers cannot send an Authorization header on a WebSocket, so the UI first exchanges its key for a single-use ticket (POST /api/auth/ws-ticket, valid 60 s) and connects with ?ticket=. Clients that cannot do that may still send ?token=; it is redacted from the server's access log. The other auth modes gate WebSockets as well: URL-token mode (AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN=1) accepts its session cookie, a Bearer header, ?token= or a ticket; create_app(require_auth=True) / YAML auth.requireAuth checks session tokens on every route and socket except the public surface above.

A token from POST /register passes the requireAuth check, so registration is closed by default. POST /register is accepted only: for the first user: while no account exists (and no login, password, header or OAuth callback is registered), the first registration creates it; from a signed-in user (Authorization: Bearer), to add an account; for anyone when the config opts in: (create_app(config={"auth": {"requireAuth": True, "allowSignup": True}}) from Python.) Otherwise it returns 403 {"error": "Registration is closed"}. Accounts live in memory, so after a restart the first-user window is open again until someone registers; create the admin in your app at startup (praisonaiui.auth.register_user("admin", password)) to close it. Under AUTH_ENFORCE and URL-token mode /register already needs the API key or URL token, as before; with no auth mode it stays open.

Signing in (POST /login, POST /register, OAuth) returns a session token in the JSON body and also sets it as an httpOnly cookie. The token is signed (HMAC-SHA256), not held in server memory, so a session survives a restart and works on every worker that shares the secret. With no config the first sign-in generates one into /auth_secret (mode 0600, never logged). For several hosts set the same secret everywhere: export AIUI_AUTH_SECRET=$(aiui auth create-secret). Sliding. Under requireAuth the cookie signs in HTTP and WebSockets, and a request past half its lifetime gets a fresh one: active users stay signed in, idle ones are signed out after sessionLifetime. A Bearer token lasts sessionLifetime from sign-in. SameSite and the cross-site guard keep other sites from riding the cookie. Sign-out. POST /logout revokes the Bearer token and the cookie and deletes the cookie. Revoked token ids stay in /auth_revoked.jsonl until they would have expired, so every worker on that data directory honours them. Session.clear_tokens() (in @aiui.on_logout) signs the user out on every device. Rotation. AIUI_AUTH_SECRET=new,old: the first secret signs, all verify. Drop old after sessionLifetime. A single new secret (or deleting auth_secret) signs everyone out. Trade-off: hosts that do not share the data directory verify sessions but do not see each other's sign-outs, so a signed-out token stays valid there until it expires. Keep sessionLifetime short in that setup, or rotate the secret.

With a provider configured (AIUI_OAUTH_ _CLIENT_ID and _CLIENT_SECRET), a browser starts sign-in at /api/auth/oauth/ ?return_url=/chat. Both that route and the callback are public in every auth mode. return_url must be a path on this server (starting with a single /). Anything else, such as an absolute URL or //host, returns to /. The callback sends the browser to #token=. The token is in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to a server, a log or a Referer. The dashboard stores it and removes it from the address bar. A client that sends Accept: application/json gets {"user", "token"} instead. OAuth tokens are session tokens, so they sign in under require_auth / auth.requireAuth.
The config file is located at AIUI_DATA_DIR/config.yaml (default: ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml).
The site title is configurable via site.title in config.yaml: This affects: HTML tag Dashboard header /ui-config.json response
Use the fast liveness endpoint for probes to avoid timeouts:
The Dockerfile includes a built-in health check:

AIUI supports multiple authentication modes: Mode Description none No authentication (default) api_key API key in X-API-Key header or api_key query param session Session token in Authorization: Bearer header password Username/password login

By default the server only serves its own pages: responses carry no CORS headers, and a page on another site can neither open a WebSocket to it nor send it a state-changing request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, including text/plain "simple" requests that skip the CORS preflight). The check uses the browser's Sec-Fetch-Site header, so it works behind a reverse proxy that rewrites Host; without that header the Origin is compared with Host and X-Forwarded-Host. Requests with neither header (curl, SDK clients) are not affected. A local dev server (Vite on another port) talking to a local server is allowed. To let another site call the server (an embedded widget, a separate frontend), list its origin:

A server reached on a loopback or private address (127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x, a Docker bridge) only answers requests whose Host is an IP address, localhost / *.localhost, a *.local name, the machine's own hostname, or a name listed in AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Anything else gets 400 Host not allowed (a WebSocket is closed with code 1008). This stops DNS rebinding, where a website points its own domain at 127.0.0.1 so that the browser treats it as same-origin with your local server. If a reverse proxy on the same machine forwards a public name to the server (nginx → 127.0.0.1:8082 with proxy_set_header Host $host), list that name: A server reached directly on a public IP address is not checked.

Internal networks: Use AUTH_ENFORCE=false if behind a trusted reverse proxy Public exposure: Always set AUTH_ENFORCE=true and use HTTPS Load balancers: Health check path is /health/live (fast, exempt from auth)

Hosting platforms should expose these endpoints: Endpoint Purpose /health/live Fast liveness probe (returns {"status": "ok"}) /health/ready Readiness probe (parallel feature checks) /health Deep health (parallel feature checks; ?deep=false for liveness) /api/protocol Protocol version and capabilities /api/protocol/negotiate Capability negotiation /api/features List of registered features
For a minimal AIUI deployment: Required: OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable Recommended: Persistent volume for AIUI_DATA_DIR Optional: AUTH_ENFORCE=true for multi-tenant environments

pages.d: One-click setup of this app's MCP server in Cursor, VS Code, Claude, Codex and 18 more clients

s.x: The Connect page (builtin.connect, app shell) puts the app's MCP server in the editors and agents people already use: Cursor, VS Code, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Devin Desktop (Windsurf), Zed, Kiro, TRAE, Antigravity, JetBrains Junie, Cline, Continue, OpenCode, Goose, Amp, LM Studio, Raycast, Copilot CLI, ChatGPT, and any other MCP client.

Setup What the page connects to Zero config: pip install praisonai-mcp The local PraisonAI MCP server over stdio (praisonai-mcp serve) One line: AIUI_MCP_URL=https://host/mcp A running HTTP MCP server, for example your agents behind serve_agents([...]) Neither The page says how to install praisonai-mcp The page needs style: app. It has no view in the default dashboard style. Turn it off with extensions: {disabled: [builtin.connect]}.

A client rail grouped by Editors, Terminal and Other. Clients installed on this machine come first. A dot marks the ones that already have the PraisonAI entry. One-click install for every client with a deep link: Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders, Kiro, TRAE, LM Studio and Raycast; for a remote server, also Goose and the claude.ai connector. After a click the page waits 2 seconds for the window to lose focus. If nothing takes the link, it offers Try again and the client's download page. praisonai connect, with a copy button. The command writes the client's config itself, shows a diff, keeps a backup and checks the server with a real MCP handshake. There is also the client's own command and the manual snippet, with the config file path. A scope picker. It splits your agents (ask_*) from the other tools, using a real tools/list, and rewrites the link, the commands and the snippet. The scope travels as a server argument (--tools), so it holds in every client, deep links included. The page warns when a client's tool cap is exceeded (TRAE takes 40, VS Code 128). Connected clients. The server records each MCP clientInfo it sees. Each row says what to do next: Connected, with sessions and when it was last used. Configured, not used yet: restart the client. Plain-text key in its config: reconnect so the key becomes an env reference. Fix it opens that client. ?client= (or ?ide=) preselects a client, so a README can link straight to its setup. Cloud-hosted clients (claude.ai connectors, ChatGPT) are marked: they connect from the vendor's cloud and need a public https URL, not localhost.

Both routes are owned by builtin.connect (features/connect.py) and sit behind the host's auth in every mode (R8). Route Returns GET /api/connect?tools=a,b available, server, scopable, scope, clients (praisonai_mcp.connect.export_catalog), status (per client: status, last_active, plaintext_secrets; no local paths), connections GET /api/connect/tools ok, tools (names), count, server, error, from one MCP handshake, cached for 5 minutes The client list comes from PraisonAI (praisonai_mcp.connect), the same code behind praisonai connect, so the CLI, the docs and this page show the same clients. (planned) OAuth for servers exposed over HTTP, following the MCP authorization spec, with a consent page and Revoke on this page.

pages.d: PraisonAIUI provides multiple health endpoints optimized for different use cases:

s.x: PraisonAIUI provides multiple health endpoints optimized for different use cases: /health/live - Fast liveness check (<500ms) /health/ready - Readiness check with optional deep checks /health - Legacy endpoint (backward compatibility)

Fast endpoint to verify the server is running. Returns immediately with minimal processing. Use for: Load balancer health probes Kubernetes liveness probes High-frequency monitoring Response time: <500ms (typically <100ms) Example: Response:

Verifies the server is ready to handle requests. Performs parallel health checks on all features with timeout protection. The provider check runs concurrently and is bounded by the same 0.5s timeout, so a slow provider cannot hang the response (or a cold /api/health). Use for: Kubernetes readiness probes Pre-deployment validation Detailed diagnostics Query parameters: ?deep=false - Skip feature checks for faster response Response time: With deep checks: <1s (parallel execution) Without deep checks: <200ms Example: Response with deep checks:

Cached version of readiness check for dashboard polling. 30-second TTL to reduce load. Use for: Dashboard health indicators Frequent client polling Status pages Response: Same as /health/ready but cached for 30 seconds

If you're upgrading from a version using only /health: Update monitoring: Change health checks to use /health/live for liveness Update readiness: Use /health/ready?deep=false for readiness probes Update dashboards: Point status indicators to /api/health (cached) Backward compatibility: The /health endpoint remains available but may be slow

Endpoint Cold Start Warm (p50) Warm (p95) Use Case /health/live <100ms <20ms <50ms Liveness probes /health/ready?deep=false <200ms <50ms <100ms Basic readiness /health/ready <1s <500ms <800ms Full diagnostics /api/health (cached) <1s <20ms <50ms Dashboard polling First request only, then cached for 30s

If you're seeing slow responses on the legacy /health endpoint: Switch to /health/live for fast checks Use /health/ready?deep=false if you don't need feature health Enable caching with /api/health for frequent polling
Features that timeout in /health/ready will show: This indicates the feature took longer than 500ms to respond. The server is still operational, but that specific feature may be experiencing issues.
Under high load, use /health/live exclusively for monitoring. It has minimal overhead and won't impact performance.

s.x: PraisonAIUI ships 81 composable UI component builders plus a built-in Notification Center. Every component returns a plain JSON/YAML dictionary, so you can build rich pages in Python (@aiui.page) or zero-code YAML (pages: in app.yaml), render any block inline inside Agent Chat (await aiui.send_block(...)), embed aiui.chat_panel() beside tables/docs on any page, and register custom React blocks through @aiui/sdk. Every dedicated component page in the sidebar renders the real interactive React component live right above its Python and YAML snippets. pages.d: Composable embedded Agent Chat panel for split-pane workspaces beside tables, charts, or documents.

s.x: chat_panel() embeds a compact, full-streaming Agent Chat panel inside any @aiui.page layout — using the same WebSocket/SSE runtime, tool calls, reasoning traces, inline approvals, and await aiui.send_block(...) renderer as /chat. Pair it with aiui.columns([...]) to build split-pane agent workspaces (for example, live charts, data tables, spreadsheets, or a doc_viewer on the left and a dedicated assistant on the right).

Runs in a compact frame with its own local session state (no duplicate sidebar rail and no ?session= URL hijacking). Does not overwrite an explicit welcome message with the global @aiui.welcome greeting. Lazily loads the shared chat chunk only when a page actually includes chat_panel.

Parameter Type Default Description title str "Agent Chat" Header title displayed at the top of the panel. agent str \ None None Optional agent name to route panel messages to. height int \ str 520 Panel height in pixels (>= 200) or a CSS length (e.g. "70vh"). session_id str \ None None Optional initial session ID to resume inside the panel. welcome str \ None None Optional empty-state greeting shown inside the panel.

pages.d: Multi-tab interactive spreadsheet with live zero-eval formulas (=SUM, =AVERAGE, =IF), cell editing, row filtering, and CSV/JSON export.

s.x: sheet() renders a live, editable spreadsheet with a formula bar (A1 | fx), zero-eval formula recalculation, instant row filtering, multi-tab workbooks, and formula-injection-safe CSV/JSON export. The exact same JSON schema renders in @aiui.page, zero-code YAML, Chat ```sheet fences, and the Split Artifacts Canvas. Double-click any cell below (for example B2 or C2) to edit a value or formula and watch the totals recalculate live. { "type": "sheet", "id": "q4-budget", "title": "Q4 SaaS Operating Plan", "tabs": [ { "name": "Q4 Budget", "grid": [ ["Department", "Budget ($)", "Actual ($)", "Variance ($)", "Status"], ["Engineering", 140000, 132500, "=B2-C2", "=IF(D2>=0, \"Under\", \"Over\")"], ["Infrastructure", 48000, 51200, "=B3-C3", "=IF(D3>=0, \"Under\", \"Over\")"], ["Marketing", 62000, 58400, "=B4-C4", "=IF(D4>=0, \"Under\", \"Over\")"], ["Total", "=SUM(B2:B4)", "=SUM(C2:C4)", "=SUM(D2:D4)", "=IF(D5>=0, \"On Track\", \"Review\")"], ["Average", "=ROUND(AVERAGE(B2:B4), 0)", "=ROUND(AVERAGE(C2:C4), 0)", "=ROUND(AVERAGE(D2:D4), 0)", ""] ] }, { "name": "Headcount", "grid": [ ["Team", "Current", "Planned", "Open Roles"], ["Core Platform", 8, 10, "=C2-B2"], ["Applied AI", 6, 9, "=C3-B3"], ["Design & DX", 4, 5, "=C4-B4"], ["Total", "=SUM(B2:B4)", "=SUM(C2:C4)", "=SUM(D2:D4)"] ] } ] }

Function / Operator Example Notes Arithmetic & comparisons =B2-C2, =(B2+C2)*1.1, =D2>=0 Safe recursive-descent parser (no eval or Function). SUM, AVERAGE / AVG =SUM(B2:B10), =AVERAGE(C2:C10) Supports single cells, ranges (A1:C5), and lists. MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA =MAX(B2:B10), =COUNT(B2:B10) Numeric vs non-empty cell counts. ROUND, ABS, IF =ROUND(AVERAGE(B2:B4), 2), =IF(D2>=0, "OK", "Over") Guards #CYCLE! and #DIV/0! automatically.

Parameter Type Description title str Toolbar title and export filename stem. tabs list[dict] Multi-tab workbook: [{"name": str, "grid": list[list], "values"?: list[list]}]. headers, rows list Shorthand for a single-tab spreadsheet when tabs is omitted. id str Optional stable artifact ID for versioned updates in the Artifacts Canvas. action str Optional page action name; displays a Save button that posts {action, id, title, tab, grid, values, tabs} to @aiui.register_page_action. save_label str Custom label for the Save button when action is set (default "Save").
Pass action="save_sheet" to turn aiui.sheet() into an editable data editor (like st.data_editor) that persists changes to your @aiui.register_page_action handler:

pages.d: Drag-and-drop file uploader backed by the authenticated /api/chat/attachments endpoint with safe server-side resolution.

s.x: file_upload() renders an accessible drag-and-drop file uploader with size validation, removable file chips, and zero-dependency uploads (raw binary X-Filename over POST /api/chat/attachments — works even without python-multipart). { "type": "file_upload", "label": "Upload dataset or document", "name": "doc", "accept": ".csv,.pdf,.txt,.md,.json", "max_size_mb": 10, "help_text": "CSV, PDF, Markdown, JSON, or plain text (max 10 MB)" }

POST /api/chat/attachments never returns internal server temp paths in HTTP responses and blocks active web types (text/html, image/svg+xml, application/javascript). Always resolve submitted handles on the server via aiui.get_uploaded_file(handle_or_id) (automatically applied in aiui.interface()) — malformed, expired, or forged path-traversal handles resolve to None. Uploaded temp files expire automatically by TTL (default 3600 s) and capacity limit (500 entries).

Parameter Type Default Description label str "Upload file" Accessible field label shown above the dropzone. name str "files" Form field key submitted with the uploaded file handle(s). accept str \ None None Comma-separated file extensions or MIME filters (e.g. ".csv,.pdf"). multiple bool False Allow uploading and submitting multiple files as a list of handles. max_size_mb float 10 Client-side file size cap in MB (enforced on the server too). help_text str \ None None Optional helper caption displayed inside the dropzone. auto_submit bool False Automatically submit the enclosing form as soon as upload finishes.

pages.d: Complete Agent-to-User Interface (A2UI) support in PraisonAIUI across v0.8, v0.9, and v0.10.

s.x: A2UI lets AI agents stream rich, interactive user interfaces—forms, cards, tabs, modals, sliders, date pickers, and dashboards—using safe declarative JSON instead of raw HTML or JavaScript. PraisonAIUI ships built-in, end-to-end A2UI support across the React App Shell (style: app), Chat inline surfaces, Split Chat + Canvas, Full-Page Canvas, Artifacts viewer, and Legacy Dashboard (style: dashboard).

You can also embed a surface directly inside any custom @aiui.page:

s.h: Option B — Split across DIFFERENT pages
s.x: Combine dedicated pages in one app so users can chat alongside a live preview, open a full-screen workspace, and inspect settings separately: Open any specific surface directly via query string: /canvas?surface=checkout.

PraisonAIUI accepts v0.8, v0.9, and v0.10 messages seamlessly: v0.8 (Upgraded automatically) v0.9 / v0.10 (Native) beginRendering (styles, root) createSurface (theme, catalogId, sendDataModel) surfaceUpdate ({component: {Text: {...}}}) updateComponents ({component: "Text", ...}) dataModelUpdate (contents: [{key, valueString}]) updateDataModel (path, value) deleteSurface deleteSurface userAction action Use aiui.v08_to_v09(messages) in Python anytime you want to inspect or persist the upgraded v0.9 payload.
If an agent uses a custom catalog URI (for example https://acme.example/a2ui/shop.json), register a custom renderer in custom JS (aiui.set_custom_js(...)):

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/surfaces List all active surfaces and message counts GET /api/surfaces/capabilities Return A2UI supported versions, catalog IDs, 18 components, and 14 functions GET /api/surfaces/{id} Fetch surface messages and metadata (returns empty list if not yet created) POST /api/surfaces/{id}/messages Append or replace ("replace": true) messages (v0.8 / v0.9 / v0.10) POST /api/surfaces/{id}/action Submit user action (/actions alias also supported) DELETE /api/surfaces/{id} Delete surface

pages.d: content.docs tells aiui build where your Markdown lives. Each file becomes a

s.x: content.docs tells aiui build where your Markdown lives. Each file becomes a page under site.routeBaseDocs (default /docs).
The path is relative to the config file.

include patterns are globs relative to dir. An exclude pattern matches the path relative to dir, a folder holding it (drafts, drafts/) or, with no /, any file or folder name (*.tmp). A leading / anchors it to dir; !pattern brings back a file an earlier pattern left out. Excluded files are not published at all: aiui build copies neither the pages nor the images next to them, and it lists what it left out. The same patterns can live in an .aiuiignore file next to aiui.yaml, one per line (# starts a comment); they add to exclude:

index.md and README.md (any case) are the page of their folder: guides/index.md is served at /docs/guides. indexFiles is accepted in the config, but other file names are not treated as index pages yet.

Field Description title Page title in the navigation; default: the first # heading, then the slug order Sort order within the folder (lower first); 0 or missing falls back to a number prefix description Meta description; default: the first paragraph of 20 or more characters, cut at 160 noindex true adds robots: noindex, nofollow and leaves the page out of the sitemap layout home on docs/index.md draws the home page layout The frontmatter block is not shown on the page.

Frontmatter layout: home on the docs home page (docs/index.md) puts a hero and a feature grid above the page's own Markdown, the way VitePress does: The hero image keeps a 16:10 box until the file arrives, so nothing below it jumps as it loads; once loaded it takes the image's own shape. Screenshots at 16:10 (1600 × 1000, say) never move the page. Only the image for the colour mode on screen downloads at first; the other one waits until the reader switches. aiui build adds for the hero to the home page's HTML, so the download starts with the page instead of after the app has drawn the hero. With site.theme.mode: system (or no mode) each image gets the matching prefers-color-scheme media query; a fixed light or dark preloads only that image. A reader whose saved light/dark choice differs from the system setting downloads both. Links and images resolve against the home page like Markdown links, and links to other sites open in a new tab. icon is one of message-square, panels-top-left, layout-dashboard, book-open, plug, shield-check, code, terminal, bot, zap, rocket and palette (lucide line icons); any other name shows no icon. Up to 4 actions and 12 features are kept. Every value is plain text. Only the docs home page reads layout: home; on other pages it does nothing.

A leading number gives the order when the frontmatter sets none, and the NN- prefix is stripped from the URL. Only a prefix at the start of a folder or file name counts: digits inside a name stay (ui-reset-2026-11.md is served at /docs/ui-reset-2026-11). A link that names the file (01-introduction.md) opens the page at its URL.

aiui build writes a site any static host can serve, with no rewrite rules: File Why index.html The site root; it shows docs/index.md (the docs home page). /docs and /docs/index open the same page and move to /, the home page's one URL (also in the sitemap, llms.txt and canonical links) docs/ .html /docs/ on hosts that map a path to .html (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages) docs/ /index.html /docs/ / on hosts that do not (S3, python -m http.server); the page drops the trailing slash docs/ .md The markdown the page loads, also for index pages (guides/index.md → docs/guides.md) and numbered files 404.html Any other path loads the site, which opens the page the URL means (/guides/setup opens /docs/guides/setup) or shows "Page not found" with links home and to search
Navigation: how pages become the sidebar SEO: meta tags, sitemap and robots.txt

pages.d: aiui build turns the docs folder into the sidebar (docs-nav.json). YAML

s.x: aiui build turns the docs folder into the sidebar (docs-nav.json). YAML navigation.tabs then splits that sidebar into tabs.

Each folder becomes a section and each Markdown file an entry: Inside a folder, pages sort by frontmatter order, then by file name (see Content Sources). A folder's section takes the title of its index.md (or another indexFiles name) and links to it; a folder without one is titled with its name, title-cased. Link a folder's index page by the folder (notes/). An entry's title is the frontmatter title, else the first # heading. The generated tree looks like this: content.docs.nav.mode picks between this generated sidebar (auto, the default) and one you list in YAML (below). Options for the generated sidebar: Frontmatter order wins over sort. A folder's index page is its section's own page (the label links there).
navigation.pages and navigation.groups list the sidebar in order, with no tab or nav.mode needed: These group keys work in tab groups too.

Every group folds: click its label, or the chevron beside a label that links to a page. Each reader's choice is remembered across reloads and visits. The group holding the current page always opens. interaction.drilldown: true makes a group label with no page of its own open the group's first page.

directory: card (a card grid) or accordion (a row per page) lists a group's pages with their descriptions at the end of the group's page. A group with no root gets a generated page at /docs/ (Guides is /docs/guides), or uses the page already there. content.docs.nav.directory does this for every folder of the generated sidebar.

The line above a page title is the page's group. styling.eyebrows: breadcrumbs shows every group above it, each with a page of its own linked. Every page's HTML carries a schema.org BreadcrumbList for search engines.

aiui validate and aiui build warn about a listed page name that matches no page (code 2101, with the closest name; aiui validate --strict fails), a tab, anchor or dropdown with nothing to open (2102) and about keys that do nothing yet (1004: nav.maxDepth, i18n.fallbackLocale, translationsDir).

With content.docs.nav.mode: manual the sidebar comes from the tab groups: each group is a section holding the pages it lists, in that order, whatever folder they live in. A pages entry may itself be a group, which nests a section (one level is the usual choice). A page is named by its URL path under the docs base (features/layouts), its file path without .md (adr/0001-replay-view, adr/index) or index for the home page. A name that matches no page is skipped (and reported, see Checks). A page listed twice appears once, where it is first listed. Frontmatter nav_title gives a page a shorter sidebar title than its heading (nav_title: CLI on a page titled "CLI API Reference"). Pages no group lists are still built and reachable by URL, but hidden: not in any sidebar, search, sitemap.xml or llms.txt (see Hidden pages). Leave a page out of the site with content.docs.exclude (see Content Sources). hidden: true on a group hides its pages the same way; on a tab it also drops the tab from the header. boost: 2 on a group ranks its pages higher in site search (0.1 to 10; a page's own boost wins; see Search). With tabs, search results can be filtered by tab. The active tab is the one whose groups list the page; for a page no group lists, the folder prefix decides as in auto mode, then the first tab.

A group's icon: in the navigation YAML, or a page's frontmatter icon:, puts a 16px line icon before its title in the sidebar and the phone drawer. Any lucide icon name (flag, house, or an old name such as home), an emoji (icon: "🚀") or an image URL (https://… or /icons/x.svg). See Icons. aiui validate warns (7009) about a name that is not an icon. Page icons work in both modes; group icons need mode: manual.

navigation.tabs groups the sidebar sections into tabs in the header. A section belongs to the first group whose group name matches its title, whose prefix is its folder, or whose pages list one of its pages. The sidebar shows only the active tab's sections, in the order of its groups; the active tab follows the URL. A section that no group of any tab claims is not shown while tabs are set. In manual mode the groups are the sections, so each one belongs to its tab. Clicking a tab opens its first page; the active tab follows the page you are on. On phones the tabs move into the navigation drawer, where tapping one shows its sidebar without leaving the page.

Key On Does icon tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown an icon before the name href tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown a link instead of a sidebar (url still works on a tab) pages tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown pages listed straight in it (before its groups) groups tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown its sidebar sections hidden tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown leaves the header and sidebar; its pages stay routable menu tab items, each with its own sidebar or href; the tab opens the list description menu item, dropdown a second line under the name tabs dropdown header tabs shown while that dropdown is open

Anchors are links pinned at the top of the sidebar on every page. An anchor with href links out; one with pages or groups opens its own sidebar, like a tab. navigation.global.anchors takes the same entries and lists them first.

navigation.dropdowns (also spelled products, with product: names) puts a switcher at the top of the sidebar. Each entry opens its own sidebar, or brings its own header tabs, so one site can hold several products. Tabs, menu items, anchors and dropdowns share one rule: each part with pages or groups gets its own sidebar, and the page you are on decides which one is open. aiui validate warns about one with no pages, groups or href (code 2102) and about a listed page that does not exist (2101).

navigation.versions publishes several versions of the docs side by side. The default version is served at the docs root; every other version comes from its own folder, with no page list needed: Key Meaning version the name in the switcher; also the folder and URL segment (v1, 2.x) default the version at the docs root (default: the first one) tag a badge after the name (Latest, Beta, Deprecated), up to 24 characters index true keeps an older version in the sitemap and llms.txt (default: only the default version) groups, pages, tabs the version's own sidebar and header tabs (with nav.mode: manual); without them the folder's pages form the sidebar hidden left out of the switcher; its pages stay routable A switcher at the top of the sidebar (and of the phone drawer) names the open version. Picking another one opens the same page in it (/docs/guide/setup and /docs/v1/guide/setup), or that version's first page when it has no such page. The sidebar, the pager, the header tabs and the site search show the open version only; the top-level tabs and dropdowns belong to the default version, and anchors show in every version. An older version's page names the default version's same page as its canonical URL and carries robots: noindex, so search engines send readers to the current docs; its pages stay out of sitemap.xml and llms.txt unless the version sets index: true. A page's own canonical or robots front matter wins. aiui validate reports two versions with one name, more than one default, and a version that lists a page from another version's folder (code 7018).

navigation.languages publishes translated docs. The default language is served at the docs root; every other one comes from its own folder, named by its code, with no page list needed: Key Meaning language the language code (fr, pt-BR); also the folder and URL segment label the name in the switcher (default: the language's own name, Français) default the language at the docs root (default: the first one) index true lists its pages in llms.txt too (default: only the default language) groups, pages its own sidebar (with nav.mode: manual); without them its folder's pages form the sidebar hidden left out of the switcher and the translation links; its pages stay routable A switcher in the header (an icon on phones) opens the same page in the other language (/docs/guide/setup and /docs/fr/guide/setup), or that language's first page when the page is not translated yet. The sidebar, the pager and the site search show the open language only. The reader's pick is remembered, and on a first visit to the docs home the reader's browser language (fr-CA finds fr) opens its translation; crawlers and other automated browsers always get the default language. navigation.languageRedirect: false turns that redirect off. Every page carries and, when it has translations, a for each (with x-default on the default language's page); sitemap.xml lists the same alternates. llms.txt and llms-full.txt hold the default language, and each other language gets its own llms- .txt. With navigation.versions too, a language folder sits inside its version's folder: docs/v1/fr/ is served at /docs/v1/fr/..., and both switchers keep the page. aiui validate reports two languages with one code, more than one default, and a version folder inside a language folder such as docs/fr/v1/ (code 7020).

navbar adds links and one primary button to the header. On phones they move into the navigation drawer. A link with type and no label shows the network's mark alone, named for screen readers. Links to another site open in a new tab. The star count needs no setup: the browser asks the public GitHub API once and keeps the answer for six hours. If it cannot get one, the button shows the mark and the label.

footer.socials maps a network to a URL and draws its mark; footer.links adds columns of links above the bottom line. Known keys: github, gitlab, x (or twitter), discord, slack, linkedin, youtube, bluesky, mastodon, reddit, telegram, facebook, instagram, threads, medium, hacker-news, npm, website, email (a mailto: URL), rss and podcast. Any other key whose URL is on one of those sites gets that mark (community: https://discord.gg/x shows Discord); the rest get a globe. Each mark is a link named for its network.

banner puts a strip above the header on every docs page: banner: "Version 2 is out." is the short form. A closed banner stays closed for that reader until its content changes, so a new announcement shows again with no key to bump.

pages.d: Learn how templates and layouts work in PraisonAIUI.

s.x: Learn how templates and layouts work in PraisonAIUI.

A template, used by the docs site (aiui build), combines: a layout: the structure around the page content slots: the components for the header, footer and table of contents (see Slots & Components) optional zones: widgets around the content (see Widget Zones) Routes pick the template for a URL (see Configuration). These are docs-site layouts; the layouts of the React app shell are a different thing (see Layouts).

Every layout sits between the site header and footer. Layout Description ThreeColumnLayout Sidebar + content + TOC (the default) TwoColumnLayout Sidebar + content (no TOC) CenteredLayout Centered content, no sidebar; hero zone FullWidthLayout Sidebar when there is navigation, wide content; hero zone FlexibleLayout Sidebar (or leftSidebar widgets), content, TOC, and widget zones
The classic documentation layout with sidebar and TOC.
Sidebar + Content without the right TOC column.
Centered content with no sidebar, ideal for articles/blogs.
The content takes the remaining width; the sidebar shows only when the site has docs navigation.
Slots can be assigned in two ways:
Point to a component defined in the components section:
Use a component type directly:

pages.d: A template names a component for each slot of its layout. In the docs site that

s.x: A template names a component for each slot of its layout. In the docs site that aiui build produces, the React renderer reads three slots; the others are validated and compiled into the manifest but do not change the page.

Slot Effect in the docs site header Its component's props (logoText, logoImage, links, cta) fill the header. YAML navbar links and CTA win over links/cta, but logoImage wins over YAML logo.light/logo.dark footer Its component's props (text, links) fill the footer bottom row, next to YAML footer right null hides the table of contents; any other value shows it left, main No effect: the sidebar is always the generated navigation and the main area the page's Markdown Without a header or footer slot, the components named header and footer are used. aiui validate checks that every ref names a component.
These name the generated navigation, the page content and the table of contents. They take no props the renderer reads.

The docs site renderer has no hook for your own slot components. The separate TypeScript runtime in the repository (src/praisonaiui-ts, see TypeScript) has a SlotRegistry for apps that render the manifests themselves. Pages in the React app shell are added with plugins instead (see Plugins).
