s.x: Widget zones place small built-in widgets (stats cards, links, banners) around the page content of a docs site (aiui build, style: docs or custom), configured per template in YAML.
FlexibleLayout renders these zones:
Use the zones property in your template configuration:

Zone Location Notes hero Above the content Banners, announcements leftSidebar Left column Replaces the docs navigation when set rightSidebar Right column Below the table of contents bottomNav Below the content Related links footer Bottom Footer widgets, above the site footer header, topNav, main Accepted by the schema; no layout renders them yet A Toc entry in rightSidebar is skipped: the table of contents is always drawn there when the page has headings. When the config defines a component named sidebar, header or footer and a template leaves the matching zone (leftSidebar, header, footer) empty, the build fills the zone with that component.
Display metrics and statistics.
Navigation links widget.
Email subscription form.
Landing page hero section.
Social media links.
Copyright notice.

Widget Props Progress label, value (0 to 100), showPercent (default true) Announcement title, message, type (info, warning, success) RecentPosts title, posts (list of title, href, date) BadgeList title, badges (list of strings)
Layout Zones rendered FlexibleLayout hero, leftSidebar, rightSidebar, bottomNav, footer ThreeColumnLayout (default) rightSidebar CenteredLayout hero FullWidthLayout hero TwoColumnLayout none

pages.d: Two commands reload during development: aiui dev for a docs site and

s.x: Two commands reload during development: aiui dev for a docs site and aiui run --reload for an app.

Run it in the folder that holds aiui.yaml: It builds the site, serves it and opens it in the browser. Save a page, a snippet or aiui.yaml and the site rebuilds and the open tab reloads by itself, at the same scroll position (the URL keeps the #heading). No configuration needed to start. A folder with only a docs/ folder of Markdown files works: the site is built with the defaults and titled after the folder. A broken edit never takes the preview down. The error is printed in the terminal and shown over the page, and the last good build stays up until you save a fix. Warnings from the build (content checks) print once each in the terminal. Production output is untouched. Each build goes to a temporary folder, removed on exit. The few lines of script that listen for rebuilds are added to pages as they are served, so aiui build output never contains them. The preview is served the way aiui serve serves the build: the same routes, cache rules and base path. The tab listens on /__aiui/dev (Server-Sent Events) with a script served from /__aiui/dev.js, so the preview runs under the site's Content Security Policy. It only answers on this machine unless you pass --host; build errors include file paths, so expose it only on a network you trust. Every option is in the CLI reference.

aiui serve --watch rebuilds the site into the output folder on every change in the configuration's folder, without reloading the browser. Use it when you want the built files on disk; aiui dev is the writing loop.
Uvicorn restarts the server when a file in the folder of app.py changes, and the restarted server loads app.py again with the same style, datastore and config.
aiui dev --examples serves a small dashboard (default port 9000) that switches between the example projects in a folder (each a directory with an aiui.yaml, or the old name aiui.template.yaml):
Config Hot-Reload: reloading the runtime config of a running server CLI

pages.d: Key-based UI strings with locale switching and {name} interpolation, served by the i18n feature (praisonaiui.features.i18n). English, Spanish and French ship bu

s.x: Key-based UI strings with locale switching and {name} interpolation, served by the i18n feature (praisonaiui.features.i18n). English, Spanish and French ship built in.

The i18n system uses a key-based translation approach: Each string has a dotted key (e.g., app.welcome, chat.send) Keys are grouped by prefix: app, chat, skills, finops, nav, error {name} placeholders are replaced at lookup time An unknown key returns the key itself; an unknown locale falls back to English
Locale Language Strings en English 36 es Spanish (Español) 36 fr French (Français) 36
A different backend implements I18nProtocol (t, list_locales, get_strings, get_locale, set_locale) and is installed with set_i18n_manager().

The React styles read a YAML i18n block. With more than one locale, the header shows a locale switcher; picking a locale loads its strings from /api/i18n/strings/{locale} and sets the server locale. A locale in rtlLocales switches the page to right-to-left.

Endpoint Method Description /api/i18n/locales GET List available locales /api/i18n/strings/{locale} GET Get all strings for a locale /api/i18n/translate POST Translate a key with optional variables /api/i18n/locale GET Get current default locale /api/i18n/locale POST Set default locale
An unknown locale returns 404; a malformed one 400.
Pass "variables": {"count": 3} to fill placeholders.

pages.d: Point the docs site at an OpenAPI spec; aiui build loads, bundles and checks it.

s.x: Name your spec in aiui.yaml; aiui validate and aiui build load and check it. A file (relative to aiui.yaml) or an http(s) URL; http://localhost:8080/openapi.json works with no flag. JSON or YAML, OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2. Swagger 2.0 is an error. A $ref to another file (paths/pets.yaml, ../common.yaml#/components/schemas/Error) resolves relative to the file naming it, URLs too, and is bundled in: no pre-bundling. Recursive schemas, across files too, stay finite. 3.0 specs are normalised to 3.1 rules for rendering (nullable, boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum, schema example); the published file keeps your version. openapi also goes on a navigation tab or group: a path or URL, {source, directory} or a list of either. A spec named twice loads once. directory: the URL folder of its endpoint pages (default api-reference).

Each problem names its file, line and JSON pointer (openapi.yaml:42: $ref '#/x' does not resolve (at #/components/schemas/Pet/properties/owner)). Errors failvalidate and build: an unreadable file or URL, YAML/JSON syntax, a missing or unsupported openapi version, info without title/version, a $ref that does not resolve, a path not starting with /, a duplicate operationId. Warning: a {param} with no path parameter.

aiui build writes openapi/ .json (the spec bundled into one file, x-excluded operations removed; : file name, -2 on a clash), openapi/index.json ({"specs": [{source, file, title, openapi, version, operations}]}), an "OpenAPI specs" section in llms.txt and an RFC 9727 API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog (each API's base URL, spec and first endpoint page).

Every operation and 3.1 webhook gets a docs page, generated at build time as Markdown with the API field components: the endpoint bar with Try it, server URL, deprecation notice, path / query / header / cookie parameters, request body, each response (schemas with oneOf/anyOf tabs, constraints and conditional requirements), request examples in several languages, response examples, callbacks and a link to the spec. They publish like hand-written pages: agent .md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, sitemap and site search (which also matches METHOD /path, the operationId and every parameter and body field name). Spec Result api.openapi only an "API Reference" group at the end of the sidebar openapi on a tab its tag groups join the tab ("API Reference" for untagged operations) openapi on a group its tag groups go inside that group tags one sidebar group per operation's first tag; label: x-group, x-displayName, summary, then name; 3.2 parent nests groups; a tag with another kind (badge) makes no group untagged webhook a "Webhooks" group x-hidden: true page built and routable, not in the sidebar or indexes x-excluded: true no page, and removed from the published spec deprecated: true a deprecation notice URL: /docs/ / /, the slug from the operationId (listPets -> list-pets, so rewording a summary keeps the URL), else the summary, else method and path (get-pets-id). x-aiui: {href: /reference/pets} sets the whole path (kebab-cased, .. dropped; see page settings). A slug already taken (by a hand-written page or another endpoint) gets -2, -3. The title is the summary as written, else the operationId in words. aiui validate warns about a duplicate tag, an unknown parent and a parent cycle.

Each field shows what the schema says, at build time, in the page Markdown (so agents and search see it too): Schema On the page $ref, allOf followed and merged into one field list oneOf / anyOf tabs, one per choice, titled by its title, else its $ref name, else its type, else "Option n"; at the top of a body or response too nullable: true, type: [x, "null"], anyOf: [X, {type: "null"}] x \ null in the type; the field still expands to X's properties object[], nested objects properties nested under "Show properties", a recursive schema stops one level down enum, const "Available options: card, bank", "Allowed value: card" minimum/maximum (exclusive too), minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems, pattern "Required range: 1 = 1 elements", "Pattern: ^[0-9]+$" examples / example on a field "Example: 5" (short values) additionalProperties, not "Additional properties: string", "Must not match: integer" if/then/else, dependentRequired, dependentSchemas (also inside allOf) a pill on each affected field: "required if method = card", "required unless method = card", "required if owner is set"; an if that tests more than sibling const / enum / required shows "conditionally required"

The side column's response example has one tab per status code, content type (when a response has several) and named example (its summary, else its key). This gives the tabs 200 · application/json · A small cat, 200 · application/json · big and 200 · application/xml: Per content type: the examples map (value, 3.2 dataValue / serializedValue, or the externalValue URL), else example, else for JSON an example built from the schema. JSON is pretty-printed (a JSON string too); XML, HTML, YAML and CSV are highlighted; other types are text.

The side column shows the request as code, one tab per language: cURL, Python and JavaScript by default. A pick is remembered, so every endpoint page opens on the reader's language. Each sample is built at build time from the spec: the server URL (variables set to their defaults; a relative or missing server is joined to https://api.example.com), path parameters (their example, else a {name} placeholder), required query, header and cookie parameters and any with an example, the first security requirement as a placeholder (Bearer, Basic, an API key in its header, query or cookie) and the body (its first example, else one made from the schema without readOnly fields). JSON, form-urlencoded and plain-text bodies work in every language; multipart/form-data in cURL, Python and JavaScript (a format: binary field is sent as a file). Languages: curl, python, javascript, go, java, ruby, php, csharp, rust, swift (also shell, node, js, py, c#, dotnet, ...). aiui validate names an unknown one. Your own samples, from an SDK say, go in the operation's x-codeSamples (or x-code-samples). They come first, in their order; one in a generated language replaces that sample, any other language adds a tab. label is the tab title (default: the language's name). The agent .md export, llms-full.txt and the page source keep every sample as a fence.

Under the title, every endpoint page has an endpoint bar (method, path, copy) and Try it: a request form with a server menu (operation, path, then spec servers) and an input per server variable, an input per path, query, header and cookie parameter (enum and boolean as menus, arrays comma-separated, empty required ones named before sending) and the body to edit (multipart/form-data as a JSON object of its fields). Inputs start with x-default, else the example (example, examples, default, const, first enum value); the body with its first example, else one made from the schema. Beside them: the curl command for exactly what will be sent, live, with copy, and after Send the status, time, size, headers and body (JSON pretty-printed). A relative or missing server URL means the site the docs are served from. With auth, the bar asks GET /api/auth/status once per page load and shows Try it only when it answers authenticated: true (an aiui serve or create_app site whose reader is signed in; without sign-in configured, every reader counts as signed in). On a static host it acts like simple. Webhooks have no Try it. Front matter playground: (same values) sets the display of one openapi: or api: page, x-aiui metadata.playground of one generated page. The request goes straight from the reader's browser to your API: no proxy, so it works on a static host and keys never pass through a third party, and the browser's CORS rules apply. The API must allow the docs site's origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin; for custom headers or a JSON body, a preflight OPTIONS with Access-Control-Allow-Headers). A blocked request says it "did not reach the API" (the curl command still works in a terminal). Response headers other than the CORS-safelisted ones show only when listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers; a cookie parameter goes only into the curl command (a browser sends just the cookies it holds). aiui build writes each page's form data to openapi/try/ .json; the form is a lazy chunk loaded on the first hover, focus or click of Try it. In the page source the bar is (without src, the bar alone, usable on a hand-written page); the agent .md keeps `GET` `/pets`. #### Authentication An operation's security (else the spec's) becomes an Authorization section on its page (a field per scheme, required when every alternative needs it, OAuth2 scopes listed) and inputs in Try it: apiKey in a header, query or cookie, http bearer (and any other scheme name), http basic (username and password, base64-encoded for you), oauth2 and openIdConnect (paste an access token; sent as Bearer). With several alternatives a menu picks one ({} in the list adds "None"); security: [] turns it off; mutualTLS is left out (a browser cannot send it). A scheme's x-default prefills its input. Values are kept in the browser tab's sessionStorage per docs site (gone when the tab closes, never localStorage) and sent only with the request itself. The curl command shows them as ******** until Show values; the request examples on the page keep placeholders (Bearer). #### Files and streams multipart/form-data: a file input per part with format: binary / byte or a contentMediaType; the chosen file replaces that field (curl --form 'photo=@cat.png'). A body that is a file (application/octet-stream, image/*, audio/*, video/*, PDF, or a format: binary schema): one file input, sent as the body (curl --data-binary). A JSON field with format: byte or contentEncoding: base64 / base64url: a file input that writes the file's encoding into the body. A text/event-stream, NDJSON or JSON Lines response is shown as it arrives: server-sent events as a list (event name, id, data with JSON pretty-printed), other streams as text. Stop ends it; reading stops at 10 MB; a broken connection says "Stream interrupted." (planned): method and kind: badge pills in the sidebar, a choice picker for any fields, api.optional, and showing image, audio and video responses inline.

Name an operation in a page's front matter and the page shows it: the endpoint bar and Try it under your # title, your Markdown, then the generated parameters, body, responses and request and response examples. "GET /users" looks in every spec the config names; "admin.yaml POST /users" in that file (its name is enough; a file only pages name is loaded, relative to aiui.yaml, and published); "webhook user-created" names a webhook. title, description and search keywords come from the operation unless the page sets them; the spec's description shows only when the page has no text of its own. The operation gets no generated page of its own: your page replaces it. playground: simple (or none) on the page changes its Try it display.
api: makes an endpoint page from the page alone: the bar, and Try it with an input per (placeholder, else default, as the example), per {param} in the path, and a JSON body of the body fields.

A pages: entry can be an operation: "GET /users", "admin.yaml POST /users" or "webhook user-created". Without a file it comes from the nearest group or tab with openapi, else api.openapi, else any spec. When a spec's own group (or api.openapi) lists operations, only the listed ones get pages, each where it is listed, and no tag groups are added. An entry for an operation a page shows (openapi: front matter) links that page. aiui validate names a reference that matches no operation (7012).

An operation's x-aiui sets its generated page: metadata is front matter (title, sidebarTitle, description, playground, tag, og:*, ...), content is Markdown shown above the description (any docs component works) and href the page URL. The x-mint key other docs tools write is read too; x-aiui wins where both set a value. From Python, praisonaiui.compiler.openapi.load_spec("openapi.yaml") returns an ApiSpec (ok, issues, document, operations, dereference(node)).

pages.d: One line in a docs page and aiui build writes the reference for a Python module, class or function from its docstrings.

s.x: Write one line in a docs page and the build turns it into the reference for that Python module, class or function: No extra tool or build step. The source is read as text (Python's ast), so the package does not have to be installed and nothing is imported. aiui dev rebuilds the page when you save a .py file. The reference goes in where the line is, in the same pass as snippets, so the page, its agent .md, llms-full.txt, search and aiui validate all see it.

You write You get ::: mypkg.client The module docstring, then its public members: __all__ in order when there is one (re-exports followed), else every public class and function ::: mypkg.client.Client The class: constructor signature and parameters, bases, attributes (annotated or documented, properties, Field(default=, description=)), then its public methods ::: mypkg.client.connect One function or method Each object gets a heading anchored by its dotted path with dashes (#mypkg-client-Client-fetch) and its signature with type hints and defaults. Names starting with _ are left out. From the docstring: Parameters: rows with the type and default from the signature, required when there is no default, and the text; documented **kwargs keys get rows too. Attributes: rows. Returns, Yields, Raises: lists of types with their text. >>> examples, :: blocks and .. code-block::: highlighted code. Notes, Warnings, .. note::, .. warning::: callouts. Google (Args:), NumPy (Parameters over ----------) and reST (:param x:, :type x:, :returns:, :rtype:, :raises E:) styles all work. reST roles become code, and < is escaped so text never turns into a tag.

YAML on the indented lines under the block (an options: mapping works too): Option Default What it does members all public Only these members, in this order; false: the object alone private false Also _name members (not __dunder__) show_source false A collapsed "Source code" block under each object heading_level 2 Heading level of the block's own object (1 to 6)
mypkg.client is mypkg/client.py, mypkg/client/__init__.py or a .pyi, in src/, then the project folder. Change the folders, searched in order:

A block naming no module or member, a file that is not valid Python, or an unknown option is 7016 in aiui validate and fails aiui build with the page and line. A ::: line inside a code fence is left alone.
The class behind this page, from ::: praisonaiui.compiler.python_api.PythonApi with members: [markdown] and heading_level: 3:

Finds and renders the objects ::: blocks name. Parameters The project folder. Folders under root searched in order for a module's file. #### PythonApi.markdown() {#praisonaiui-compiler-python_api-PythonApi-markdown} The Markdown for one ::: target block. Parameters A dotted module path, optionally followed by a class, function or method. The block's options (members, private, show_source, heading_level). Returns str: Headings, signatures and field rows for the docs Markdown pipeline. Raises ApiReferenceError: When target names nothing, or a listed member does not exist.

pages.d: Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

s.x: Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

Top-level seo block in aiui.yaml: Every key is optional; the defaults are what most sites want. siteUrl is needed for absolute canonical URLs and sitemap.xml. Without it the build falls back to a CNAME file next to the config (or in docs/), and without either there is no sitemap and llms.txt / llms-full.txt use root-relative links. What the build publishes for agents (agent-ready .md pages, llms.txt by nav group, markdown.instructions): AI-ready docs.

aiui build automatically generates: File Purpose sitemap.xml All doc URLs with lastmod dates robots.txt Crawl rules + sitemap pointer llms.txt AI crawler index (llmstxt.org), one section per nav group llms-full.txt Every page as agent-ready Markdown, in one file docs/**/*.html Per-route HTML with meta tags + crawl nav .nojekyll GitHub Pages Jekyll bypass No extra flags are needed: the files are written whenever content.docs is configured (the site-URL ones only when a site URL is known, see above). A robots.txt or sitemap.xml next to aiui.yaml is published as it is, instead of the generated one.

One rule decides the sitemap, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, site search and the page's robots meta, so they never disagree: Page Sidebar Sitemap, llms, search normal yes yes index, follow noindex: true yes no noindex hidden no no (yes with seo.indexing: all) noindex (index, follow with all) any, with seo.robots.index: false as above no sitemap or llms files; search kept noindex searchable: false yes sitemap and llms yes; site search no index, follow Each page has exactly one robots meta tag. noindex does not add nofollow: crawlers still follow the page's links to the pages that are indexed. With seo.robots.index: false, robots.txt says Disallow: /, and no sitemap.xml or llms*.txt is written (one left from an earlier build is removed).

A hidden page is built and reachable by its URL (share the link), but it is not in the sidebar, the previous / next links or search, and not indexed. In content.docs.nav.mode: manual, hidden: true on a group or tab hides all its pages, and pages no group lists are hidden too (Navigation). A folder without an index.md is a sidebar section only, never a page: it gets no route and no sitemap entry.

seo.contentSignals writes a Content-Signal line into robots.txt, saying how crawlers may use the pages: search (search results), aiInput (answers grounded on the page) and aiTrain (model training). Keys you leave out are left out of the line; with no contentSignals there is no line.

Use frontmatter on any markdown page: If description is omitted, the first paragraph is used automatically. Component and HTML tags are left out of it: a page that opens with or a multi-line gets its first sentence of prose. Any Open Graph, Twitter or article tag, the canonical URL, the robots value and keywords can be set per page (quote keys that have a colon): Each tag is decided once, in this order (later wins): the built defaults, seo.metatags, seo.paths (shorter paths first), the page's frontmatter. Then og:url follows the canonical and twitter:image the og:image (unless set themselves), and twitter:card is summary_large_image when the page has an image. Root-relative URLs (/images/x.png) become absolute. A noindex page keeps noindex whatever the overrides say, and a robots value with noindex (from frontmatter or a seo.paths folder) also leaves the page out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search, so they never disagree. Open Graph keys (og:, article:) are written as property=, the rest as name=; every value is HTML-escaped. aiui validate rejects a seo.metatags key that is not a tag name.

Install Pillow and every docs page gets its own share image, with no config: The build draws a 1200x630 PNG per page and publishes it at /og/ .png (/og/docs/guide/install.png). Each card shows the page title (sized to fit, up to three lines), its sidebar group, as much of the description as fits, the site name with its logo and the site's host, in the theme's accent and colour mode (site.theme.preset, accent, accentDark, mode; preset paper gets the paper colours). A PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF logo is drawn as is; an SVG or emoji logo becomes the site's initial on an accent tile. Latin text uses the UI's own font; other scripts use a system font (Noto Sans CJK, Arial Unicode, Noto Sans or DejaVu Sans). The card becomes the page's og:image and twitter:image, with a summary_large_image card, in the built HTML and when the docs app moves between pages, and the site root shares the docs home's card. Which image a page gets, first match wins: Set by Image 'og:image' in the page's frontmatter or a seo.paths folder that image, no card drawn og:image in seo.metatags that image on every page, no cards drawn seo.ogImages: false, or Pillow not installed seo.defaultImage otherwise the page's generated card Cards are cached by a hash of what they show (in $AIUI_DATA_DIR/og-cards, else ~/.praisonaiui/cache/og-cards), so aiui dev and repeat builds only draw the pages that changed, and new cards are drawn in parallel. Without Pillow, aiui build prints one note saying how to turn them on.

Each route HTML file contains: (absolute HTTPS) Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type, og:site_name, og:image: the page's social card by default), each once Twitter Card tags (summary_large_image with an image) Your seo.metatags, seo.paths and frontmatter tags One JSON-LD @graph: Organization, WebSite (with a SearchAction: ?q= opens site search), TechArticle (publisher, dateModified with content.docs.lastUpdated, keywords, image) and a BreadcrumbList from the sidebar groups Static with links to every doc page (for non-JS crawlers) pre-rendered page content

When users navigate via the sidebar, React updates title, canonical, OG, Twitter, robots, and JSON-LD to match the current page, with the same tags, overrides and order as the built HTML (docs-nav.json carries each page's seo map). The built page's JSON-LD graph stays while it is the page shown.
See GitHub Pages for publishing the build. Submit your sitemap in Google Search Console:

pages.d: Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and

s.x: Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and choose what readers see on a URL with no page.

List moved pages under redirects: at the top level of aiui.yaml: Key Meaning source A site path starting with /. :name matches one path segment; a final :name* matches the rest of the path, including nothing (/docs/v1/:slug* matches /docs/v1 and /docs/v1/a/b). destination A site path or a full URL. It can reuse the names from source. permanent true (default) answers with 301, false with 302. The first matching rule wins. Leave out the --base-path prefix: rules use site paths and the build adds the base path.

s.h: Where each kind of rule works
s.x: aiui build publishes every rule whose source is not a published page: Host Exact source (/docs/old) Wildcard source (/docs/v1/:slug*) aiui serve 301 / 302 301 / 302 (a file at the path wins) Netlify, Cloudflare Pages 301 / 302 from the _redirects file 301 / 302 from _redirects GitHub Pages, any static host A stub page at the old URL (meta refresh, a canonical link, a script redirect) The docs app follows the rule from the page-not-found view The query string and the #section carry over unless the destination sets its own. A stub never replaces a real file; it has noindex and a canonical link to the new URL. The link check treats every source as a valid link.
aiui validate warns when an exact rule loops or ends at a docs path with no page (7010), or when a page is still published at its source (7011).

A URL with no page shows "Page not found", a link home, the search, and up to three pages from the sidebar whose names are close to the URL (a typo such as /docs/instalation offers Installation), unless a redirects: rule matches first. Set the heading and text under errors:: Key Default Meaning title Page not found The heading and the browser tab title description A line naming the missing path Markdown under the heading redirect false true sends readers to the home page instead of showing the page

pages.d: Every page as clean Markdown for agents, llms.txt by nav group, llms-full.txt, agent instructions, Visibility, Accept text/markdown, an MCP server and Ask AI with cited answers.

s.x: aiui build publishes each docs page twice: the page people read, and the same page as clean Markdown for AI agents. Nothing to configure, and it works on any static host. URL What it holds /docs/ .md the page as agent-ready Markdown (below) /llms.txt the llmstxt.org index: one ## section per nav group, each page linked as its .md /llms-full.txt every indexed page's agent-ready Markdown in one file /.well-known/llms.txt, /.well-known/llms-full.txt copies, where some agents look first Each page's HTML names its Markdown (). Links are absolute with a site URL (seo.siteUrl or a CNAME, see SEO), root-relative otherwise. Hidden and noindex pages stay out of the llms files. An llms.txt or llms-full.txt next to aiui.yaml is published as it is.

In the source In the .md front matter # Title, then > description , , … a blockquote with a bold label: > **Note:** … / one heading per tab, a level under the heading above / a numbered list: 1. **Install** a list item: - Guide , (in ), , - `user_id` (path, string, required): … (nested one level); a bold "Request example" over its fences; the content , , other tags, comments their content (a bold title, an italic caption); comments removed links to pages (setup.md, /docs/setup) absolute .md URLs; other links absolute URLs Code is never changed. Copy page, View as Markdown and Open in ChatGPT / Claude use this version; the browser renders the untouched source, published as /docs/ .source.md. .mdx pages work the same way, and are in search and llms-full.txt.
Every .md, llms.txt and llms-full.txt then carries, under the title, a > ## Agent instructions quote block with these lines.

s.h: Content for people or for agents only
s.x: for="humans" shows on the page and in site search only; for="agents" only in the .md and the llms files.
aiui serve answers a page URL with its Markdown when Accept ranks text/markdown at least as high as text/html (browsers still get the page):

aiui serve and aiui dev also run an MCP server for the site at /mcp, so an editor's agent can search and read the docs while it works, and tell you when a page let it down. Nothing to install or configure: Tool What it returns search_docs(query, limit=10) the best matching pages and sections (ranked as the search dialog ranks them), each with its path, URL and a snippet read_page(path) one page's agent-ready Markdown; path is a page path (/docs/guide/install) or URL list_pages() every page by nav group (llms.txt) submit_feedback(path, helpful, comment?) stores a vote on a page, like a reader's "Was this page helpful?", with source: agent The first three are read-only. submit_feedback lets an agent report a page that is wrong, outdated, unclear or missing what it needed, so docs problems reach you from the agents reading them. Reports land in the same store as readers' votes, so aiui docs feedback counts them together (in the CSV and JSON exports source tells them apart), under the same limits as the page's vote button: 20 a minute per client (shared with /api/docs/feedback), 4 KiB, a 1,000-character comment, and only for pages that exist. The tool is not listed when page feedback is off (feedback: false) or posted to your own endpoint. Connect from the page menu (Copy MCP server URL, Connect to Cursor, Connect to VS Code), or add it by hand: Agents also find it on their own: /.well-known/mcp (also mcp.json and mcp/server-card.json) serves a server card with the endpoint and the tools, and llms.txt ends with an "MCP server" section linking it. The transport is Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC over POST, protocol versions 2025-03-26 to 2025-11-25) and stateless. Requests whose Host is not a name the server answers to (DNS rebinding; behind a reverse proxy on the same machine list the public name in AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS) or that come from another site's page (Origin; allow one with --cors-origins or AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) are refused. To turn the server off: A static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) runs no server, so it has no /mcp and the menu shows no MCP items; the .md pages and llms files above still work there.

aiui serve and aiui dev also answer questions about the docs, with the sections each answer came from. Set a model key in the environment and serve; there is nothing to configure: The server ranks the build's sections for the question (the same ranking as search, widened so a long question still finds its pages), sends the best six to the model and streams a Markdown answer that cites them as [1], [2]. Your key stays on the server: it is read from the environment and never logged or sent to the browser. Model setting Where content.docs.assistant.model, else AIUI_ASSISTANT_MODEL, else OPENAI_MODEL_NAME, else gpt-4o-mini which model answers OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL any OpenAI-compatible API, including a local server (OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1 needs no key) a provider/model name such as anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 goes through LiteLLM when it is installed, with that provider's key Without a key the endpoint still answers: it returns the best matching sections and says AI answers are not set up, so readers never hit an error. Key Default What it does starters none up to six questions offered before the reader asks instructions none extra rules for every answer (tone, names, scope); up to 4,000 characters model see above the model endpoint none on a static host, the ask URL of an aiui serve running the same build assistant: false turns it off. The build writes these settings into ui-config.json, which is public: keep secrets out of instructions.

When the server has a model, the docs header shows Ask AI. It opens a side panel with your starter questions; answers stream in, cite their sections as [1] links that open the page at that section, list the sections under the answer, and can be copied or stopped. Follow-up questions keep the conversation. Other ways in: Entry point What it does ⌘I / Ctrl+I opens the panel ?assistant= on any page URL opens the panel and asks; the parameter leaves the address bar select a passage in a page an Ask about this chip quotes it in the question search (⌘K) an Ask AI: row under the results a page with mode: assistant the page's text, then the panel inline: a full "Ask the docs" page window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('aiui:docs-ask', { detail: { question, context } })) from your own JavaScript A server without a key shows none of this (the API above still returns the best sections). A static host shows it only when endpoint names an aiui serve running the same build; allow the site's origin there with --cors-origins https://docs.acme.dev.

POST /api/docs/ask with {"question": "...", "context": "...", "page": "/docs/x", "history": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]} (only question is required; context is a quoted passage, history the earlier turns) answers with Server-Sent Events: Event Data sources [{"n": 1, "title", "heading", "path", "url", "snippet"}], the sections the answer may cite as [n] text {"text": "..."}, the next piece of the Markdown answer done {} unavailable {"message": "..."} instead of text when no model is set up error {"message": "..."} when the model call failed GET /api/docs/search?q=install&limit=10 returns {"results": [{"title", "heading", "anchor", "path", "url", "snippet"}]}, ranked as the search dialog ranks them, and each page's Markdown is at /docs/ .md, so another app can embed docs search and answers. The endpoints are public like the site, so they are guarded: 10 questions a minute per client, a 32 KiB body, a 2,000-character question, the same Host and Origin checks as the MCP server, and application/json or text/plain bodies (a static site on another origin posts text/plain, allowed with --cors-origins or AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS). Answers spend your key, so put a public site behind your own rate limits too.

pages.t: Analytics, support chat and cookie consent
pages.d: Add web analytics or a support chat widget to a docs site with one line per

s.x: Add web analytics or a support chat widget to a docs site with one line per provider, and ask readers for consent before anything loads. aiui build adds them to every page (the home page, each docs page and 404.html). Each client-side page change counts as a page view.

A provider takes its main id as a plain value (ga4: G-ABC1234) or a block with more settings. The build checks every id and URL and stops on a bad one. Key Settings (first one is the main id) Page views on navigation ga4 measurementId (G-...) Counted by GA4's enhanced measurement (page changes based on browser history, on by default) gtm tagId (GTM-...) Pushes {event: "aiui.pageview", page_path, page_title} to the data layer posthog apiKey (phc_...), apiHost (default https://us.i.posthog.com), sessionRecording (default false) Counted by PostHog (history_change) plausible domain, server (default https://plausible.io, or your own instance) Counted by Plausible fathom siteId Counted by Fathom (data-spa="auto") umami websiteId (a UUID), src (default https://cloud.umami.is/script.js) Counted by Umami segment key (the write key) analytics.page() mixpanel projectToken, region (us, eu or in) Counted by Mixpanel (track_pageview: "url-with-path") scripts A list of https:// script URLs for any other tool Up to the tool Support chat widgets load when the browser is idle, so they never slow the first paint: Key Settings intercom appId (calls Intercom('update') on each page change) crisp websiteId (a UUID) front chatId

With consent, nothing loads until the reader accepts. A small banner at the bottom of the page offers Decline and Accept, the same size and style, so declining is as easy as accepting. The choice is remembered in the browser's local storage (aiui-consent: granted or denied). The banner uses the site's theme colours in light and dark mode and fits a phone screen. Key Default Meaning required true consent: true is short for this; false loads without asking. banner true false: no built-in banner; your own consent tool decides (below). text, accept, decline an English sentence, Accept, Decline The banner's words. policy, policyLabel none, Privacy policy A link to your privacy page (a site path or URL). Change of mind. Any link to #cookie-settings opens the banner again, for example in the footer: Cookie settings. Declining after accepting reloads the page, so the trackers that were running stop. Your own consent tool. Set banner: false and tell the page the reader's choice from the tool's callback:

Readers whose browser sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track get no analytics (support chat still loads); respectDoNotTrack: false counts them anyway. aiui dev leaves integrations out so previews are not visits; dev: true under integrations loads them there too.

No inline script is emitted: the settings are a JSON data block and the loader is a file at the site root (/aiui-integrations.js). The build's Content Security Policy adds each provider's hosts per directive by itself (Compiler(config).external_origins() lists them). A tag manager container (gtm) loads whatever tags you add to it, so with gtm the policy is report-only until you add their hosts under site.csp and set it to enforce.

pages.d: Put a docs site behind a password, keep some pages open to everyone, and limit

s.x: Put a docs site behind a password, keep some pages open to everyone, and limit others to a group of readers. aiui serve and aiui dev enforce it; there is nothing to install and no account system to run.

s.h: A password for the whole site
s.x: Every page now asks for the password. A reader who opens any page gets a sign-in page in the site's own theme, at that URL, and lands on the page they asked for. The session lasts seven days. /__aiui/login shows who is signed in and a Sign out button (link to it from navbar.links if you want one). Passwords are always written env:NAME: the build stores the variable's name, never the password. Change the variable and restart to change the password; every reader signed in with the old one is signed out.

Most docs want a public home and quickstart and the rest behind sign-in: public lists page paths relative to the docs (/ is the home page, /docs/quickstart also works) and patterns (* matches any part of a path). A page can also say it in its front matter: public: false keeps a page behind sign-in when a pattern would open it, so public: ["*"] plus public: false on a few pages protects only those.
Readers sign in with their password alone; it tells the server who they are.

Give readers groups, then name the groups a page is for: A page with groups is for readers in at least one of them. To any other signed-in reader it does not exist: a 404, and it is missing from their sidebar, search, llms.txt, MCP and Ask AI. A signed-out reader who opens it gets the sign-in page (they may be a member).

A page's rule covers everything made from it: its HTML (including the copy inside ), its .md and .source.md files and Accept: text/markdownanswer, its social card under/og/, its Try it data and its RSS feed. docs-nav.json, search-index.json, llms.txt and llms-full.txt (and their /.well-known/ copies) hold only the pages the reader may read (so the pages do not carry the navigation, as they do on a site without sign-in, and the build writes no split search index, search-index/: search reads the cut search-index.json), and the MCP server, Ask AI, /api/docs/search and page feedback see only those pages. An AI tool that connects to /mcp without the browser's cookie reads the open pages. The sitemap lists only open pages. Code, styles, fonts, images and ui-config.json are open to anyone, so open pages render (do not put a secret in an image). Any other file (OpenAPI specs, a nav group's generated page, files you copied in) needs sign-in.

Protected answers carry Cache-Control: private, so a shared cache never hands one reader's page to another. The session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure over HTTPS (also behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-Proto). It is signed with a key derived from the reader's password. Passwords are compared in constant time. Ten wrong passwords from one address in ten minutes block that address for the rest of the ten minutes (429). Sign-in and sign-out only accept a form posted from the site itself (AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS adds origins, as for the rest of aiui). A password variable that is not set is logged as a warning; that reader cannot sign in.

Sign-in needs the aiui server. A static host (GitHub Pages, a CDN) serves every file of the build, so aiui build warns (7017) on a site with content.docs.auth; serve it with aiui serve (deployment). aiui validate reports front matter public or groups on a site without content.docs.auth, and a group no reader is in (7017). A docs folder served by aiui run uses the app's own sign-in instead (deployment).

pages.d: A docs site built with aiui build ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy

s.x: A docs site built with aiui build ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy and needs no configuration. The policy allows the scripts the site runs and nothing else, so injected markup cannot run a script, and only your own site can show the docs in a frame.

aiui build works the policy out from what the site actually loads: Source Directive The site's own files (app, chunks, fonts, customCss/customJs files, the site.components module and its import map's hash) 'self' The small inline scripts the build writes (theme, URL, redirect stubs) script-src 'sha256-…', one hash each The JSON the build inlines in each page (its Markdown, the navigation and route manifest) nothing: type="application/json" is data the browser never runs Google Fonts and font, stylesheet and script URLs in site.theme.fonts, customCss, customJs style-src, font-src, script-src Integrations (analytics, support chat) each provider's hosts YouTube, Vimeo and Loom embeds on a page frame-src (the privacy-friendly player) The servers of your OpenAPI specs (Try it) connect-src assistant.endpoint, feedback.endpoint on a static host connect-src A navbar primary button of type: github (the star count) connect-src https://api.github.com Everything else stays strict: no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' for scripts, object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self'. Images and media load from 'self', data:, blob: and any https: host, so Markdown images and badges keep working. Styles allow 'unsafe-inline': the app's code highlighting, diagrams and dialogs set inline styles. The policy goes out three ways: Every built page carries it as , right after . This works on any static host, GitHub Pages included. _headers in the build folder sends it as a header on Netlify and Cloudflare Pages, with frame-ancestors 'self' added (a meta tag cannot carry frame-ancestors). aiui serve and aiui dev send the /* headers of _headers, so the preview behaves like the host. The aiui dev reload script is a file (/__aiui/dev.js), so it runs under the same policy. On another host (nginx, S3 with CloudFront, a CDN), copy the header line from _headers into its configuration.

site.csp Effect unset On for a docs build (reported only when integrations.gtm is set, see below); off for other builds true On, enforced false Off: no meta tag, no _headers report-only Only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only in _headers and from aiui serve: the browser logs what the policy would block, and blocks nothing a map On, with extra sources per directive (a string or a list). A list with 'none' replaces the directive (frame-ancestors: ["'none'"] forbids every frame). report-only: true in the map reports instead of enforcing. report-uri sets where the browser posts reports Directive names are lower-case words (script-src, connect-src, ...) and sources contain no spaces, ; or ,: anything else is a config error, so the value is always a valid header.

customJs that calls another server (fetch, a WebSocket, a widget): add its origin under connect-src, frame-src or script-src. Raw HTML in a page needs no sources: the page renders YouTube, Vimeo and Loom players, and (all allowed above), shows any other as a link and removes , and similar elements before the policy is ever involved. aiui validate names each one (finding 7019; see raw HTML). Inline event handlers (onclick="…") never run. Tag Manager (integrations.gtm) runs whatever tags the container holds, which the build cannot see, so the default there is report-only. Add the hosts of your tags and set site.csp: true to enforce. Legacy site.plugins: mermaid and syntax-highlight load from their CDN, which the policy allows when they are listed. Other dashboard plugins are not meant for docs pages. To find what a page needs, open the browser console: every blocked load or script is logged with the directive that blocked it. report-only shows the same messages without blocking anything.

pages.d: Every aiui command and option. aiui --help prints the same

s.x: Every aiui command and option. aiui --help prints the same information from the installed version. The wheel also installs the command as praisonaiui. For a short tour of the commands you will use most, see CLI Usage.

Run the server for a Python app (app.py) or a YAML chat agent (chat.yaml). Option Default Description APP_FILE required A Python file that registers callbacks, or a .yaml/.yml chat config --port, -p 8000 Port. If it is taken, the next free port (up to 10 further) is used. The port is bound before the URL is printed and the server serves that socket, so two apps started together never get the same port --host 127.0.0.1 Address to bind to --reload, -r off Restart when files change --style, -s detected app (the React app shell, default), chat (the classic chat), docs, agents, playground, dashboard (legacy) or custom --preset minimal for app.py Page preset: minimal (Chat + your pages), agent (Chat, Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory), or ops (all built-in ops pages) --pages none Explicit comma-separated page IDs (e.g. chat,sessions), all, or a preset name (minimal, agent, ops) --backend, -b standalone standalone, or praisonai to use the PraisonAI WebSocket gateway --datastore, -d sdk Session storage: sdk (shared with PraisonAI Agents), sdk:/path, json, json:/path or memory. Without the flag, a chat YAML's datastore: key is used --config, -c none A docs-site YAML to build before serving (optional) --output, -o aiui Folder the UI files are written to; by default next to APP_FILE Style: for a Python app --style wins, then aiui.set_style(); for a YAML app its style: key wins over --style. Without any of them aiui run detects one: @aiui.profiles plus registered agents gives agents, and anything else (including @aiui.reply and @aiui.page) opens app (the React app shell). For Python app.py files that do not call aiui.set_pages(), aiui run defaults to the minimal preset (Chat + your own pages) unless --preset, --pages, or AIUI_PAGES is set. In app, aiui run opens the chat layout (the chat without a canvas) unless AIUI_LAYOUT, aiui.set_layout() or YAML layout: picks another. See UI Styles, Layouts, and Build a focused app. A chat YAML's top-level keys: name, instructions, model, welcome, goodbye, starters, profiles, tools, features, datastore, style, theme, branding, dashboard, pages, layout and extensions. layout: takes a layout id (layout: command) or the same block as aiui.yaml (default, available, user_choice, primary, options); extensions: takes enabled: / disabled: lists, as in aiui.yaml. Any other key prints a warning naming it, since it would otherwise be ignored without a word. aiui run loads ~/.praisonai/.env and then ./.env before starting, without overriding variables that are already set.

Scaffold a starter Python Agent UI (app.py) or a Docs UI config (aiui.yaml) in the current folder. Refuses to overwrite existing files unless --force is given. Option Default Description --template, -t minimal App templates (writes app.py): agent, openai, anthropic, langgraph, crewai, pydantic-ai, praisonai, dashboard. Docs templates (writes aiui.yaml): minimal, docs, marketing --force, -f off Overwrite existing files --frontend off Also scaffold a Vite + React + shadcn frontend project For docs templates, the file's first line (# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json) gives autocomplete and hover docs in editors (Editor setup). Create the folder it points to (for the docs template, ./docs with at least one .md file) before aiui build.

Check a docs-site configuration and its pages. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --strict off Unknown keys, broken links, nav entries without a page and content issues (7xxx) become errors (exit 1) --format text json prints {valid, errors, warnings}, each with code, file, line, message, suggestion Each finding prints as [category] code file:line: message with a fix hint under it: Code Finding 1003 unknown key (ignored); in a $ref file the file is named 1004 key accepted but has no effect; unknown component tag in a page 2101 a nav entry names no docs page 2102 a navigation tab, menu item, anchor or dropdown with no pages, groups or href 5001, 51xx, 5201 theme, layout and search settings that are ignored 6001, 6002 broken link or missing image (aiui docs check-links); OpenAPI spec problems 7000 page front matter is not valid YAML (the page loses its title) 7001 front matter key has the wrong type (keys) 7002 image without alt text (`, with noalt;alt="" marks a decorative image) 7003 two files publish the same page URL (intro.md and 01-intro.md) 7004 two sidebar entries in one folder have the same title 7005 heading skips a level (## then ####) 7006 page has nothing beyond its headings 7007 {{name}} with no value under variables: (variables) 7008 snippet not found, outside the project folder, or including itself (fails aiui build) 7009 icon (front matter, navigation, a component's icon="…") that is not a lucide name, an emoji or an image URL, with the nearest name 7010 a redirect loops, or ends at a docs path with no page (redirects) 7011 a page is published at a redirect's source, so the redirect never runs 7012 front matter openapi: / api: or a navigation METHOD /path entry that names no operation in the loaded specs (OpenAPI) 7013 front matter related names a page that does not exist (related pages) 7014 a site.customCss, site.customJs, site.theme.fonts or site.theme.codeLanguages file that is not in the project folder (fonts and custom files) 7015 site.theme.code names a theme that is not bundled (with the nearest name), or a site.theme.codeLanguages file is not a TextMate grammar (code blocks) 7016 a ::: module block names no module or member, or has an unknown option (fails aiui build; Python API reference) 7017 content.docs.auth is set, and only aiui serve / aiui dev enforce it (aiui build); front matter public / groups without content.docs.auth, or a group no reader is in (docs sign-in) 7018 two navigation.versions with the same name, more than one marked default: true, or a version that lists a page of another version's folder (versions) 7019 raw HTML a page shows differently than written: an that is not a YouTube, Vimeo or Loom video (shown as a link; the host is named), or , , , , , , (removed). Also an aiui build warning (raw HTML) 7020 two navigation.languages with the same code, more than one marked default: true, or a version folder inside a language folder (docs/fr/v1/; languages) 7021 site.components is not a .js / .mjs file in the project folder, or the build finds no component tag in it (your own components) 7022 a class on a component tag or raw HTML that docs pages drop (not a docs utility class; the nearest allowed one is suggested), or a style attribute (always removed). Also an aiui build warning (styling with classes) 7101 site.theme.accent under WCAG AA 3:1 contrast on the light or dark background, with a shade that passes 7102 logo, favicon or site.theme.background image that is not a file in the project folder (branding) Without --config, validate, build and serve read ./aiui.yaml. The old name aiui.template.yaml still works: when it is the only one there it is used, with a one-line hint on stderr to rename it, and the exit code is unchanged. When both files exist, aiui.yaml wins. An explicit --config always wins and prints no hint. See Config file name.

Print the JSON Schema of aiui.yaml, generated from the Config model of the installed version; --output, -o writes it to a file. The schema is also published at https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json; see Editor setup.

Build a static docs site from the configuration. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --output, -o aiui Output folder --minify off Minify the JSON manifests --strict off Stop with exit code 1 on a broken link (without it, broken links are warnings) The output holds index.html, 404.html, the UI bundle (assets/, aiui-manifest.json), the manifests (ui-config.json, docs-nav.json, route-manifest.json), one HTML file and the Markdown source per page, robots.txt and .nojekyll. sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt are added when the site URL is known (seo.siteUrl, or a CNAME file next to the configuration or in docs/).

Find broken page links, #anchors, images, component hrefs and nav entries before you deploy. Prints file:line: target: reason (did you mean X?) and exits 1 when a link is broken. See Writing docs pages → Check links. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file --external off Also request every http(s) URL (HEAD, then GET; 16 at a time) --timeout 10 Seconds to wait for each external URL --json off Print {"checked", "pages", "broken": [{file, line, target, reason, suggestion}]}

Build (unless --no-build) and serve a docs site. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --output, -o aiui Folder to serve --port, -p 8000 Port (next free port if taken) --host 127.0.0.1 Address to bind to --no-build off Serve the existing output without building --watch, -w off Rebuild when a file in the configuration's folder changes (reload the page yourself; aiui dev reloads it for you) --cors-origins empty Comma-separated allowed origins; empty means same-origin only --ssl-certfile none Certificate file for HTTPS --ssl-keyfile none Private key file for HTTPS --open / --no-open auto Open the site in a browser. Auto opens it only when run from a terminal; never in CI, under a test runner or from a script (when a browser opens) Paths without a file extension fall back to the single-page app. Paths that try to leave the output folder are refused. Every response carries the /* headers of the build's _headers file, which holds the site's Content Security Policy. #### When a browser opens aiui serve, aiui dev and aiui dev --examples open a browser tab only for a person at a terminal. With neither flag, the tab opens when standard output is a terminal and no CI or test runner is detected (CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, BUILDKITE, PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST). --open forces it, --no-open skips it, and AIUI_NO_BROWSER=1 turns it off everywhere, for scripts and coding agents that start these servers.

Preview the docs site while you write it: build, serve, and reload the open browser tab on every save. A failed build is shown in the terminal and over the page while the last good build stays up. Run it in the folder that holds aiui.yaml, or in a folder with only a docs/ folder. See Hot Reload. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --port, -p 8000 Port (next free port if taken) --host 127.0.0.1 Address to bind to --open / --no-open auto Open the preview in a browser; auto as for aiui serve (when a browser opens) --base-path as aiui build URL path to preview the site under --examples, -e none Run the examples dashboard for this folder instead (default port 9000) aiui dev --examples examples is the older dashboard that lists the example projects in a folder and switches between them. In a folder with no configuration and no docs/ but an examples/ folder, plain aiui dev still opens it.

Command Options Description aiui doctor --server, -s (default http://127.0.0.1:8000), --json Structured diagnostics against a running server. The first two checks need no server: aiui Version (the imported version against PyPI's latest) and aiui Install (the version and folder actually imported; warns when pip's metadata names another version, as a stale editable install does, and prints the reinstall command) aiui health-check --server, -s, --detailed, -d Server health; --detailed shows each feature aiui health same Alias of health-check aiui test --server, -s (default http://127.0.0.1:8082) Integration tests against a running server: chat, memory, sessions, endpoints, features, all. See API Testing

--config applies the extensions: policy from that YAML. doctor checks the entry point, the SDK version gate, static_dir and SRI hashes, and (unless --no-builtin) page ids that a built-in page shadows. A plugin's own commands run as aiui ... or aiui plugins ...; AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 turns that lookup off. See UI plugins.
These talk to a running server over HTTP. Every one takes --server, -s URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8000).
Runtime configuration (stored in config.yaml under the data directory).
A2UI surfaces for the agent canvas; see A2UI Overview.
Manage in-app notifications (NotificationStoreProtocol, REST + SSE); see Notifications.
Inspect live HTTP latency, throughput, memory, and recorded metrics.
aiui auth create-secret prints a new session secret (offline; see Sessions); aiui auth create-key --name my-app creates an API key on the running server and prints it once.
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Invalid configuration, failed request or other error 2 File or folder not found, or an unknown --style 3 Build failed 4 No free port near the requested one

Variable Effect AIUI_DATA_DIR Data directory (default ~/.praisonaiui): sessions, runtime config.yaml, plugin state AIUI_SHELL app turns the dashboard style into the React app shell; legacy turns app back into dashboard AIUI_LAYOUT Default app-shell layout id; see Layouts AIUI_TEMPLATES_DIR Serve or build with another frontend bundle folder AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Origins allowed for cross-site requests and WebSockets (comma-separated, or *) AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS Extra host names a loopback or private-address server answers AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN Require the URL token on every request AUTH_ENFORCE true gates every route and WebSocket behind auth AIUI_AUTH_SECRET Session signing secret (comma-separated to rotate: first signs, all verify); default a generated /auth_secret AIUI_SESSION_LIFETIME How long a sign-in lasts while unused (14d default, 12h, 3600); overrides YAML auth.sessionLifetime AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD 1 stops loading plugin CLI commands PRAISONAI_MODEL Default model for built-in agent features (default gpt-4o-mini) OPENAI_API_KEY Used by agent features and examples that call OpenAI The security variables are described in Deployment.

pages.d: Reference for import praisonaiui as aiui.

s.x: Reference for import praisonaiui as aiui.
These functions configure the server. Call them at module level in your app.py, before the server starts.

Set the UI style. Parameter Type Values style str "app" (the React app shell), "chat" (the classic chat), "dashboard", "agents", "playground", "docs", "custom" Priority under aiui run: CLI --style, then set_style(), then auto-detection (a plain chat app gets app). See UI Styles.

Choose which pages the app shows besides its own, in every style. The list covers built-in pages, the app shell's layout pages (start, artifacts, templates, connect, api-reference, ...) and dashboard-plugin folders, including the ones in ~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins that every app on the machine would otherwise share. Pages the app registers itself (@aiui.page(), register_page, register_plugin) and installed entry-point plugins always appear. Without set_pages every page shows. An id that names no page is reported with a warning at startup. Use aiui pages ids to see all available page IDs, or inspect aiui.PAGE_PRESETS for the built-in preset definitions (minimal, agent, ops). aiui.set_pages("all") / aiui.set_pages("ops") (or aiui run app.py --preset ops / --pages all) shows every page and makes every layout's sidebar list them all, grouped (Agent, Work, Control, ...), as the legacy dashboard did: each page in its React version where there is one, otherwise the legacy view inside the app shell. The layout picker keeps working. aiui run --pages chat,sessions is the same as set_pages(["chat", "sessions"]). The app's own pages (register_page, @aiui.page) are listed in their group in every layout's sidebar, not only under More (⌘K).
Shorthand for set_pages(list(keep)): aiui.only_my_pages() shows only the app's own pages, aiui.only_my_pages("chat") adds Chat.

s.h: aiui.create_shell_app(*, config=None, pages=None, plugins=None, routes=None, csp=None, require_auth=False, config_path=None)
s.x: Build a minimal Starlette ASGI app that mounts only the React app shell, selected pages, plugin assets/routes, and caller-supplied routes — without mounting agent server endpoints (/sessions, /run, /agents, /teams, /api/chat/*) or the 48 backend agent features (unmatched paths return 404). Pass csp="strict" (a directive dict, or (html, hashes) -> str) to attach a strict Content-Security-Policy header with exact 'sha256-…' hashes for the shell's executable inline scripts. Related helpers: aiui.render_shell_html(request=None, *, style="app") → (html, inline_script_hashes) aiui.shell_inline_script_hashes(html) → sorted 'sha256-…' tuple (skips type="application/json" and src="…") aiui.shell_csp_header(html, *, base=None, extra=None) → rendered Content-Security-Policy header value See Build a focused app → Mount only the shell.

Configure the sidebar branding (title text and logo). Parameter Type Default title str "PraisonAI" logo str "" (no logo: the PraisonAI brand glyph) logo is an image URL or path (/static/logo.svg, https://…, data:image/…) or a short text mark. Left empty, every UI draws the PraisonAI glyph on the accent tile. Also configurable via config.yaml:

Set the persistence backend for sessions and messages. Without a call, the server uses the SDK store shared with PraisonAI Agents (SDKFileDataStore, from praisonaiui.datastore_sdk), falling back to JSONFileDataStore. aiui run --datastore sets the same thing from the command line.
Set the AI provider for chat completions.

Register an agent object (for example a PraisonAI Agents Agent) under a name. Together with an @aiui.profiles callback, registered agents make aiui run pick the agents style. Agents created in the dashboard's Agents page are a separate store (/api/agents/definitions).
Remove a page from the sidebar.

Pause the agent and wait for the user to answer. Preferred entry point for interactive agent flows — supersedes the legacy AskUserMessage class. Parameter Type Description question str Text shown to the user. options list[str] \ None Optional list of choices. When given, the user picks one; otherwise they type free text. timeout float Seconds to wait before giving up. Default 300 (5 min). Returns a PromptResult dataclass (text, choice, message_id). The result is truthy when the user answered, falsy on timeout. The answer comes back over the chat WebSocket (ask_response), so a question needs the WebSocket transport; the HTTP fallback (POST /run) can show it but not answer it. Time spent waiting for the answer does not count against the @reply inactivity timeout (AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT). aiui.ask and AskUserMessage work the same way.
Emit an error message to the chat. A thin helper around Message with metadata={"kind": "error"} — keeps the public surface small.

s.h: aiui.configure(*, datastore=None, branding=None, theme=None, chat=None, custom_css=None, custom_js=None, style=None)
s.x: One call for the common setters. Every keyword is optional; each one is forwarded to the matching set_* function, which you can still call directly. Parameter Type Description datastore str Storage backend: "memory", "json", "json:/path", "sdk", "sdk:/path". branding dict Forwarded to set_branding(...). Keys: title, logo (any other key raises TypeError). theme dict Forwarded to set_theme(...). Keys: preset, dark/dark_mode, radius; brand_color goes to set_brand_color(). chat dict feedback goes to set_feedback_enabled(), mode to set_chat_mode(), other keys to set_chat_features(). custom_css str CSS text, passed to set_custom_css() unchanged. It is not read from a file: pass Path("styles.css").read_text() to use one. custom_js str \ Path Path to a JS file; same as set_custom_js. style str UI style — "chat", "dashboard", etc.

Handle incoming chat messages. This is the core callback. Annotate the parameter as str (async def on_reply(message: str)) to get the text only. Otherwise the callback gets a MessageContext with: message.text (alias message.content): the user's text message.session_id: the session id message.agent_name: the selected agent, if any message.attachments: the files sent with the message, [{id, name, content_type, path}] (see Attachments) How a reply ends: If the callback raises, the run ends with one run_error frame carrying the exception text. The chat shows the error under whatever was streamed, the reply is saved with status: "error" (so it is still there after a reload), the run ledger counts it as failed, and the traceback is logged. Stop (chat_abort, POST /api/chat/abort, POST /cancel) cancels the callback task: the callback gets asyncio.CancelledError at its next await, so an LLM call or tool it is waiting on stops too. A callback that sends nothing (no token, message, step or tool event) for AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT seconds (default 600) is cancelled and the run fails with a timeout. Set AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0 for no limit.

The greeting on a new, empty chat. The chat runs it through POST /welcome once per page load and shows what it says (aiui.say, or streamed tokens) as plain text on the empty thread: in the app shell's chat and every layout, the chat style and the dashboard's chat. In a layout's new-chat hero (the site's mark and name) the greeting takes the place of the generic "Ask anything…" line, with the starters below it. It is not saved to the conversation. A chat YAML's welcome: key registers one for you.

Runs when a chat's last browser connection closes, after any reply still running there finishes, as that chat (aiui.user_session is readable): use it for clean-up. Nobody is listening any more, so what it sends is dropped.

Each moment of a chat has a handler. The names are aliases: @aiui.on_message and @aiui.reply register the same handler (the last one registered wins). Decorator Runs Same as @aiui.on_message For each message the user sends; gets the MessageContext (message.content). @aiui.reply @aiui.on_chat_start Once per chat, right before its first reply (again after on_chat_end ran for it). @aiui.on_stop When the user presses Stop, as the stopped chat. @aiui.cancel @aiui.on_chat_end When the chat ends (above). @aiui.goodbye @aiui.author_rename Maps an author (agent) name to the name the chat shows. @aiui.welcome The greeting on an empty chat, once per page load (no chat yet). Every handler may be async def or a plain def. on_chat_start runs in the reply's task (so aiui.say and aiui.Message work) and needs a reply handler; if it raises, that turn fails with the error and the next turn runs it again. author_rename is called once per name per reply (a failing handler keeps the name); the display name goes on every frame of the reply (agent_name) and the saved reply, never on the agent the user picked. @aiui.resume is not called yet (below).

pages.d: The aiui.yaml schema: what aiui validate checks and aiui build

s.x: The aiui.yaml schema: what aiui validate checks and aiui build compiles. The source of truth is schema/models.py (Config). The runtime state file of a running server is a different file; see Runtime Persistence below.

aiui validate, aiui build and aiui serve find the file in this order: --config, when given. It always wins and prints nothing extra. ./aiui.yaml. ./aiui.template.yaml, the old name. It still works; the command prints one dim line on stderr and its exit code does not change: Using aiui.template.yaml; rename it to aiui.yaml (the old name keeps working). When both files exist, aiui.yaml is used and the command says so in one line (Using aiui.yaml; aiui.template.yaml is also here and is ignored.). With neither, the command stops with Configuration file not found: aiui.yaml. aiui init writes aiui.yaml and refuses to overwrite either name without --force. aiui dev reads either name, and aiui dev --examples accepts either name in each example folder. aiui.yml is not looked up; pass it with --config.

Any mapping can live in its own file. $ref names a YAML (or JSON) file, relative to the file that holds the $ref: Included files can include others; keys written next to $ref override the included ones. Paths stay inside the folder of aiui.yaml; a file that includes itself, directly or through others, is an error ($ref cycle: aiui.yaml -> config/nav.yaml -> aiui.yaml). Errors name the file and line of the $ref (aiui.yaml:6: $ref './config/nav.yaml' not found); a YAML error or an unknown key inside an included file names that file. validate, build, serve, docs check-links and the server all read includes.

aiui init starts aiui.yaml with this line: Editors that run the YAML language server (VS Code with the Red Hat YAML extension, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, Zed) then complete keys, show each key's description on hover and underline wrong values as you type; add the line to an existing aiui.yaml for the same. The schema is generated from the Config model, so it never drifts from aiui validate. For the exact installed version (offline, or pinned), run aiui schema -o aiui.schema.json and use $schema=./aiui.schema.json.

Key What it sets Page schemaVersion Schema version (1) below site Title, description, theme, logo, custom CSS below, Theming style UI style (docs by default for a site) UI Styles content Where the Markdown lives Content Sources components, templates, routes Layout of each page below, Templates, Slots navigation, navbar, footer, logo, search Docs site chrome Navigation seo, i18n, a11y Meta tags, locales, accessibility switches SEO, i18n layout Chat position, and the app shell's layouts Layouts chat, auth, dashboard, widgets, extensions Chat, sign-in, dashboard and plugin settings Deployment, Plugins dependencies shadcn components to install at build time below aiui validate --strict turns unknown keys into errors.
Always specify the schema version:
Note: The ui field is a theming hint. Components are UI-agnostic and use CSS classes you can style with any framework.

Auto-install shadcn components at build time: When you run aiui build, missing components are installed with npx shadcn@latest add into the frontend source (src/frontend in a repository checkout). This only matters when you build the frontend yourself; the bundled React app does not change.

editLink, lastUpdated and feedback draw the page footer; see Writing docs pages → Page footer. related is the related pages list. mcp is the docs MCP server and assistant is Ask AI. indexFiles and nav (mode, sort, collapsible, maxDepth) are accepted but not read by the build yet; see Navigation.
Define reusable components:
Type Description Header Site header with logo, nav, CTA Footer Site footer DocsSidebar Documentation sidebar navigation Toc Table of contents DocContent Rendered markdown content
Templates combine a layout with slot assignments:

Layout Description ThreeColumnLayout Sidebar + Content + TOC TwoColumnLayout Sidebar + Content CenteredLayout Centered content, no sidebar FullWidthLayout Full width content FlexibleLayout WordPress-style widget zones
Place widgets in layout zones without modifying markdown: Zones, the widgets and which layouts render them: Widget Zones.

Map URL patterns to templates: Route matching uses glob patterns: * - one path segment ** - any number of segments The first matching route wins, so list specific routes before broad ones. A route's slots can override only the right slot in the docs site (right: null hides the table of contents); header and footer are read from the template, so per-route overrides of them have no effect.

Single source of truth for all runtime feature state. In addition to aiui.yaml (which drives static site generation), PraisonAIUI uses a unified runtime config file, config.yaml in the data directory (AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui/). This file stores all feature state — agents, channels, guardrails, schedules, and runtime settings — in a single YAML file that persists across server restarts. This is compatible with the gateway.yaml schema used by praisonai gateway start --config.

All CRUD operations (dashboard, REST API, CLI) automatically write back to this file: Feature Section Written On Config Runtime runtime_config PATCH, PUT, DELETE, apply Guardrails guardrails Register Channels channels Add, update, delete Schedules schedules Add, remove, update Agents agents Create, update, delete Atomic writes: a temp file and os.replace() prevent corruption. Hot reload: the Config Hot-Reload watcher, once started, reloads this file after external edits. Secrets: channel secrets are written as env:VAR_NAME references (a _ref key works too); the server refuses an inline token that looks like a secret and redacts secrets in API responses. Rule of thumb: secrets (API keys, tokens) go in environment variables; preferences (model, theme, branding) in the config file.

File Purpose Used By aiui.yaml Static site layout, components, routes aiui build, aiui serve, aiui validate $AIUI_DATA_DIR/config.yaml Runtime feature state (agents, channels, config) aiui run, dashboard API gateway.yaml Subset of config.yaml (legacy compatibility) praisonai gateway start

Parameter Type Required Description children Sequence[dict] ✅ List of component dicts refresh_every float ❌ App shell: re-fetch the page every N seconds while visible (_refresh_every) params dict ❌ In an action reply: values written into the page URL's query string (_params) Returns: dict with _components key — triggers structured rendering in the frontend.
