A data table. In the app shell it sorts by header click, formats typed columns, and can search, page, link rows and open a row in a side panel. The old call shape keeps working unchanged. A larger table with typed columns, dict rows and search: Parameter Type Required Description headers Sequence[str] ✅ unless columns Column header labels rows Sequence[Sequence \ dict] ✅ Row arrays in column order, or dicts keyed by column key (sent as arrays) columns Sequence[str \ dict] — Column config (below). Gives the headers when headers is not set row_ids Sequence[str] — Stable unique ID per row. Makes rows selectable by click, Enter or Space actions Sequence[str] — Row action button labels (requires row_ids) searchable bool — A search box that keeps the rows holding every typed word (in the browser) page_size int — Rows per page; 0 shows every row. Unset: 50 per page once there are more than 100 rows sortable bool — False turns header sorting off. Default on row_href_key str — Key (in dict rows, or a column key) holding each row's link. The first cell becomes the link and a click on the row opens it row_detail bool — A click (or Enter) on a row opens a side panel listing the row's fields detail_key str — Key in dict rows holding a list of block dicts the side panel renders instead of the fields (implies row_detail) detail_load_key str — Key in dict rows holding a lazy section key loaded via POST /api/pages/{id}/action ({"_lazy": key, "_params": ...}) when that row's side panel opens (implies row_detail) detail_load str — Prefix for lazy row detail keys (f"{detail_load}{row_id_or_index}"; implies row_detail) max_height int \ str — Height of the scrolling body (px or CSS length, 0 for none). Default 70vh, so the header stays in view caption str — Accessible name of the table and its search box Column dict keys: key, label, type, format, decimals, tones, tone_above, tone_below, thresholds, href_key, width (px or CSS length), align (left, center, right) and sortable (False for one column). A plain string is a column whose key and label are that string. type Cell value Shows auto (default) anything Text as sent; a column of numbers lines up at the end; {"text", "href"} is a link and {"src", "alt"} an image text any The value as text number number (or {"value", "tone"}) Right-aligned, tabular figures. format: compact (1.2k, 3.4M), percent (a fraction: 0.123 → 12.3%), multiplier or x (2.3x), fixed (exactly decimals, default 2); none groups digits. decimals sets the fraction digits. Optional threshold colouring: tone_above (number or [n, tone], default success), tone_below (number or [n, tone], default error), or ordered thresholds: [{"gte": 1, "tone": "success"}, {"lt": 0.5, "tone": "error"}] link {"text", "href", "external"} or a URL; or text with the column's href_key A link. Only http(s), mailto, tel and relative URLs are kept badge text, or {"text", "tone"} A badge; tones maps a value to success, warning, error or info tag a list (or comma-separated text) One badge per item, toned like badge image URL, or {"src", "alt"} A small rounded thumbnail (format: "wide" for 16:9); alt defaults to the column label progress 0..1 A bar and its percent date ISO text, or epoch seconds or ms Nov 22, 2026 in UTC; format: "datetime" adds the time, "iso" gives 2026-11-22. Sorts by time sparkline a list of numbers A small trend line (no axes); sorts by the last point A header click sorts ascending, descending, then back to the server's order: stable, numeric-aware (1,234, 1.2k, 12%, 2.5x), empty cells last; headers are buttons with aria-sort. On a phone the table scrolls sideways. The legacy dashboard style draws the dict as a plain text table. With row_ids, the dashboard renderer emits bubbling DOM events from the table, so a custom view can own query state (search, filters, page, sort) and react to rows: Event detail aiui:table-select {rowId, index} aiui:table-action {action, rowId} Because events carry the stable rowId, selection stays correct after the server re-sorts or filters rows. Loading, empty and error states compose from existing components (aiui.skeleton(), aiui.empty(), aiui.alert()):
A text block. Parameter Type Required Description content str ✅ Text content

A chart with tooltips, colours from the theme's --chart-1..5 tokens (light and dark) and the full width of its column, down to a phone. The chart library loads in its own chunk the first time a page shows a chart. Parameter Type Default Description title str "" Chart title data list[dict] [] Rows, e.g. [{"month": "Jan", "views": 1200}]. A histogram also takes plain numbers chart_type str "bar" bar (columns), barh (horizontal bars), line, area, scatter, pie, donut, histogram, heatmap, sparkline kind str — Alias of chart_type x str first text column Category key. Scatter: the x value (default: first numeric column). Histogram: the measured value y str \ list[str] every numeric column Series key, or keys for several series y2 str — A secondary series drawn as faint bars on its own scale (bar, barh, line, area) labels dict[str, str] — Display names for keys in the legend and tooltip label str — Scatter: key naming each point in the tooltip tooltip list[str \ dict] — Extra row keys (or {"key", "label", "format"} dicts) shown in the tooltip (including scatter & heatmap) stacked bool False Stack the series (bar, barh, area) reference number, list of numbers, {value, label} or a list of them — Dashed reference lines (a vertical line on barh) color_by_reference bool False Bars at or above the first reference keep the series colour; bars below it are muted x_format, y_format str — number (1,234.5), compact (1.2k, 3.4M), percent (0.25 → 25%), multiplier (1.5x), duration (seconds → 1:05). Axis ticks default to compact, tooltips to number x_domain, y_domain [min, max] auto X / value axis range, e.g. x_domain=[1e3, 1e7] on scatter or y_domain=[0, 1] with y_format="percent" x_scale, y_scale str "linear" "linear" or "log" (non-positive values are omitted safely) clip bool \ number \ [min, max] — Clamp outliers to x_domain/y_domain (True), an upper cap (number), or [min, max] (histogram edge bins show ≤/+; heatmap colour scale clamps to bounds) bins int Sturges' rule (max 30) Histogram bin count height int 240 Plot height in px; barh grows with its rows, pie and donut are 260 caption str — A line of muted text under the chart legend bool more than one series Show the legend value str "value" Heatmap: the cell value key. x is the column key and y the row key (defaults x and y) facet str — Key whose values split the rows into small charts in a responsive grid (at most 24 panels) facet_scales str "shared" "shared" (one value scale across all panels) or "free" (each panel scales to its own data) Heatmap. Columns and rows keep the order they first appear in data, so sort the rows (Mon..Sun, 0..23) before passing them; a repeated cell sums. Cells are coloured on a sequential scale from the theme's first chart colour (light and dark), empty cells are outlined, y_format formats the values in the tooltip and the colour scale under the grid, and y_domain fixes the scale. Cells keep a minimum width, so a wide grid scrolls sideways inside the chart on a phone. Sparkline. One series, no axes, the last value printed beside it; height defaults to 48 px. A number list under a metric is aiui.metric(..., sparkline=[...]). Small multiples. With facet, each panel is 160 px high (48 for a sparkline) unless height is set, panels follow first-seen order, and the legend is shown once. y_domain overrides the shared scale. An unknown chart_type or format raises ValueError. A dict written by hand ({"type": "chart", "data": [...], "chart_type": "line"}) works too: missing keys are inferred from the first row, and column, hbar and doughnut are accepted as kind names. At most 5,000 rows are drawn. The legacy dashboard style shows a summary card instead of the chart.

s.h: aiui.metric(label, *, value, delta, delta_color, caption, sparkline, benchmark, benchmark_label)
s.x: A metric card with optional delta indicator and caption. benchmark compares a numeric value with a reference: a ratio of 2 or more reads as a multiple ("17x below median"), a smaller one as a percentage ("25% above median"), and it is coloured like a delta (delta_color applies, so "inverse" makes "above" the loss). sparkline draws the numbers as a tiny trend line under the value. A delta that starts with +/↑ or -/↓ (or a signed number) is coloured as a gain or a loss. Use caption for a neutral note under the value, so a subtitle such as "-2 from plan" is not coloured by accident. Parameter Type Required Default Description label str ✅ — Metric label value Any ✅ — Main metric value delta str ❌ None Change indicator (e.g. "+5%") delta_color str ❌ "normal" "normal" (rise is good), "inverse" (fall is good, e.g. "-3 days"), or "off" (never coloured) caption str ❌ None Neutral note under the value, never coloured. help is an alias sparkline list[float] ❌ None Numbers drawn as a tiny trend line under the value benchmark float ❌ None Reference the value is compared with ("17x below median") benchmark_label str ❌ "benchmark" Name of the benchmark in that line

Default: fit the content csp str ❌ None Content-Security-Policy for the frame, replacing the default below trusted bool ❌ False Render inline in the page instead of in a frame, sanitised (see below) title str ❌ None Accessible name of the frame (default "Embedded content") Security model Default (sandboxed frame). In the app shell the content renders in an built from srcdoc, without allow-same-origin. Its scripts run in an opaque origin: they cannot read or change the app's page, cookies, localStorage or session, cannot call /api/* as the signed-in user, cannot open pop-ups, submit forms or navigate the top window. A also blocks network access. The default policy is default-src 'none'; img-src data: https:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'. Pass csp= to tighten or loosen it; the frame sizes itself with a small inline script, so a policy without script-src 'unsafe-inline' needs a fixed height. trusted=True (inline). The content is placed in the page through the sanitised Markdown pipeline (rehype-sanitize): scripts, event handlers, style, and are removed. Use it for simple markup (tables, lists, links) that should flow with the page text; use the default frame for SVG and anything with scripts. Never put untrusted text into raw HTML yourself. Escape values you interpolate (html.escape(...)) even inside the frame: an injected script cannot reach the app, but it can still change what the frame shows. Legacy dashboard style. html renders in the same sandboxed frame (fixed height, default 320 px). html_embed there still sets the HTML directly on the page, where scripts and inline handlers run: pass only content you wrote. #### Theme variables These CSS custom properties are defined on the page in both themes and copied into every html frame, where they follow light/dark changes live: Variable Meaning --aiui-fg Body text --aiui-muted Secondary text, axis labels --aiui-border Hairlines, grid lines --aiui-bg Page background --aiui-surface Card / panel background --aiui-accent Brand accent (follows the theme preset) --aiui-success / --aiui-warning / --aiui-danger / --aiui-info Status colours --aiui-font / --aiui-font-mono Font stacks The frame's body already uses --aiui-fg and --aiui-font and has a transparent background, so plain HTML matches the page.

On submit the form POSTs every input by name (else label) as JSON to /api/pages/{page}/action, handled by @aiui.register_page_action(action); action is normally the page id. If the handler returns a block tree (aiui.layout([...]), i.e. {"_components": [...]}) the page re-renders with it; a reply with message shows a toast instead. submit_on_change=True submits whenever an input changes: right away for selects, pills, chips, checkboxes and dates, 400 ms after the last keystroke for text. A submit with the same values as the last one is skipped, and a change made while one is in flight posts once more when it returns. s.h: aiui.filter_bar(action, *, inputs, chips, defaults, reset_label, method, update_url)
s.x: Parameter Type Required Default Description action str ❌ "" Action id (normally the page id; optional with method="get") inputs Sequence[dict] ✅ — Input components chips bool ❌ True Show active filters as removable chips defaults dict ❌ None Reset value per input name ({"start", "end"} for a date range) reset_label str ❌ "Reset" Label of the control that clears all filters method str ❌ "post" "get" writes filter values into the page URL and re-fetches page data (no action handler needed) update_url bool ❌ False With method="post", also write submitted values into the page URL after a successful action A compact wrapping row (a search landmark) that posts like form with submit_on_change. Under it, each active filter is a chip ("Channel: Ann ×", one chip per value of a list); the × posts the form with that filter reset, and Reset posts all of them reset. A filter is active when its value differs from its reset value: defaults[name], else the first option of a select, radio or single segmented input, else empty; number and slider inputs only when defaults names them. Chips are read from the values the server sent, so the handler must return the page rebuilt from the posted values. A full example: examples/python/32-filter-page/app.py. tags_input, date_range_input, segmented_input and filter_bar render in the app shell (the default style); the legacy dashboard style shows them as JSON.

pages.t: API Reference page and OpenAPI document
pages.d: The running server describes its own HTTP API at /api/openapi.json and lets you try every route from the app.

s.x: Every aiui server publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document of its own HTTP API, and the app shell has a page to read it and send requests. Nothing to configure: both are on by default. GET /api/openapi.json is built from the route table the server is running, when it is asked. It lists every API route it answers (/api/*, /v1/* and the unprefixed data routes such as /sessions and /run): the core, each enabled built-in, and the routes of your plugins and register_feature() features. It cannot go stale, and a built-in you switch off (extensions: {disabled: [builtin.training]}) leaves it. Field Comes from tags The built-in that owns the route (sessions, api, config…), a plugin's or feature's name, else core summary, description The handler's docstring: first line, then the rest (plain text; a leading POST /path — is dropped) parameters Path parameters and their types ({id:int} is an integer) security Bearer token; [] on the public routes (/api/health, sign-in) servers /: the server that served the document x-websockets The WebSocket routes (/api/chat/ws, /api/logs/stream) The route needs the same credentials as every other /api route in each auth mode. A plugin the caller may not use (an entry-point plugin that is off by default on a remote or sign-in server) is left out. Switch the document and the page off with extensions: {disabled: [builtin.api-reference]}. Use it anywhere an OpenAPI file goes: client generators, API tools, or the API reference of an aiui docs site (api: {openapi: http://localhost:8000/api/openapi.json}, see OpenAPI).

A feature adds request bodies, responses or anything else to its operations with an optional openapi() method, keyed by "METHOD /path": The OpenAI-compatible routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings…) carry their request bodies this way.

In the app shell (style: app), API Reference in the Control group (/api-reference) shows the routes by feature with a search box (method, path or text). Pick a route to read it and try it against this same server: fill in the path parameters, a query string and a JSON body (prefilled from the document's example); Send request shows the status, time and the response, pretty-printed; Copy cURL gives the same request for a terminal, with $AIUI_TOKEN in place of a token; OpenAPI JSON downloads the document; ?op= opens one route (/api-reference?op=get_api_sessions). Requests go to the same origin with your session, so no proxy, CORS setup or pasted key is needed. The default dashboard style is unchanged; its Inspector and API pages stay.

The following status values are used throughout the health API: Status Meaning Color Code "ok" Service is functioning normally Green "healthy" Service is functioning normally (legacy) Green "degraded" Service is partially functional Yellow "error" Service has errors Red "unknown" Status cannot be determined Yellow Note: Both "ok" and "healthy" indicate successful operation. The system accepts either value for backward compatibility.
Returns the overall server health status. Response:

Returns detailed JSON health information from the provider gateway. Always responds with Content-Type: application/json. The base fields from the provider's health() payload are merged with the normalised fields below. Response: Field Type Description status string One of the health status values above. type string Provider type (from provider field, falls back to class name). agents integer Count of agents reported by the provider. detail string Human-readable detail; "ok" for healthy providers. api_key string Built-in PraisonAIProvider only: "set" when a model key is in the environment (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, …), a local base URL is set (OLLAMA_HOST, OPENAI_BASE_URL, …) or a key is saved in Settings; "missing" otherwise. PraisonAIUI includes built-in integration tests via aiui test. These run against a live server and verify chat, memory, sessions, and API endpoint health.

Command What it tests aiui test endpoints That the feature endpoints answer: health, features, sessions, chat, provider, channels, agents, config, skills, memory, schedules, approvals, auth, knowledge, guardrails, i18n, telemetry, security, logs, usage and more aiui test features Create, read, update and delete for guardrails, knowledge, memory, workflows, channels and eval aiui test chat Sends messages, checks the reply lands in the session history and that two sessions stay separate aiui test memory Stores a fact in one session and recalls it in another (recall is skipped, not failed, when the fact is stored but the model does not use it) aiui test sessions The session is persisted in the server's datastore (GET /sessions/{id}, any backend or AIUI_DATA_DIR) aiui test all All of the above in sequence The only option is --server / -s (default http://127.0.0.1:8082). chat and memory need an app that replies with a model. Each suite prints one line per check and a summary box, for example 34 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped for endpoints; optional checks such as GET /api/provider/agents are skipped when the provider does not offer them.

pages.d: src/praisonaiui-ts is a small TypeScript package, named praisonaiui, for

s.x: src/praisonaiui-ts is a small TypeScript package, named praisonaiui, for rendering an aiui build site inside your own React or Next.js app. It reads the JSON manifests the build writes and gives you layout and slot components. Status You do not need this package to use PraisonAIUI. aiui run and aiui build ship their own UI inside the Python wheel, and nothing in the current UI is published to npm. The praisonaiui package on npm is version 0.1.0 (January 2026); the source in the repository is 0.2.0 and is not published. The package is not built or tested in CI. To extend the UI that aiui run serves, write a plugin against @aiui/sdk instead; see UI plugins.
Without next installed, npm run build writes the JavaScript but fails at the type-declaration step. React 18 or later is a peer dependency; Next.js 14 or later is optional at runtime.

pages.d: Manifest loading and template resolution in the praisonaiui TypeScript

s.x: Manifest loading and template resolution in the praisonaiui TypeScript package. Read the overview first: the package is optional and built from src/praisonaiui-ts.
Create an instance that loads the three manifests written by aiui build. load() uses fetch, so configPath is a URL path the browser can reach. It throws if any of the three files fails to load.

Find the template for a path. Routes are tried by priority, highest first (aiui build gives the first route in the YAML the highest). In a pattern * matches one path segment and ** any number. It returns null when no route matches or the route names a template that does not exist.
A static map from a component type to a React component, for your own renderer to look up. Nothing in the package reads the registry on its own; the components in Components do not consult it.

pages.d: This document uses RFC 2119 keywords: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY.

s.x: Version: v1alpha1 (draft) Status: Draft — not yet normative Date: August 2026 This document uses RFC 2119 keywords: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY.

ADP defines a declarative format for describing application UI design: site metadata, theming, navigation, reusable components, page templates, and URL routing. It does NOT define: Server-side APIs or data models Agent orchestration or workflow graphs Infrastructure or deployment configuration Executable code or templating logic in manifests Implementations MUST treat ADP manifests as data, not code.

Term Definition Manifest A YAML or JSON document conforming to this spec Application The root kind: Application manifest describing a complete UI Component A named, reusable UI block with a type and props Template A layout definition assigning components to slots or zones Slot A named region within a layout (e.g. header, main) Zone An ordered list of widgets in a slot (WordPress-style) Route A URL pattern mapping to a template Catalog Published JSON Schema defining allowed component types Compiler Tool that validates and emits runtime JSON manifests Renderer Runtime that consumes compiled manifests and renders UI
Every ADP manifest MUST include:

schemaVersion — integer bumped on breaking envelope changes apiVersion — string group/version (e.g. adp.io/v1alpha1, adp.io/v1) metadata.version — application SemVer (independent of protocol version) Breaking changes MUST increment apiVersion (e.g. v1alpha1 → v1) Deprecated fields MUST include deprecated: true and SHOULD include x-sunset date

Manifests MAY be authored as YAML (.application.yaml) or JSON (.application.json). Semantics MUST be identical. Runtimes MUST NOT consume YAML directly; compilers MUST normalise to JSON before validation.

An Application spec MUST contain at minimum: Field Required Description site.title YES Application display name templates YES At least one template routes YES At least one route All other fields are OPTIONAL.
Theme MAY use preset shorthand or reference a DTCG token file:

ADP separates top tab bar from sidebar source: navigation.tabs — top-level tab bar with grouped pages content.docs.nav.mode: auto — sidebar generated from filesystem scan content.docs.nav.mode: manual — sidebar driven by navigation.tabs groups Renderers MUST honour content.docs.nav.mode when building sidebar (R29)
Rules: Component IDs MUST be unique within the manifest type MUST match an entry in the published component catalog props MUST validate against the catalog JSON Schema for that type

Rules: layout MUST be a known layout type in the catalog Each slot value MUST be { ref: id }, { type: ComponentType }, or null Zones MUST use zone names valid for FlexibleLayout A template MUST declare either slots or zones, not both (R13)

Rules: Routes MUST be ordered most-specific-first match MUST be a glob pattern template MUST reference a key in spec.templates Renderers MUST resolve routes at runtime using compiled route-manifest.json

Implementations MUST publish a component-catalog.schema.json (meta-schema) and a catalog instance such as catalogs/default.catalog.json: Custom component types MUST be registered via plugin schema layers. Unknown types MUST cause validation failure in strict mode.

A conforming compiler MUST: Parse YAML or JSON manifest Normalise to JSON Validate against application.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) Validate cross-reference rules (see validation-rules.md) Validate component props against catalog schema Emit runtime manifests: ui-config.json — site, components, templates, theme, navigation route-manifest.json — ordered routes with template refs docs-nav.json — filesystem-derived navigation (if mode auto)

Manifests MAY include external files using Backstage-style placeholders: Rules: Paths MUST be relative to the containing manifest Path traversal (../../) MUST be rejected Supported placeholders: $yaml:, $json:, $text:
Vendor extensions MUST use the x-adp- prefix: Implementations MUST preserve unknown x-adp-* fields. Non-prefixed unknown fields MUST be rejected in strict mode.

An implementation is ADP-conformant if and only if it: Accepts manifests with apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 and kind: Application Validates all MUST-level requirements in this spec and validation-rules.md Rejects manifests with unknown fields in strict mode Emits runtime JSON manifests from valid Application specs Resolves routes to templates at render time
Research report Implementation status PraisonAIUI mapping JSON Schema: application JSON Schema: component catalog JSON Schema: theme Examples

pages.d: Cross-reference validation rules for Application Design Protocol manifests. These constraints cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone and MUST be enforced by c

s.x: Cross-reference validation rules for Application Design Protocol manifests. These constraints cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone and MUST be enforced by conforming compilers. Rules use RFC 2119 keywords: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY. Inspired by AWP validation rules R1–R32 pattern.

Rule Level Description R1 MUST schemaVersion MUST equal 1 for apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 R2 MUST kind MUST be Application for root manifests R3 MUST metadata.name MUST be unique within a deployment scope R4 MUST NOT Unknown top-level fields outside x-adp-* namespace in strict mode

Rule Level Description R5 MUST Every spec.components entry MUST have a unique ID R6 MUST Every component type MUST exist in the published component catalog R7 MUST Component props MUST validate against catalog JSON Schema for that type R8 MUST NOT A component ID be referenced by ref: unless it exists in spec.components R9 SHOULD Unused components (defined but never referenced) SHOULD emit a warning

Rule Level Description R10 MUST Every spec.templates entry MUST declare a valid layout from the catalog R11 MUST Slot names in templates.*.slots MUST be valid for the declared layout R12 MUST Zone names in templates.*.zones MUST be valid for FlexibleLayout R13 MUST Each template MUST declare either slots or zones, not both R14 MUST Inline slot { type: X } types MUST exist in the component catalog R15 MUST Slot { ref: id } MUST resolve to a component in spec.components

Rule Level Description R16 MUST Every route template MUST reference a key in spec.templates R17 MUST Routes MUST be ordered most-specific-first (longer/more precise patterns before wildcards) R18 MUST Route slot overrides MUST use valid slot names for the target template's layout R19 SHOULD At least one route SHOULD match the site root or docs base path

Rule Level Description R20 MUST If content.docs.dir is declared, the directory MUST exist at compile time R21 MUST If content.docs.nav.mode is manual, navigation.tabs MUST be non-empty R22 SHOULD If content.docs.nav.mode is auto, a content source MUST be declared Navigation model: navigation.tabs — top tab bar content.docs.nav.mode — sidebar source: auto (filesystem scan) or manual (use navigation.tabs groups)

Rule Level Description R23 MUST NOT $yaml:, $json:, or $text: paths traverse outside the project root R24 MUST Included files MUST parse as valid YAML/JSON/text respectively R25 MUST NOT Circular file includes (A includes B includes A)

Rule Level Description R26 MUST If theme.tokens is declared, the referenced file MUST exist and validate against DTCG 2025.10 R27 MUST NOT Both theme.preset and theme.tokens be declared simultaneously

pages.d: There is no single existing standard for designing full application UI from a declarative text file. Instead, the problem is addressed in fragments:

s.x: Version: 1.0 (draft) Date: August 2026 Scope: UI, layout, navigation, theming — declarative application design from text manifests Status: Research and recommendation; not yet a published standard

There is no single existing standard for designing full application UI from a declarative text file. Instead, the problem is addressed in fragments: Docs-site generators (commercial docs platforms, PraisonAIUI, Hugo) declare navigation and layout in config files. Form libraries (JSON Forms, RJSF) declare layout trees from JSON Schema. Agent UI protocols (A2UI, AG-UI) declare streaming component surfaces for LLM-generated UI. Catalog standards (OpenUI, Backstage) declare component metadata without runtime layout. Design token standards (DTCG 2025.10) declare theming without structure. Recommendation: Define an Application Design Protocol (ADP) that synthesises proven patterns from 45 surveyed standards into a UI-only manifest format. PraisonAIUI already implements approximately 60% of this model. ADP formalises, extends, and publishes what exists today.
A protocol that lets a developer (or LLM) describe an application's visual design — pages, navigation, components, themes, routes — in one or more text files, without writing application code.

Need Who solves it Gap Docs site from config Commercial docs platforms, PraisonAIUI, Docusaurus No shared spec; some use JSON, others YAML or JS Component catalog OpenUI, A2UI No layout or routing Layout trees JSON Forms uiSchema Forms only, not app shells Theming DTCG, Material 3 Tokens only, no pages Agent-generated UI A2UI Runtime streaming, not human-authored static sites Software metadata Backstage Catalog entities, not UI composition

Human-readable — editable without IDE plugins LLM-safe — structural schema rejects unknown fields Portable — same manifest renders on any ADP-compliant runtime Validatable — fail fast at build time, not in the browser Extensible — plugins add catalog entries, not inline code Accessible — ARIA hints required in component catalog
Each entry describes how UI/layout/navigation is declared — the primary comparison dimension.

s.x: Mechanism Standards How it works ADP Envelope document K8s, Backstage, OAM, AWP apiVersion + kind + metadata + spec Adopt Component registry + ref PraisonAIUI, OpenUI Named map; templates use ref: Adopt Layout + slots PraisonAIUI, JSON Forms Layout type + named regions Adopt (unified) Route → template PraisonAIUI, Flutter URL glob → template Adopt Navigation tree Docusaurus, Storybook Hierarchical groups → pages Adopt Design token file DTCG, Material 3 Token JSON with aliases Adopt Catalog allowlist A2UI, OpenUI Closed component vocabulary Adopt Schema + uiSchema split JSON Forms, RJSF Data vs presentation Partial Streaming surfaces A2UI, AG-UI Incremental JSON updates Future Layered spec AWP, Helm Separate files merged at compile Adopt File includes Backstage, OpenAPI $yaml: / $ref external files Adopt Structural pruning K8s CRD Reject unknown fields Adopt Validation rules R1–Rn AWP Cross-ref beyond JSON Schema Adopt JS executable config Docusaurus, Gatsby Code config Reject Visual canvas Figma, Webflow Proprietary designer Reject Code-only UI Compose, SwiftUI No wire format Out of scope

Dimension PraisonAIUI A2UI Backstage Authoring format YAML JSON (stream) YAML Envelope schemaVersion only Message version apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec Navigation navigation.tabs[] + filesystem N/A N/A (metadata catalog) Components components{id: type, props} Catalog + adjacency list Entity kinds Layout templates{layout, slots, zones} Surfaces N/A Routes routes{match, template} N/A N/A Schema published Pydantic only JSON Schema catalog JSON Schema per kind Runtime React SPA Any renderer Catalog API Primary use Docs sites Agent-generated UI Software inventory Synthesis: ADP combines PraisonAIUI's composition model, the published $schema of commercial docs platforms, A2UI's catalog allowlist, and Backstage's envelope and file includes.
YAML is the best authoring format for application design manifests.

Commercial docs platforms — the closest docs-site analogues — use JSON config with a published $schema URL for IDE autocomplete. This works well for flat-to-moderately-nested config but becomes verbose for deep layout trees. A2UI uses JSON as both authoring and wire format because LLMs emit structured JSON reliably and ambiguity is unacceptable at runtime. Docusaurus and Gatsby use JavaScript/TypeScript config for programmatic power — but this sacrifices portability and LLM generation safety.

Format Strengths Weaknesses for ADP YAML Comments; readable nesting; LLM-friendly; PraisonAIUI continuity Ambiguous typing; merge key footguns; no native DRY JSON Unambiguous; $schema IDE support; proven by commercial docs platforms No comments; verbose for layout trees TOML Clear flat tables (Hugo) Poor for nested templates/zones CUE / Jsonnet / Pkl Typed composition without templating Learning curve; not LLM-default HCL Modules, expressions Ecosystem-bound; overkill for UI-only JS/TS Full programmatic power Not portable; not LLM-safe

Primary authoring: YAML — best for nested templates / zones trees Alternate authoring: JSON — for teams preferring $schema editor tooling Never at runtime: YAML — always compile to JSON before serve Composition: $yaml: file includes (Backstage), not Helm Go templates Power users: Optional CUE/Jsonnet compiles to YAML before validation Verdict: YAML remains the recommended default, but ADP MUST accept JSON as an equivalent authoring format with identical semantics.

Declarative, not executable — manifests describe intent; runtimes render; no inline code or templating logic in core spec. Schema-first — JSON Schema 2020-12 is canonical; YAML is authoring convenience. Structural strictness — unknown fields rejected in strict mode (K8s CRD pattern). Catalog allowlist — component type must exist in published catalog (A2UI pattern). Envelope consistency — every document uses apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec. Separation of concerns — theme, navigation, components, templates, routes are distinct spec sections. Compile, don't interpret — YAML → validated JSON manifest → static assets at build time. Accessibility by default — catalog entries include ARIA role hints (WAI-ARIA pattern). Versioned protocol — schemaVersion integer + apiVersion string; breaking changes bump version. Extension namespace — x-adp-* prefix reserved; plugins register catalog layers. File composition — $yaml: includes for modular configs (Backstage pattern). Route-driven rendering — URL resolution selects template; no hardcoded layout in renderer.

PraisonAIUI today ADP equivalent schemaVersion: 1 schemaVersion + apiVersion components + ref: spec.components + slot refs templates.layout + slots spec.templates routes spec.routes site.theme spec.theme Compiler → JSON manifests ADP compile pipeline Pydantic validation JSON Schema + cross-ref rules

Gap ADP fix No published JSON Schema Publish application.schema.json navigation.tabs compiled but not rendered Mandate runtime consumption in spec route-manifest.json not used for routing Mandate route-driven template resolution Dual slots + zones models Unified: zones = ordered slot arrays Closed hardcoded component types Published component-catalog.schema.json No envelope (kind, metadata) Add Backstage-style envelope

Existing aiui.yaml (and aiui.template.yaml) files remain valid. Migration steps: Add apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 and kind: Application (optional during transition). Wrap top-level keys under spec: (compiler accepts both shapes during v1alpha1). Rename site fields unchanged; map navigation, templates, routes as-is. Publish catalog; register custom component types via plugin schema layers. See adp/aiui-mapping.md for field-by-field mapping.

Should ADP standardise layout type names (ThreeColumnLayout) or allow runtime-defined layouts? Should navigation support both filesystem-auto and manual tabs in one spec, or require a mode switch? Should agent-driven surfaces (A2UI) be a separate kind: Surface or embedded in Application? Should theme reference DTCG token files directly or use simplified preset shorthand?

The research across 45 standards yields a clear synthesis: Envelope from Backstage/K8s Composition from PraisonAIUI (components → templates → routes) Catalog from A2UI/OpenUI Theming from DTCG Validation from AWP (structural schema + R-rules) Authoring in YAML (default) with JSON alternate (published $schema pattern) Status: Research draft — see adp/implementation-status.md for implementation gaps. pages.d: PraisonAIUI is a Python package (PyPI aiui, import praisonaiui) with a

s.x: PraisonAIUI is a Python package (PyPI aiui, import praisonaiui) with a Starlette + Uvicorn server and two frontends: Part What it is CLI (aiui) aiui run app.py starts the server; aiui build compiles a YAML docs site into static JSON manifests Server (server.py, features/) HTTP routes, the chat WebSocket, and one feature module per domain (sessions, agents, theme, attachments, ...) Providers @aiui.reply callbacks or the PraisonAI provider turn a message into RunEvents (see Providers) React app shell (style: app) The default of create_app(), aiui run, and apps with @aiui.page (see React app shell), alongside the chat, agents, playground and docs styles Legacy dashboard style The opt-in vanilla-JS dashboard (--style dashboard or style: dashboard; templates/frontend/plugins/), kept working for backwards compatibility Plugins First-party pages and features are catalog records; third-party packages use the praisonaiui.plugins entry point (see Plugins) The data flow of a docs site is YAML config → Pydantic models → compiler → JSON manifests → React. The layer map, the numbered rules, and the architecture decision records live in the repository at ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/adr/.
With the praisonai backend, PraisonAIUI has two complementary integration layers. They solve different problems and run side-by-side.

AG-UI sits alongside MCP and A2A in the agentic protocol stack: Protocol Purpose MCP Gives agents tools A2A Agent-to-agent communication AG-UI Agent-to-user-interface (streaming) Gateway Infrastructure management (channels, nodes, instances)

AG-UI is an open, event-based protocol by CopilotKit that standardizes how agent backends stream events to frontends. PraisonAI implements it at praisonaiagents/ui/agui/. What it does: Streams ~16 standard event types (text deltas, tool calls, state sync, generative UI) over SSE. Who uses it: LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, AWS Strands, Mastra, Pydantic AI, LlamaIndex, AG2, and PraisonAI. #### Usage Frontend compatibility: CopilotKit, or any AG-UI-compatible client.

The gateway integration connects PraisonAIUI's dashboard features to the live WebSocketGateway backend for infrastructure management. What it does: CRUD for channels, nodes, instances; live bot status; heartbeat monitoring. #### How It Works #### Key Files File Purpose features/_gateway_ref.py Thread-safe singleton holding reference to the live gateway features/channels.py Channel CRUD + live status enrichment from gateway features/nodes.py Node CRUD + gateway health enrichment integration.py Calls set_gateway() on start, clears on stop config_store.py Unified ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml — single source of truth for all feature state #### API Endpoints Endpoint Methods Description /api/channels GET, POST List/create channels /api/channels/{id} GET, PUT, DELETE Channel CRUD /api/channels/{id}/toggle POST Enable/disable /api/channels/{id}/status GET Live running status /api/channels/{id}/restart POST Restart a channel bot /api/channels/{id}/test POST Test connectivity of a channel bot /api/channels/platforms GET Supported platforms /api/nodes GET, POST List/register nodes /api/nodes/{id} GET, PUT, DELETE Node CRUD /api/nodes/{id}/status GET Node status + gateway enrichment /api/nodes/{id}/agents GET, PUT Agent bindings /api/instances GET Connected instances /api/instances/heartbeat POST Presence heartbeat

AIUIGateway.start() in integration.py mounts the gateway and dashboard REST API on one server. Chat uses the built-in WebSocket/SSE RunEvent protocol; AG-UI is mounted separately via AguiFeature when enabled:

AG-UI (/agui) Gateway (/api/*) Layer Conversation Operations Transport SSE (server-sent events) REST + WebSocket Purpose Stream agent responses to users Manage channels, nodes, instances Frontend CopilotKit / AG-UI clients PraisonAIUI React dashboard Protocol Open standard (~16 event types) Internal REST API

pages.d: aiui run app.py is the one entry point for an app. It imports app.py (under

s.x: aiui run app.py is the one entry point for an app. It imports app.py (under the module name user_app, so an if __name__ == "__main__": block does not run), reads what the module registered, and starts its own server on --host and --port.
Run: aiui run app.py (opens the app shell, the aiui run default; use aiui run app.py --style chat for the classic chat UI)

Run: aiui run app.py (opens the default app shell; pass --style dashboard for the legacy vanilla-JS dashboard — see UI Styles). A module that builds its own app with create_app() and starts Uvicorn under if __name__ == "__main__": is not special-cased: aiui run ignores that app and serves its own. Run such a file with python app.py instead.

Run: aiui run app.py. An async main() together with an import of AIUIGateway from praisonaiui.integration switches to the praisonai backend. When the module defines main(), the CLI sets the PORT and HOST environment variables from --port/--host (unless they are already set) and calls your main(), so main() must read them to honour the CLI options, as above. Without a main(), the CLI builds its own AIUIGateway on --host/--port and registers the module's agent (or each item of agents). The backend needs the praisonai package (pip install "aiui[praisonai]").

app.py contains Backend Style async main() and from praisonaiui.integration import AIUIGateway praisonai as below anything else standalone detected from the callbacks Detection runs whenever --backend is standalone, which is also the default, so passing --backend standalone does not turn it off. The style rules are in UI Styles.
--reload restarts the server when a file in the folder of app.py changes.

pages.d: How the PraisonAIUI test suites are laid out and how to run them. To test a

s.x: How the PraisonAIUI test suites are laid out and how to run them. To test a running server from the outside, see API Testing.

CI runs ruff check src/praisonaiui, then pytest tests/unit tests/integration -v --no-cov --timeout=120. Tests marked live call a real LLM provider and skip unless PRAISONAI_LIVE_TESTS=1; tests/integration/conftest.py clears provider API keys for the others. The Python suites that need Node 22.15+, src/frontend/node_modules or Chromium run in e2e shard 1 with RUN_BROWSER_TESTS=1 and --fail-on-skip, which fails the run if any test skips (see tests/README.md). Folder What is in it tests/unit/ Isolated tests: schema, compiler, docs scanner, serve, server and app-shell manifest, plugins, CLI, each feature. They use tmp_path and Starlette's TestClient, and start no server tests/unit/fixtures/ Golden files, such as the default dashboard HTML and the built-in page snapshot tests/integration/ End-to-end tests: the validate → build → serve pipeline through Typer's CliRunner, endpoints, agentic round trips, attachments. Some need praisonaiagents or an API key and skip without them tests/ (top level) Feature-level tests for each domain API The suites grow with every change, so count them instead of trusting a number written here:
From src/frontend (Node version in .nvmrc):

Playwright suites in src/frontend/e2e/ start real servers (with a scripted provider instead of a model) and drive Chromium against the default dashboard, the app shell, the chat style, the docs site and the layouts. They serve dist/, so build first: The projects, servers and baselines are described in src/frontend/e2e/README.md.
